**The form called Sadasiva is completely free from any trace of the mode of ignorance. He is the cause of the entire material creation and is a personal expansion from the body of the original Personality of Godhead. The Vayu Purana and other scriptures state that he resides on Sivaloka.**

**Комментарий:**

Thus far Srila Rupa Gosvami has drawn the following conclusions: Sri Krsna is the original Personality of Godhead, Narayana and other forms of Godhead are His vilasa and svamsa expansions, and there are also jivas who become avesa incarnations. From the svamsa expansion lying on the Garbha Ocean come Visnu, Brahma, and Rudra, who are originally His own expansions, but the latter two roles are sometimes also played by jivas.

There are other opinions. For example, it might be said that Lord Sadasiva is the original truth, that He alone deserves to be called svayam- rupa,that Narayana and the others are His expansions, and that the three guna-avataras are created by Him. This is supported by the Kaivalya Upanisad (6-9):

*acintyam avyaktam ananta-rupam*  
*sivam prasantam amrtam brahma-yonim*  
*tam adi-madhyanta-vihinam ekam*  
*vibhum cid-anandam arupam adbhutam*

**“Inconceivable, unmanifest, peaceful, immortal, and all-auspicious, He is the expander of unlimited forms, the Absolute Truth, from which everything originates. Having no beginning, middle, or end, He pervades all existence. He is pure, blissful consciousness, formless and amazing.**

*uma-sahayam paramesvaram prabhum*  
*tri-locanam nila-kantham prasantam*  
*dhyatva munir gacchati bhuta-yonim*  
*samasta-saksim tamasah parastat*

**“By meditating on the peaceful, three-eyed, blue-throated Supreme Lord accompanied by His consort Uma, a sage attains Him, who is beyond the realm of ignorance and is the master of creation, the source of all created beings, and the witness of everything.**

*sa brahma sa sivah sendrah*  
*so ksarah paramah svarat*  
*sa eva visnuh sa pranah*  
*sa kalagnih sa candramah*

**“He is Brahma, Siva, and Indra. He is the infallible, absolutely independent Supreme, Lord Visnu. He is the air of life, the fire of annihilation, and the moon.**

*sa eva sarvam yad bhutam*  
*yac ca bhavyam caracaram*  
*jhatva tam mrtyum atyeti*  
*nanyah pantha vimuktaye*

**“He is everything that has been and everything that is, both moving and nonmoving. Knowing him, one overcomes death. 'There is no other path to liberation”**

Although these reliable and authoritative statements of sruti seem to equate Lord Siva with Lord Narayana, we need to understand these statements correctly. Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana explains that these verses describe only Lord Narayana, the vilasa expansion of Krsna, the original Godhead. Siva is also a name of Narayana, and thus the two names are used interchangeably in the Maha-narayana Upanisad 13.3: sivam acyutam narayanam. Similarly, Uma is another name of Kirti, one of Lord Narayanas principal saktis. Then, since this passage describes the Lord of Vaikuntha and not the guna-avatara of the material world, nila-kantha indicates “one whose neck is adorned with a blue gem.” And finally, Sivaloka should be understood as the Supreme Lords abode, Vaikuntha.

Srila Jiva Gosvami, in his Bhagavat-sandarbha (72), has cited the verses of the Vayu Purana (49.153-61) mentioned in this verse, beginning with the words andaughasya samantat tu (“surrounding the mass of all the universal eggs”), which glorify Lord Sivas abode.

**The Brahma-samhita s5.8\] explains the original form of Lord Siva: “Rama-devi, the spiritual potency, beloved consort of the Supreme Lord, is the regulatrix of all entities. The divine plenary portion of Krsna creates the mundane world. At creation there appears a divine halo of the nature of His own subjective portion. This halo is divine Sambhu, the masculine symbol or manifested emblem of the Supreme Lord, this halo is the dim twilight reflection of the supreme eternal effulgence. This masculine symbol is the subjective portion of divinity who functions as progenitor of the mundane world, subject to the supreme regulatrix. The conceiving potency in regard to mundane creation makes her appearance out of the supreme regulatrix. She is Maya, the limited, nonabsolute potency, the symbol of mundane feminine productivity.”**

**Комментарий:**

This is Sri Brahma-samhita’s discussion of Lord Krsnas expansion as Lord Sadasiva. The discussion continues with these words:

*kamo bijam mahad dhareh*

**“The intercourse of these two brings forth the faculty of perverted cognition, the reflection of the seed of the procreative desire of the Supreme Lord.**

*linga-yony-atmika jata*  
*ima mahesvari prajah*

**“All offspring of the consort of the great lord sMahesvara\] of this mundane world are of the nature of the embodiment of the mundane masculine and feminine generative organs.**

*saktiman purusah so yam*  
*linga-rupi mahesvarah*  
*tasminn avirabhul tinge*  
*maha-visnuh jagat-patih*

**“The person embodying the material causal principle, viz. the great lord of this mundane world sMahesvara\] Sambhu, in the form of the male generating organ, is joined to his female consort, the limited energy sMaya\], as the efficient causal principle. The Lord of the world Maha-visnu is manifest in him by His subjective portion in the form of His glance.” (Brahma- samhita 8-10)**

Verse seven of the Brahma-samhita states that the Supreme Lord always enjoys with His pleasure potency, Rama. Rama is tad-vasa,subordinate to the Supreme Lord in their mutual enjoyment and never separated from Him. Indeed, she can never be separated from Him because she is of His very essence. The Hayasirsa Pancaratra says, na visnuna vina devi / na visnuh padmajam vina. “The goddess is never alone without Visnu, and Visnu is never without the lotus-born goddess.” And the Visnu Purana (1.8.15) describes her as nityaiva sa jagan-mata / visnoh srir anapdyini. “Lord Visnu s consort, Sri, is the eternal mother of the universe and is always by His side.”

Sambhu (Sadasiva) is a reflection and representative of the svayam-rupa Lord. According to the Visva-kosa dictionary, lingam cihne numane ca. “Linga can mean sign or ‘inference.” Lord Sadasiva is also Bhagavan, the Lord of the spiritual sky, full in six opulences, an expanded form of mundane success. His body is jyoti-rupa, pure spirit. The revelation that Sadasiva, the lord of the material creation, expands from Krsna is supporting evidence that Krsna is the original form of the Supreme, just as the detection of a dewlap on an animal is evidence that the animal is a cow.

The consort energy of Lord Sambhu in the material world is the inferior sakti who comprises the three modes. When the Supreme Lords expansion, Sankarsana Maha-visnu, desires to glance at this inferior saktiy the mahal-tattva begins to evolve. Thus Lord Visnus desire is the seed of material existence (mahad bijam). The word mahat refers to the countless finite living beings impregnated in the womb of material nature by Lord Visnus glance. They become mahesvari-prajah, the offspring of the Lords feminine prakrti, the all-powerful ruler of creation. And they are linga-yony-atmikahy born from the combination of the supreme enjoyer and His prakrti. These conditioned jivas are also known as children of prakrti because they are fully dependent on her.

Sri Brhad-bhagavatamrta glorifies Lord Rudra in the second and third chapters of the first part (2.80-98 and 3.1-42) and in the third chapter of the second part (3.48-66), and Sri Caitanya-caritamrta describes Rudra in his role as guna-avatara (Madhya 20.307-12).

Srimad-Bhagavatam also presents Lord Rudra prominently in several cantos. The Third Canto describes his birth from the forehead of Brahma (3.12.6-20). The Fourth Canto explains the terrible reactions Prajapati Daksa suffered for offending him (chapters 2-6). The Fifth Canto describes Sri Rudra residing on Ilavrta-varsa and worshiping Lord Sankarsana, from whom he expands (5.17.15-24). And the Eighth Canto tells the history of Lord Rudra drinking the poison churned from the Milk Ocean (8.7.18- 46) and describes his encounter with Lord Visnus Mohini incarnation (chapter 12).

Ksirodaka-sayi Visnu is the Lord of the Milk Ocean and Supersoul of the living entities. Although He is not the Lord of Vaikuntha, He is called Narayana because He is a vilasa form of Garbhodaka-sayi Visnu, who is a vilasa of Maha-visnu. Lord Maha-visnu can be called Narayana because He rests on the Karanarnava, the water of creation. His nondifferent expansion resting on the Milk Ocean is thus also Narayana.

Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhus explanation of the guna-avatara Visnu is recorded in Sri Caitanya-caritamrta (Madhya 20.313-18).

### Text 47

*visnuh sattvam tanotiti*  
*sastre sattva-tanuh smrtah*  
*avatara-ganas casya*  
*bhavet sattva-tanus tatha*  
*bahir-angam adhisthanam*  
*iti va tasya tat tanuh*

**Пословный перевод:**

visnuh — Visnu; sattvam — the mode of goodness; tanoti — spreads; iti — thus; sastre — in the scripture; sattva-tanuh — having sattva as His body; smrtah — is known; avatara-ganah — the many incarnations; ca — and; asya — His; bhavet — are; sattva-tanuh — embodiments of goodness; tatha — also; bahih-angam — external; adhisthanam — His residence; iti — thus; va — or; tasya — His; tat — that; tanuh — body.

**Перевод:**

**The scriptures describe Lord Visnu and His many incarnations as sattva-tanu. This word can indicate that Visnu propagates (tanoti) the mode of goodness (sattva) or that the mode of goodness is His body (tanu) because it is His external place of residence.**

**Комментарий:**

Sri Suta Gosvami uses the word *sattva-tanu* in his statement *sreyamsi tatra khalu sattva-tanor nrnam syuh:* “Of these three sBrahma, Visnu, and Siva\], all human beings can derive ultimate benefit from Visnu, who propagates the quality of goodness.” *(Bhagavatam* 1.2.23)

It might be asked whether this word *sattva-tanu,* which can be translated “embodiment of material goodness,” is a material form assumed by Lord Visnu. If so, then worshiping that form of His would not likely result in liberation. According to the *Vedanta-sutras* (4.1.3) one can gain liberation only by worshiping the Supreme in His original form as the Soul of all existence: *atmeti tupa-gacchanti grahayanti ca* (“Only as the Supreme Soul can He be properly understood and explained to others”).

This doubt is resolved by the explanation that sattva-tanu has meanings other than “the embodiment of material goodness,” meanings consistent with Lord Visnu\`s granting liberation. The verb tan means “to propagate,” and so tanu can mean “propagation” as well as “body.” Lord Ksirodaka-sayi Visnu and the incarnations who appear from Him propagate the mode of goodness.

Or, alternatively, sattva-guna is Lord Visnu’s external place of residence, as opposed to Vaikuntha, His real home. Suta Gosvami also says sattvam yad brahma-darsanam: “It is the quality of goodness that enables one to see the Absolute Truth” (Bhagavatam 1.2.24). This means that the Supreme Lord can be realized through the knowledge that arises in clear and peaceful consciousness influenced by sattva-guna.

*sarva-sastre prasidhyati*

### Text 49

*tatha hi sri-dasame,*  
*harir hi nirgunah saksat*  
*purusah prakrteh parah*  
*sa sarva-drg upadrasta*  
*tam bhajan nirguno bhavet*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha — thus; hi — indeed; sri-dasame — in the Tenth Canto; harih— the Supreme Lord Hari; hi — indeed; nirgunah — untouched by the material modes; saksat — absolutely; purusah — the Personality of Godhead; prakrteh — to material nature; parah — transcendental; sah — He; sarva — everything; drk — seeing; upadrasta — the witness; tam — Him; bhajan — by worshiping; nirgunah —free from the material modes; bhavet — one becomes; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**As, for example, in the Tenth Canto (10.88.5): “Lord Hari, however, has no connection with the material modes. He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the all-seeing eternal witness, transcendental to material nature. One who worships Him becomes similarly free from the material modes.”**

**Комментарий:**

Lord Visnu controls the mode of goodness by His sweet will, without

becoming entangled by it. He personally (saksat) remains always in His original independent position, not coverable by any power of the material energy. To some extent the three modes cover Brahma and the other demigods, but the modes can never touch Visnu because material desire can never compel Him to consort with them. He sees everything (sarva-drk), and He bestows the transcendental vision (drs or darsana) that leads all fit candidates to liberation. He is the ever-present witness for these souls on the path to liberation, and He is their goal, not just another object to leave aside. Therefore by worshiping Him a human being becomes also transcendental to the material modes. Niranjanah paramam samyam upaiti: “Freed from the taint of material association, one attains transcendental equality with the Supreme.” (Mundaka Upanisad 3.1.3)

*tad-bhakter eva nityata*

### Text 52

*tatha hi padme,*  
*smartavyah satatam visnur*  
*vismartavyo na jatucit*  
*sarve vidhi-nisedhah syur*  
*etayor eva kinkarah*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha hi — for example; padme — in the Padma Purana; smartavyah — should be remembered; satatam — always; visnuh — Visnu; vismartavyah — should be forgotten; na — not; jatucit — ever; sarve — all; vidhi — rules; nisedhah — and prohibitions; syuh — are; etayoh — of these two; eva — only; kinkarah — servants.

**Перевод:**

**As stated in the Padma Purana (Uttara-khanda 71.100), “Lord Visnu should always be remembered and never forgotten. All other injunctions and prohibitions are servants of these two.”**

**Комментарий:**

In common language nitya means “regular” or “constant,” but in the specific contexts of sacrifice and service it means “obligatory”. When failure to perform some particular activity will lead to loss, that activity is called nitya. Since Lord Visnu is the Supreme Person, failure to perform devotional service to Him leads to losing the real value of human life. Therefore devotional service to Lord Visnu must be considered nitya. Moreover, there is no more serious obligation than this devotional service. By fulfilling ritual obligations like chanting the Gayatri mantra at the junctures of the day, a person can achieve the Pitrloka, but by performing devotional service to Visnu one can achieve Visnu\`s abode.

### Text 53

*vyamohaya caracarasya jagatas te te puranagamas*  
*tam tam eva hi devatam paramikam jalpantu kalpavidhi*  
*siddhante punar eka eva bhagavan visnuh samastagama-*  
*vyaparesu vivecana-vyatikaram nitesu nisciyate*

**Пословный перевод:**

vyamohaya — for creating illusion; cara — moving entities; acarasya — and nonmoving entities; jagatah — for all creatures; te te — all of them; purana- agamah — the Puranas and other Vedic literatures; tam tam — various; eva hi — indeed; devatam — demigods; paramikam — as chief; jalpantu — let them speak; kalpa-avadhi — for the duration of Brahmas day; siddhante — in the final conclusion; punah — rather; ekah — one; eva — only; bhagavan visnuh — the Supreme Personality of Godhead Visnu; samasta — of all; dgama — the Vedic literatures; vyaparesu — the discussions; vivecana — of discrimination; vyatikaram — to the end; nitesu — when brought; nisciyate — is ascertained.

**Перевод:**

**Thus the same Padma Purana (Patala-khanda 93.26) states: “Each of the many Puranas and other Vedic scriptures speaks of particular demigods as supreme just to bewilder the moving and nonmoving living entities. Let these scriptures dispute like this perpetually. But when one studies and analyzes all of them collectively, one concludes that Lord Visnu is the one and only Supreme Personality of Godhead.”**

**Комментарий:**

How can one say that Visnu alone is supreme when there are so many conflicting scriptural statements? Vyasadeva himself has presented various

Puranas that speak of Brahma, Rudra, or others as the supreme being. While it is true that the Puranas and other scriptures seem to make contending claims of supremacy, these claims should be properly understood. According to the Padma Purana, persons other than Visnu are put forward as the one Lord of creation to bewilder the faithless among the souls living in the bodies of demigods, humans, and animals, as well as in mountains and other immobile bodies.

The true philosophical siddhanta is established in the Vedanta-sutras, in its commentaries by reputable Vaisnava acaryas, and in Srimad-Bhagavatam, the natural commentary on Vedanta compiled by the sutras\` author. When we carefully interpret the statements of all the revealed scriptures with the guidance of this faultless siddhanta, employing both literal and metaphorical readings, we will conclude that Visnu alone is the Supreme Truth, the unlimited reservoir of knowledge and bliss.

**Комментарий:**

To support his contention that since Visnu is supreme He alone should be worshiped, Suta Gosvami cites this verse from Srimad-Bhagavatam concerning the behavior of spiritually advanced persons. Brahma, Rudra, and other demigods are certainly the lords of the mass of created beings (bhuta-patin), but their personal appearance is ghastly in comparison with the perfectly peaceful forms of the Supreme Godhead. Still, because the pure devotees of these various selfsame expansions of the Supreme Godhead are free from envy, they never disrespect Brahma, Rudra, or other demigods:

Certainly, then, when Brahma and Siva are not selfsame avataras of Lord Visnu, they worship Him with fixed devotion. Lord Visnu alone possesses all six opulences of Godhead in full. Others, however, such as Ravana, Bana, Paundraka, Vrka, Baka, and Trnavarta, were dear to neither the demigods nor Lord Hari, and so they were enemies of the whole world.”**

### Text 59

*atra prakrti-sabdena*  
*cic-chaktir abhidhiyate*  
*abhinna-bhinna-rupatvad*  
*asyaivokta samasama*  
*iti purusavatara-gunavatara-nirupanam.*

**Пословный перевод:**

atra — here; prakrti-sabdena — by the word prakrti; cit-saktih — the spiritual energy; abhidhiyate — is indicated; abhinna — nondifferent; bhinna — and different; rupatvat — because of being; asya — to Him; eva — indeed; ukta — is said to be; sama — equal; asama — and unequal; iti — thus; purusa- avatara — of the purusa-avataras; guna-avatara — and of the guna-avataras; nirupanam — the description.

**Перевод:**

**In this verse the word prakrti indicates the Lord’s spiritual energy. Because she is simultaneously different and nondifferent from Him, she is said to be both on the same level and not on the same level.**

**This ends the description of the purusa-avataras and guna-avataras.**

**Комментарий:**

The word prakrti in text 58 refers to the Supreme Lords superior, spiritual energy, which is nondifferent from Him. She is described in the Upanisads and Puranas:

*parasya saktir vividhaiva sruyate*  
*svabhaviki jnana-bala-kriya ca*

**“The scriptures say that this Supreme has many kinds of energies who, though autonomous agents, are nondifferent from Him and partake of His own innate nature. They manifest His knowledge, power, and activity.” (Svetasvatara Upanisad 6.8)**

*visnu-saktih para prokta*  
*ksetrajnakhya tatha para*  
*avidya-karma-samjnanya*  
*trtiya saktir isyate*

**“Lord Visnu\`s personal energy is known as superior. Another energy of His, called the ‘knower of the field,' is also superior. His third energy is called activity in ignorance.'” (Visnu Purana 6.7.61)**

Because this spiritual energy is both nondifferent and different from Lord Visnu, the Maha-varaha Purana calls her samasama. She is nondifferent from Him in the way that heat is nondifferent from fire. The verse cited here from Svetasvatara Upanisad expresses this nondifference with the word svabhaviki, “innate.” The Amara-kosa dictionary considers svarupa (“essential identity”), svabhava (“innate character”), and nisarga (“nature”) as synonyms.

Although the Supreme Lord\`s personal energy is nondifferent from Him, there is also a distinction. This subtle distinction is called visesa. The principle of visesa allows us to say “Existence exists,” “The difference is different,” and “Time is always.” Although the distinction between the subject and predicate of these three statements is subtle, intelligent speakers still find sensible meaning in them.

But don\`t these statements just depict the svabhava, or innate character, of these phenomena — existence, difference, and time? Yes. And that svabhava can be called visesa. In other words, visesa applies in situations where phenomena and their characteristics are inseparable. Without this faculty of visesa, the Supreme Truth can never be known in terms of the qualified (visesya) and His qualification (visesana).

Moreover, statements that express visesa, such as “Existence exists,” cannot be proven fallacious using the argument that they can be negated in certain circumstances; whereas statements such as “Here is a pot” can be proven fallacious because there are circumstances in which “here” refers to a location where there is no pot.

Nor does this principle of visesa apply in a series of ever-receding causes and effects — each cause needing a preceding one to support it, ad infinitum. In this case, the possessor of qualities is the first cause, who has no cause. His faculty of visesa allows Him to express qualities that are nondifferent from Himself without help from any other support.

The conclusion that Lord Visnu possesses personal potencies simultaneously different and nondifferent from Himself is supported by the same evidence that establishes His supreme identity. The evidence that shows that He is the creator of the universe implies that He has complete free will, knowledge, and the ability to act. One without a second, He becomes many through His faculty of visesa, by which He manifests variety even though there is nothing different from Him.

In his book Siddhanta-ratna Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana has given a complete explanation of visesa. Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu uses acintya-bhedabheda, “inconceivably different and nondifferent,” to express the same visesa principle.

**Перевод:**

**Sri Narada (2) is also described in the First Canto (1.3.8): “In the millennium of the rsis, the Personality of Godhead accepted the third empowered incarnation in the form of Devarsi Narada, who is a great sage among the demigods. He spoke expositions of the Vedas which deal with devotional service and which inspire nonfruitive action.”**

**Комментарий:**

In the phase of universal creation following that of the four Sanas, sages appeared, Narada among them. Narada compiled a textbook of practice for devotees of Visnu (a satvata-tantra), which is known as the Narada Pancaratra. According to Narada\`s method of devotional service, one should adjust ones activities so that they become fit for offering to the Supreme Lord. Those activities will then help one become free from the bondage of material work. This method is like the use of mercury, a dangerous poison, to remove other toxins from one\`s body.

### Text 6

*pravartanaya loke \`smin*  
*sva-bhakter eva sarvatah*  
*harir devarsi-rupena*  
*candra-subhro vidher abhut*

**Пословный перевод:**

pravartanaya — for the distribution; loke — in the world; asmin — this; sva-bhakteh — of His own devotional service; eva — indeed; sarvatah — everywhere; harih— Lord Hari; devarsi-rupena — as the sage among the demigods; candra — like the moon; subhrah — radiant white; vidheh — from Brahma; abhut — appeared.

**Перевод:**

**Manifesting a radiant moonlike complexion, Lord Hari appeared from Brahma as the sage among the demigods to distribute everywhere His own devotional service.**

**Комментарий:**

The first half of Srila Sanatana Gosvami\`s Brhad-bhagavatamrta describes

Narada Muni\`s travels throughout the universe in search of Krsna\`s dearest devotees. The second half of the same work depicts Narada appearing several times in order to give important guidance to Gopa-kumara, who is searching for the Lord of his heart. Especially significant are Narada\`s instructions to Gopa-kumara in part two, chapter four (from text 123) and chapter five (from text 49).

Narada appears frequently in Srimad-Bhagavatam, most often in the roles of instructing spiritual master and divine messenger. He advised Dvaipayana Veda-vyasa to compile the Bhagavatam (1.5-6). He consoled Yudhisthira when Dhrtarastra left home (1.13.38-60) and warned him when Krsna was about to finish His pastimes (1.14.8). He was also present when Sukadeva spoke the Bhagavatam to Pariksit (1.19.10).

He inquired from his father Brahma about the supreme creator (2.5.1-8). He revealed to Hiranyaksa where to find Hiranyaksa\`s enemy, Visnu (3.18.1). He told Devahuti about Kardama Munis good qualities (3.22.9) and informed Lord Siva about his wife Sati\`s suicide (4.5.1). He preached to Dhruva (4.8.25-61) and to Dhruva\`s father Uttanapada (4.8.63-69), and he praised Dhruva in the assembly of the Pracetas (4.12.41-43). He enlightened King Pracinabarhi with the story of Puranjana (4.25-29), instructed the Pracetas on how to attain the Supreme (4.32.3-22), and became the spiritual master of Priyavrata (5.1.6). He taught the principles of the Narada Pancaratra to Savarni Muni (5.19.10) and always sings Lord Ananta\`s glories in Brahmas assembly (5.25.8).

After inspiring the thousands of Haryasvas and Savalasvas to renounce material life, he received a curse in return from their father Daksa (6.5). He related the history of King Citraketu to Sukadeva (beginning from 6.14.9). He and Angira Muni preached to Citraketu when the king was lamenting his own son\`s death (6.15.1-8). He initiated Citraketu into the worship of Lord Ananta (6.15.27-28, 6.17-25) and brought Citraketu\`s son back to life (6.16.1-3).

At Maharaja Yudhisthiras Rajasuya sacrifice, Narada explained to him why Krsna awarded liberation to His enemies, Sisupala and Dantavakra (7.1.13-34). In explaining how the Vaikuntha gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya were cursed to become demons, he narrated Prahlada\`s life story to Yudhisthira (7.1-10). Narada prevented Indra from arresting Hiranyakasipu\`s pregnant wife, kept her safely at his asrama, and imparted transcendental knowledge to Prahlada in her womb (7.7.7-16).

During the battle between Bali and Indra, after Indra had killed Jambhasura, Narada informed Jambhasura\`s friends and relatives of his death (8.11.19). Then, on behalf of Lord Brahma he asked the demigods to stop the battle before they entirely destroyed the dynasty of the demons (8.11.43-44).

He also advised Hariscandra to take Lord Varuna\`s help in obtaining a son (9.7.8).

Just before Krsna\`s birth, Narada warned Kamsa that the demoniac persons who were a great burden on the earth would be killed (10.1.64). Narada cursed Kuvera\`s sons after they had publicly bathed naked in the company of young girls (10.10.5-22). He also led the Gandharvas, Vidyadharas, Siddhas, and Caranas in singing the praises of Giridhari at His coronation as Govinda, Lord of the cows (10.27.24).

Narada divulged to Kamsa the secret that Krsna, Balarama, and Subhadra were really Vasudevas children (10.36.17). He recounted to Krsna the pastimes Krsna would perform in Mathura and Dvaraka (10.37.9-23). And he gave information to Kalayavana that impelled him to attack Krsna at Mathura (10.50.43).

He told Mayavati, who was living as a maidservant of Sambara, that the infant given to her, which had been found in the belly of a fish, was actually her husband Cupid (10.55.7). To Krsna and His parents and queens, Narada explained this amazing rebirth of Cupid as Pradyumna (10.55.36).

He gave news to the Vrsnis of Aniruddha\`s capture by Bana (10.63.2), told the Yadus about Sambas capture by the Kurus (10.68.13), and visited Krsna in His many palaces in Dvaraka (10.69).

Narada informed Krsna that Yudhisthira Maharaja was eager to perform the Rajasuya sacrifice (10.70.32-43), he spoke of Krsna\`s glories in the presence of Princess Laksmana (10.83.17), and with a number of other great sages, he came to Kuruksetra to be with Krsna and His devotees during a solar eclipse (10.84).

With other sages, Narada traveled on Krsna\`s chariot to Videha (10.86.17- 18). Another time He inquired from Lord Nara-Narayana about how the Absolute Truth, who is beyond words, can be described by the Vedas. The Lord replied by recounting the Prayers of the Personified Vedas (10.87.4-8).

Asked by Vrkasura which of the three lords of the universe can be most easily pleased, he told Vrka to worship Lord Siva (10.88.14-16).

Narada and other sages cursed the impetuous young Vrsnis, which led to the destruction of their dynasty (11.1.11-16). He instructed Vasudeva in pure devotional service by relating the discussions of King Nimi with the nine Yogendras (11.2-5).

Krsna personally glorified Narada by telling Uddhava, devarsinam narado \`hṁḍ: “I am Narada Muni among saintly demigods” (11.16.14).

This verse poetically says that the Lord assumed the form of Varaha (bibhrat kraudim tanum). The complete picture is that His form of Varaha exists eternally in Vaikuntha and appears as an avatara at certain times and places in the material creation.

Sri Brhad-bhagavatamrta (2.3.15-16) mentions that Lord Varaha is present within the shell of elemental earth that surrounds the universe, where the goddess Bhumi worships Him with incomparable opulence. In the Third Canto of Srimad-Bhagavatam (chapters 13, 17, 18 and 19) Maitreya tells Vidura about the Varaha avatara. And in the Fifth Canto (5.18.34- 39) Sukadeva describes how Bhumi-devi worships Lord Varaha in the Uttarakuru region of Jambudvipa.

**Пословный перевод:**

dvih— twice; avirasit— He appeared; kalpe — in the day of Brahma; asmin — this; adye — in the first; svayambhuva-antare — reign of Svayam- bhuva Manu; ghranat — from the nostril; vidheh— of Lord Brahma; dhara — of the earth; uddhrtyai — for the raising; caksusiye — during the reign of Caksusa Manu; tu — on the other hand; niratah — from the water; hiranyaksam — Hiranyaksa; dhara-uddhare — while lifting the earth; nihantum — to kill; damstri — among tusked beasts; pungavah — the most eminent; catus-pat — having four legs; sri-varahah — Sri Varaha; asau — He; nr-varahah — half-man, half-boar; kvacit — sometimes; matah — considered.

**He appeared twice in this day of Brahma. He first appeared during the reign of Svayainbhuva, the first Manu. He came out from the nostril of Lord Brahma and raised the earth planet from the lower regions of the universe. That supreme among tusked animals appeared again during the reign of Caksusa Manu. At that time, while lifting up the earth He came out from the universal waters to kill Hiranyaksa. Sri Varaha has four legs, but sometimes He is understood to have a form as half-man, half-boar.**

The first of these two Varaha appearances is described in the Bhagavatam\`s First Canto, and the second is described in the Second Canto. Both of these Varaha incarnations, as well as two Lord Matsya avataras, appeared during this first day, the Brahma-kalpa, of Brahmas current month, occurring during the beginning of his fifty-first year. The first Lord Varaha appeared during the Svayambhuva manvantara, when He came out from Lord Brahmas nostril and lifted the earth. The second Lord Varaha appeared during the reign of Caksusa Manu, when He came from within the universal water, lifted the earth, and killed Hiranyaksa.

Lord Varaha is portrayed with a half-human, half-boar form in the Padma Purana and other texts.

The previously quoted verse from the Second Canto, describing Lord Varaha\`s second appearance, mentions neither the Caksusa manvantara as the time nor the water of devastation as the source of His advent. How do we know, then, to distinguish this Varaha as a separate appearance? Evidence is found in the Fourth Canto. Previously the Supreme Lord had arranged for Daksa to be killed because of his offenses against Lord Siva and Sati. The Lord then gave Daksa a new body in the Caksusa manvantara and inspired him to repopulate the universe.

### Text 16

*kalparambhe tada nasti*  
*sutotpattir manor api*  
*kvasau pracetaso daksah*  
*kva ditir kva diteh sutah*

**Пословный перевод:**

kalpa — of the day of Brahma; arambhe — at the beginning; tada — then; na asti— there was not; suta — of sons; utpattih — birth; manoh — of Manu; api—even; kva — where; asau — he; pracetasah— son of the Pracetas; daksah — Daksa; kva— where; ditih — Diti; kva — where; diteh — of Diti; sutah— a son.

**Перевод:**

**In the beginning of Brahma’s day Manu did not yet have any offspring, so how could Daksa, son of the Pracetas, be present? And how then could Diti or Diti’s son be present?**

**Комментарий:**

Here is proof that Hiranyaksa and the avatara of Varaha who killed him appeared not in the Svayambhuva manvantara but later, in the Caksusa manvantara. There is no evidence that Svayambhuva\`s sons (Priyavrata and Uttanapada) or daughters (Akuti, Devahuti, and Prasuti) had children of their own during Svayambhuva\`s reign as Manu. There is evidence, however, that the Pracetas were descendants of Uttanapada, that Daksa was the son of the Pracetas, that Diti was the daughter of Daksa, and that Hiranyaksa was the son of Diti and her husband Kasyapa. It is thus not possible that Hiranyaksa, born eighteen generations (more than a billion years) after Uttanapada, could have been killed by the Lord Varaha who appeared at the beginning of the kalpa.

**Комментарий:**

In the initial narration of Lord Varaha\`s appearance, in the Third Canto, Maitreya Muni did not distinguish between the two Varahas, even though he described incidents from the pastimes of both of Them. In the thirteenth chapter of that canto, Maitreya described how Lord Varaha lifted the earth out of the Garbha Ocean. He mentioned in texts 31 and 32 of that chapter that Varahadeva also easily disposed of a demon who attacked Him when He came out of the water. At the beginning of the fourteenth chapter, Vidura asked to hear more about the killing of this demon, whom he identified as Hiranyaksa.

It may be asked why Lord Varaha had to rescue the earth in the middle of the first manvantara, long before the scheduled devastation of the lower part of the universe. As indicated here, special circumstances sometimes lead to a universal flood during a manvantara. The Matsya Purana relates that Svayambhuva Manu was once cursed by Agastya Muni to have the worlds inundated during his reign. When the earth was thus lost in the water, Lord Varaha appeared and lifted her out. In the sixth manvantara, Caksusa Manu was similarly cursed. According to the Visnu-dharmottara and other Puranas, however, the flood at that time was due to the Supreme Lords desire.

### Text 21-22

*tatha hi,*  
*manv-antare pariksine*  
*deva manv-antaresvarah*  
*mahar-lokam athasadya*  
*tisthanti gata-kalmasah*  
*manus ca saha sakrena*  
*devas ca yadu-nandana*  
*brahma-lokam prapadyante*  
*punar-avrtti-durlabham*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha hi — thus; manv-antare — a manv-antara; pariksine — when it is finishing; devah — the demigods; manv-antara — during the manv-antara; isvarah — presiding; mahah-lokam — Maharloka; atha — then; asadya — reaching; tisthanti — they remain; gata-kalmasah — freed from contamination; manuh — Manu; ca— and; saha — together with; sakrena — Indra; devah — the demigods; ca — and; yadu-nandana — o Yadu-nandana (Vajranabha); brahma-lokam — Brahmaloka; prapadyante — achieve; punah — again; avrtti — from which return; durlabham — rare.

**Перевод:**

**“At the end of Manu’s reign, the demigods who presided during his manvantara go in a purified condition to Maharloka, where they remain for some time. Manu, Indra, and their company of demigods then achieve Brahma-loka, o Yadu-nandana, from where one rarely returns to material life”**

**Комментарий:**

The end of a manvantara is also the end of the term of authority for Indra and the other demigods. They do not die at this time, but they have to vacate Svargaloka, since that region of the universe is being inundated. They go first to the higher planet Maharloka, and from there to the highest planet of the universe - Brahmaloka, or Satyaloka.

Generally, for those who must die, even for those who die while facing an enemy in battle, achievement of this realm of Lord Brahma is very rare. And even if some do achieve it, they cannot remain very long; when their good karma dissipates they must return to the lower worlds. As Sri Krsna states in the Bhagavad-gita (8.16): a-brahma-bhuvanal lokah punar-avartino \`rjuna (“From Brahmaloka on down, all the worlds are places where repeated birth and death take place”).

The retired Indra and other appointed demigods, however, can remain on Satyaloka for the rest of Brahmas life, and then may attain liberation along with him:

*brahmana sa te sarve*  
*samprapte pratisancare*  
*parasante krtdtmanah*  
*pravisanti param padam*

**“When the universe is dissolved at the end of Brahmas life, all of them, if they have perfected their lives, enter the supreme abode along with Brahma.”**

Srila Sridhara Svami cites this smrti in his commentary on Srimad- Bhagavatam 3.32.10.

**Комментарий:**

Markandeya Rsi spoke this passage, taken from the Visnu-dharmottara (1.75.5-6), to Sri Krsna\`s great-grandson Vajra. When the flood of devastation engulfs the earth and the seven Patala planets, the eight highest mountain ranges, headed by the Himalayas, escape destruction and remain visible to the demigods.

### Text 44

*sarva-veda-viruddham ca*  
*kapilo' nyo jagada ha*  
*sankhyam asuraye' nyasmai*  
*kutarka-paribrmhitarn*

**Пословный перевод:**

sarva-veda — to all the Vedas; viruddham — contrary; ca — and; kapilah — Kapila; anyah— another; jagada — spoke; ha — indeed; sankhyam— Sankhya philosophy; asuraye — to Asuri; anyasmai — another; kutarka — with bad logic; paribrmhitam — filled.

**Перевод:**

**“A different Kapila spoke to a different Asuri a Sankhya philosophy contrary to the Vedas and full of bad logic”**

**Комментарий:**

To resolve the confusion about whether Kapila avatar a was also the author of the well-known atheistic Sankhya, the Padma Purana explains that the atheist Kapila was a different person, a jiva who used the same name and promoted a similar but deviant philosophy. The son of Devahuti taught Sankhya principles perfectly consistent with the Vedas and Upanisads, but the other Kapila invented his own ideas without following Vedic authority.

According to a statement of Markandeya Rsi's in the Mahabharata (Vana- parva 211.21), the atheist Kapila was a powerful descendant of the fire god:

*kapilam paramarsim ca*  
*yam prahur yatayah sada*  
*agnih sa kapilo nama*  
*sankhya-yoga-pravartakah*

**“Self-controlled renunciants often refer to Kapila as an exalted sage. He was one of the fire gods descended from Agni, appearing with the name Kapila to institute the Sankhya yoga system”**

Lord Brahma mentions the original Lord Kapila, son of Devahuti, in his summary of the principal lila-avataras:

*jajne ca kardama-grhe dvija devahutyam*  
*stribhih samam navabhir atma-gatim sva-matre*  
*uṣṛ yayatma-samalam guna-sanga-pankam*  
*asmin vidhuya kapilasya gatim prapede*

**“The Lord then appeared as the Kapila incarnation, being the son of the Prajapati brahmana, Kardama, and his wife Devahuti, along with nine other women sHis sisters\]. He spoke to His mother about self-realization, by which, in that very lifetime, she became fully cleansed of the mud of the material modes and thereby achieved liberation, the path of Kapila.” (Bhagavatam 2.7.3)**

The demigod Aryama and other residents of Hiranmaya-varsa praise Lord Kapila with these words:

*yasminn asankhyeya-visesa-nama-*  
*rupakrtau kavibhih kalpiteyam*  
*sankhya yayd tattva-drsapaniyate*  
*tasmai namah sankhya-nidarsanaya te*

**“O my Lord, Your name, form, and bodily features are expanded in countless forms. No one can determine exactly how many forms exist, yet You Your- self, in Your incarnation as the learned scholar Kapiladeva, have analyzed the cosmic manifestation as containing twenty-four elements. Therefore if one is interested in Sankhya philosophy, by which one can enumerate the different truths, he must hear it from You. Unfortunately, non devotees simply count the different elements and remain ignorant of Your actual form. I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.” (Bhagavatam 5.18.33)**

The Bhagavatam (9.8.9-13) describes how the sons of Sagara, while searching for their fathers sacrificial horse, came upon Lord Kapila at His asrama and attacked Him, resulting in their bodies suddenly burning to ashes.

### Text 53

*sri-dhruva-priyah (11), tatraiva,*  
*viddhah sapatny-udita-patribhir anti rajno*  
*balo 'pi sann upagatas tapase vanani*  
*tasma adad dhruva-gatim grnate prasanno*  
*divyah stuvanti munayo yad upary-adhastat*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-dhruva-priyah — Sri Dhruva-priya; tatra eva — there also; viddhah — pinched; sapatni — by a co-wife; udita — uttered; patribhih — by the sharp words; anti—in the presence; rajnah — of the king; balah — a boy; api — although; san — being; upagatah — took to; tapase — for severe penances; vanani — a great forest; tasmai — to him; adat — gave as a reward; dhruva-gatim — a path to the Dhruva planet; grnate — who was praying; prasannah — being satisfied; divyah — the denizens of higher plan- ets; stuvanti — praise; munayah — great sages; yat — since; upari — above; adhastat — below; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**Sri Dhruva-priya (11) is also described in the seventh chapter of the Second Canto s2.7.8\]; “Being insulted by sharp words spoken by his stepmother in the presence of the king, Prince Dhruva, though only a boy, took to severe penances in the forest. The Lord was satisfied by his prayer and awarded him the Dhruva planet, which is worshiped by the great sages, above and below.”**

**Комментарий:**

King Uttanapada was so intimidated by his wife Suruci that he could not say anything when she insulted Dhruva, the son of his other wife. Due to his ksatriya spirit, Dhruva could not tolerate being insulted, even though only five years old, and so he at once left home. By good fortune he met Sri Narada on the way, and under the saints guidance Dhruva performed austerities in the forest. After six months his austerities became so severe that the well-being of the entire universe seemed threatened. At that time Lord Visnu appeared to Dhruva and awarded him a planet of his own to governin the highest region of the universe. This history is narrated in eighth and ninth chapters of the Fourth Canto of Srimad-Bhagavatam.

In the present verse, the sages “above” are the first sages in the universe, Brahmas sons Marici, Atri, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Bhrgu, Vasistha, Daksa, and Narada (Bhagavatam 3.12.22). The sages “below” are the seven sages Citraketu, Suroci, Viraja, Mitra, Ulbana, Vasubhrdyana, and Dyuman, who are sons of Vasistha and his wife Arundhati (Bhagavatam 4.1.40-41). Thus the sons of Brahma are “above” (upari), and the second generation saptarsis are “below” (adhastat).

### Text 54

*svayambhuve 'vatarokter*  
*namnas cakathanad iha*  
*yajhadinam ca tatroktya*  
*parisesya -pramanatah*  
*prasiddhya prsnigarbheti*  
*tad-akhyasya nigadyate*  
*hantayam adrir ity-adau*  
*padye govardhanadri-vat*

**Пословный перевод:**

svayambhuve — during the reign of Svayambhuva; avatara — of the incarna- tion; ukteh — because of being described; namnah — of the name; ca — and; akathanat — because of there being no mention; iha — in this text; yajna- adinam — of Lord Yajna and so on; ca — and; tatra — there; uktya — be- cause of there being mention; parisesya — of elimination; pramanatah — by the logic; prasiddhya — by the proof; prsnigarbha iti —as Prsnigarbha; tat — that; akhyasya — about Him who has the name; nigadyate — it is spoken; hanta ayam adrih iti — “Indeed this hill”; adau — which begins; padye — in the verse; govardhana-adri-vat — like Govardhana Hill.

**Перевод:**

**Considering that this avatara is said to have appeared in the Svayain-bhuva manvantara, that He is not specifically named in this verse sfrom the Second Canto, chapter seven\], and that each of the other incarnations (Yajna and so on) who appeared in that period are specifically named in that chapter, by elimination we conclude that this must be the well-known avatara Prsnigarbha. This is the same kind of reasoning used to conclude that the hill referred to in the verse beginning “Indeed this hill sBhagavatam 10.21.18\] is Govardhana.**

**Комментарий:**

From the Srimad-Bhagavatam's description of Lord Visnu's appearing before Dhruva, it is not clear whether the Lord came directly from Vaikuntha to bless Dhruva or instead took birth from a father and mother. Srila Rupa Gosvami resolves this doubt using the technique known as parisesya-nyaya, or “logic of the remainder”

Lord Yajna and the other incarnations who appeared during the Svayam-bhuva manvantara are all mentioned by name in the Bhagavatam, and except for Prsnigarbha, Their pastimes are mentioned along with Their names. However, the second and fourth cantos do contain descriptions of an un- named avatara who favored Dhruva during Svayambhuva Manus reign. The blessing of Dhruva is not associated with any of the other avatara of this manvantara, and therefore by parisesya-nyaya we can conclude that the blessing must have come from Lord Prsnigarbha.

Another example of using this logic to identify a certain person from a description of his particular activities is found in the verse glorifying Govardhana Hill spoken by the gopis when they were enchanted by the sound of Krsna’s flute:

*hantayam adrir abala hari-dasa-varyo*  
*yad rama-krsna-carana-sparasa-pramodah*  
*manam tanoti saha-go-ganayos tayor yat*  
*paniya-suyavasa-kandara-kandamulaih*

**“Of all the devotees of Hari, this hill is the best! o my friends, this hill sup- plies Krsna and Balarama, along with Their calves, cows, and cowherd friends with all kinds of necessities - water for drinking, very soft grass, caves, fruits, flowers, and vegetables. In this way the hill offers respects to the Lord. Being touched by the lotus feet of Krsna and Balarama, the hill appears very jubilant” (Bhagavatam 10.21.18)**

The gopis do not mention the hills name in this verse, but one can deduce from the context that they refer to none other than Giriraja Govardhana.

He was able to reprove Prthivi and induce her to give up her reluctance to produce food for everyone.

**Комментарий:**

In Srila Sanatana Gosvami's Brhad-bhagavatamrta, Lord Nrsimha's special kindness toward Prahlada is mentioned by Brahma (1.2.68-69), by Siva (1.3.80-81), and by Prahlada himself (1.4.24-25 and 38).

In Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Adi-lila, chapter seventeen, Srila Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami describes the incidents of Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu's assuming the mood of Sri Nrsimha and Nrsimha's threatening Chand Kazi for his obstruction of Lord Caitanya's sankirtana.

Srimad-Bhagavatam (Canto Seven, chapters 8-10) describes Lord Nrsimha's killing Hiranyakasipu and blessing Prahlada. In the Fifth Canto (Bhagavatam 5.18.7-14), Prahlada, while living in Hari-varsa, offers prayers to Lord Nrsimha.

In the Second Canto (2.7.14) Lord Brahma has this to say about the Nrsimha avatara:

*trai-pistaporu-bhaya-ha sa nrsimha-rupam*  
*krtva bhramad-bhru-kuti-damstra-karala-vaktram*

*urau nipatya vidadara nakhaih sphurantam*

**“The Personality of Godhead assumed the incarnation of Nrsimha-deva in order to vanquish the great fears of the demigods. Another name of Lord Kurma is Ajita, and by that name He is included in Srimad-Bhagavatam among the manvantara-avataras. Srila Rupa Gosvami will discuss these manvantara-avataras in the next chapter of the Laghu-bhagavatamrta.

The appearance of Lord Kurma during the churning of the Milk Ocean is described in the seventh chapter of the Eighth Canto of Srimad- Bhagavatam, and the prayers to Lord Kurma by Aryama and other residents of Hiranmaya-varsa are described in the Fifth Canto (5.18.29-33).

The demigods and demons were churning the Ocean of Milk with the Mandara Mountain in order to extract nectar. The mountain rotated back and forth, scratching the back of Lord Tortoise, who, while partially sleeping, was experiencing an itching sensation.” (Bhagavatam 2.7.13)**

According to Sri Padma Purana, the same Kurma avatara who lifted Mandara Mountain later lifted the entire earth from the lower regions of the universe. Other scriptures, however, including the Visnu-dharmottara Purana, describe the Kurma who perpetually holds up the earth as the one who lifted Mandara Mountain. Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana prefers this last version as the more reasonable, especially since Srila Rupa mentions it last.

### Text 74

*vamanas trir abhivyaktim*  
*kalpe 'smin pratipedivan*  
*tatradau danavendrasya*  
*baskaler adhvaram yayau*  
*tato vaivasvatiye 'smin*  
*dhundhor makham asau gatah*  
*aditau kasyapaj jatah*  
*saptame 'sya catur-yuge*  
*pratigraha-krte jatas*  
*traya eva trivikramah*

**Пословный перевод:**

vamanah — Lord Vamana; trih — three times; abhivyaktim — appearance; kalpe — in the day of Brahma; asmin — this; pratipedivan — assumed; tatra — there; adau— first; danava-indrasya— of the king of demons; baskaleh— Baskali; adhvaram — to the sacrifice; yayau — He went; tatah — then; vaivasvatiye — during the Vaivasvata manvantara; asmin — this; dhundhoh — of Dhundhu; makham — to the sacrifice; asau — He; gatah— went; adi- tau — in Aditi; kasyapat—from Kasyapa; jatah— born; saptame — in the seventh yuga cycle; asya — of this (manvantara); catuh-yuge— in the cycle of four yugas; pratigraha-krte— for taking charity; jatah — born; trayah — three; eva — indeed; trivikramah — forms of Lord Trivikrama.

**Перевод:**

**Lord Vamana has appeared three times in this day of Brahma. The first time He visited the sacrifice of Baskali, king of the demons. During the current Vaivasvata manvantara, Lord Vamana first went to the sacrifice of Dhundhu, and then later, in the seventh yuga-cycle of this manvantara, He took birth as the son of Kasyapa from the womb of Aditi. Lord Trivikrama has thus appeared three times for the purpose of accepting charity.**

**Комментарий:**

Lord Vamana accepted charity from Baskali in the first manvantara, that of Svayambhuva. His second appearance is mentioned in the Vamana Purana:

*dhundhor yajne vararohe*  
*bhagavan madhusudanah*  
*deham vamanakam krtva*  
*gatvayacat tri-pistapam*

**“O elegant woman, the Supreme Lord Madhusudana assumed the body of a dwarf and went to the sacrifice of Dhundhu to beg from him Indra’s heaven’’**

The third time Vamana appeared He tricked Bali into returning Indra’s kingdom to Him, as described at length in the Eighth Canto of Srimad-Bhagavatam, chapters 17-23.

In the Second Canto (2.7.17-18) Lord Brahma gives the following de- scription of Vamana’s third appearance:

*jyayan gunair avarajo 'pyaditeh sutanam*  
*lokan vicakrama iman yad athadhiyajnah*  
*ksmam vamanena jagrhe tripada-cchalena*  
*yacnam rte pathi caran prabhubhir na calyah*

**“Although the youngest of Aditi's sons, He possesses qualities that surpass those of all the others. And considering that He stepped over all the planets of the universe, He is certainly the Supreme Personality of Godhead. On the pretense of asking for a measurement of three footsteps of land, He took away all the lands of Bali Maharaja. He asked Bali's permission because a person who adheres to the path of religion may not be deprived of property, even by authorities, without giving permission.**

*nartho baler ayam urukrama-pada-saucam*  
*apah sikha-dhrtavato vibudhadhipatyam*  
*yo vai pratisrutam rte na cikirsad anyad*  
*atmanam anga manasa haraye 'bhimene*

**“Bali Maharaja, who put on his head the water that washed the Lords lotus feet, thought only of keeping his promise despite being forbidden by his spiritual master. The king dedicated his own body to fulfilling the measurement of the Lords third step. For such a personality, even the kingdom of heaven, which he had conquered by his strength, was of no value”**

The Brhad-bhagavatamrta often mentions the same Lord Vamana. Narada sees Vamana worshiped by His elder brother Indra (1. 2. 1-7), and Indra laments to Narada that although Vamana showed His mercy by returning Indra's kingdom, He did it in a way that also humiliated him (1. 2. 16- 17). Narada gives his opinion that Bali has conquered the Supreme Lord, who now serves as Bali's doorkeeper (1. 4. 13), Lord Siva gives his opinion that Lord Vamana became Bali's doorkeeper because He favored Bali's grandfather Prahlada (1. 3. 82-83), and Prahlada gives his opinion that Vamana acts as Bali's doorkeeper just to keep Bali captive (1. 4. 32-33). Prahlada also tells Narada that Vamana cannot easily be seen at Bali Maharajas gate; He shows Himself only to those whom He chooses, like Durvasa (1. 4. 33).

In the second chapter of the second part of Sri Bhagavatamrta, Gopa- kumara hears from some brahmanas about Vamana-devas avatara and His residence in Indra's court. Gopa-kumara then goes to heaven to see Lord Vamana and there witnesses Indra worshiping Him. In that assembly of devas, Vamana treats Gopa-kumara very kindly.

In the first part of the Brhad-bhagavatamrta, chapter four, Narada visits Kimpurusa-loka, where Hanuman always worships the Deity of Lord Ramacandra and recites His glories. In the second part of the Brhad-bhagavatamrta (4. 239-274), Gopa-kumara visits the eternal Ayodhya in the spiritual world and is granted intimate association with Lord Rama and His brothers.

As described in Sri Caitanya-caritdmrta (Madhya 9. 178-217), when Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu traveled in South India He met a brahmana devotee of Ramacandra who would not eat because he could not tolerate the idea that the demon Ravana had kidnapped the Lords consort. Lord Caitanya rescued this brahmana by discovering a passage in the Kiirma Purana explaining how Ravana had captured only a shadow of Mother Slta, created by maya.

Lord Caitanya's associate Murari Gupta was an incarnation of Hanuman and was fully devoted to Lord Ramacandra. When Lord Caitanya tried to convince Murari to worship Radha and Krsna instead, Murari made the attempt but could not abandon the lotus feet of his beloved Lord Rama. Lord Caitanya was completely satisfied with Murari Guptas unswerving devotion(Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya 15. 142-57). The gosvamis Rupa and Sanatana had a similar experience with their brother Anupama when they suggested he give up the worship of Lord Ramacandra and adopt the worship of Lord Krsna (Cc. Antya 4. 30-43).

Srimad-Bhagavatam describes Lord Ramacandra's pastimes in chapters ten and eleven of the Ninth Canto.

Lord Brahma glorifies Him in three verses in the Second Canto (2. 7. 23-25):

*asmat-prasada-sumukhah kalaya kalesa*  
*iksvdku-vamsa avatirya guror nidese*  
*tisthan vanam sa-dayitanuja dvivesa*  
*yasmin virudhya dasa-kandhara artim arcchat*

**“Due to His causeless mercy upon all living entities within the universe, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, along with His plenary extensions, appeared in the family of Maharaja Iksvaku as the Lord of His internal potency, Sita. Under the order of His father, Maharaja Dasaratha, He entered the forest and lived there for considerable years with His wife and younger brother. Ravana, who was very materially powerful, with ten heads on his shoulders, committed a great offense against Him and was thus ultimately vanquished.**

*yasma adad udadhir iidha-bhayanga-vepo*  
*mdrgam sapady ari-puram hara-vad didhaksoh*  
*dure suhrn-mathita-rosa-susona-drstya*  
*tatapyamdna-makaroraga-nakra-cakrah*

**“The Personality of Godhead Ramacandra, being aggrieved for His distant intimate friend sSita\], glanced over the city of the enemy Ravana with red- hot eyes like those of Hara swho wanted to burn the kingdom of heaven\]. The great ocean, trembling in fear, gave Him His way because its family members, the aquatics like the sharks, snakes, and crocodiles, were being burnt by the heat of the angry red-hot eyes of the Lord.**

*vaksah-sthala-sparsa-rugna-mahendra-vaha-*  
*dantair vidambita-kakub-jusa iidha-hasam*  
*sadyo subhih saha vinesyati dara-hartur*  
*visphurjitair dhanusa uccarato dhisainye*

**“When Ravana was engaged in the battle, the trunk of the elephant which carried the king of heaven, Indra, broke into pieces, having collided with the chest of Ravana, and the scattered broken parts illuminated all directions. Ravana therefore felt proud of his prowess and began to loiter in the midst of the fighting soldiers, thinking himself the conqueror of all directions. But his laughter, overtaken by joy, along with his very air of life, suddenly ceased with the resounding of the bow of Ramacandra, the Personality of Godhead.”**

Because of this information, some think that Krsna Dvaipayana was an empowered jiva like Sanaka Kumara and his brothers.

The First Canto of Srimad-Bhagavatam (chapters 4 and 5) relates how Dvaipayana Vyasa received from Narada the instruction to compile the Bhagavatam and (chapter 7) how Vyasa then meditated on the subject of the Bhagavatam, namely Sri Krsna and His energies.

It will be shown later on that Krsna and His own catur-vyuha - Himself, His brother Balarama, His son Pradyumna, and His grandson Aniruddha - are not expansions of the purusa-avatara.

The passages from devotional scriptures cherished by Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu and His followers focus primarily on Sri Krsnas glories. There are many such passages: for example, the last two chapters of part one of Brhad-bhagavatamrta, the last three chapters of that books part two, many passages throughout Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, and the entire Tenth Canto of Srimad-Bhagavatam. In the Bhagavatam's Third Canto, chapters 2 and 3, Uddhava remembers Krsna with special poignancy just after His disappearance.

In the Second Canto (2. 7. 26-35) Lord Brahma praises Krsna's pastimes in ten verses, beginning with this one:

The Lord conies in His original form, with beautiful black hair. And just to expand His transcendental glories, He acts extraordinarily. No one can properly estimate how great He is. ”**

*vaikunthas carcisas tadvat*  
*valmi-kalpas tato 'parah*

**“The twenty-second day is called Bhavana, followed by Supuman, Vaikuntha, Arcisa, and Valmi.**

*sapta-vimso 'tha vairajo*  
*gauri-kalpas tathaparah*  
*mahesvaras tatha proktas*  
*tripuro yatra ghatitah*

**“The twenty-seventh is Vairaja, then Gauri, and then Mahesvara, when the three cities of the demons are destroyed.**

*pitr-kalpas tathante ca*  
*yah kuhur brahmanah smrtah*  
*trimsat kalpah samakhyata*  
*brahmano divasaih sada*

**“At the end is the Pitr-kalpa, thought of as the new-moon day of Brahma. The thirty kalpas known by these names always correspond to the days of Lord Brahmas month.**

*atitas ca bhavisyas ca*  
*varaho vartate 'dhuna*  
*pratipat brahmanah prokta*  
*dvitiyardhasya sampratarn*

**“These kalpas have occurred in the past and will occur in the future. The present kalpa, known as Varaha, is considered the first day in the second half of Brahmas life.”**

The kalpa named Sveta or Sveta-varaha is also called the Brahma-kalpa because Brahma took birth during a Sveta-varaha-kalpa. 'The particular Pitr-kalpa (thirtieth day) that comes at the end of the first half of Brahmas life is known also as the Padma-kalpa because at that time the worlds are recreated from the lotus flower on which Brahma was born. In each kalpa there are fourteen manvantaras, and each manvantara includes seventy-one cycles of four ages. Altogether there are nearly one thousand yuga cycles in one kalpa.

## Chapter 4 - Manvantara-avataras, Yuga-avataras, Avesas and Avasthas

## Text l

*atha manv-antaravatarah,*  
*manv-antaravataro 'sau*  
*prayah sakrari-hatyaya*  
*tat-sahayo mukundasya*  
*pradurhhavah suresu yah*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha — next; manv-antara — during the reign of a Manu; avatarah— an incarnation; asau — that; prayah — usually; sakra-ari— the enemies of Indra; hatyaya — by killing; tat — of him (Indra); sahayah — helper; mukundasya — of Mukunda; pradurhhavah — an appearance; suresu — among the demigods; yah — which.

**Перевод:**

**Now the manvantara-avataras: A manvantara-avatara is Lord Mukunda appearing among the demigods, usually for the purpose of helping Indra by killing his enemies.**

**Комментарий:**

In the word manvantara, antara means “a period of time” In other words, a manvantara refers to the period in which a Manu reigns.

According to Halayudha's dictionary,

*vastu-madhye tatha chidre*  
*vyavasaye 'ntar-atmani*  
*avakase bahir-yoge*  
*visese vasare ntaram*

**“Antara can mean ‘the inside of an object,' ‘hole,’ ‘resolve,’ ‘mind,’ ‘space,’ ‘external relationship,’ ‘peculiarity,’ or ‘period of time.’”**

In the Second Canto of Srimad-Bhagavatam (2. 7. 20) Lord Brahma gives a general description of the manvantara-avataras:

*cakram ca diksv avihatam dasasu sva-tejo*  
*manv-antaresu manu-vamsa-dharo bibharti*  
*dustesu rajasu damam vyadadhat sva-kirtim*  
*satye tri-prstha usatim prathayams caritraih*

**“As the manvantara incarnations, the Lord has descended into each of the Manu dynasties and ruled over the miscreant kings, subduing them with His powerful wheel weapon. Undeterred in all circumstances, His reigns were characterized by His glorious fame, which spread over the three lokas, and above them to the planetary system of Satyaloka, the topmost in the universe.”**

In his instructions to Sanatana Gosvami, Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu described the manvantara-avataras and listed them by name (Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya 20. 319-28).

### Text 2

*yukte kalpavataratve*  
*yajnadinam api sphutam*  
*manv-antaravataratvam*  
*tat-tat-paryanta-palanat*

**Пословный перевод:**

yukte — simultaneous; kalpa-avataratve — while being an avatara for a kalpa; yajna-adinam — of Lord Yajna and others; api — even though; sphutam — self-evident; manvantara-avataratvam — being a manvantara-avatara; tat-tat—of each (manv-antara); paryanta — for the duration; palanat— because of giving protection.

**Перевод:**

**Some kalpa-avataras, like Lord Yajna, are also clearly manvantara-avataras because they give special protection for the duration of the reigns of particular Manus.**

**Комментарий:**

By definition, a kalpa-avatara appears at some time during a particular day of Brahma, and a manvantara-avatara appears in order to help the demigods for the duration of a Manus reign. Thus it is certainly possible for one incarnation to be both a kalpa-avatara and a manvantara-avatara.

**Перевод:**

Raivata, the fifth Manu, was the third brother of Uttama and Tamasa, the third and fourth Manus. The demigods collectively called the Vaikunthas were brothers of the manvantara-avatara Vaikuntha. Although the word kalpana usually means “manufacture,” it can also indicate “manifestation.” The verb klp, from which kalpana is derived, means “produce” or “imagine,” but it also sometimes means “able” Thus Lord Vaikuntha showed His extraordinary ability by exhibiting a Vaikuntha planet within the material world. Srila Sanatana Gosvami mentions this pastime in his Brhaci-bhdgavatdmrta (1. 2. 22) and further explains it in his Dig-darsini commentary on that book.

Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu, the avatara for the current Kali-yuga, appears only once in an entire day of Brahma. Although He has a golden complexion, He accepts the name “Krsna.” Indeed, He is Krsna Himself.

### Text 41

**Перевод:**

**Комментарий:**

This statement of the Visnu-dharma Purana does not indicate that Lord Krsna Caitanya Mahaprabhu does not manifest His own form in Kali-yuga. The avatara for Kali-yuga is usually a specially appointed jiva who, according to smrti-sastra, generally has a blackish complexion. Lord Caitanya, however, appears in just one specific Kali-yuga out of the thousand in each day of Brahma. He is the pita-varna form of the original Supreme Lord mentioned by Garga Muni (Bhagavatam 10.8.13). When He descends, the krsna-varna avesa incarnation for Kali-yuga unites with Him.

In Sri Caitanya-caritamrta (Madhya 6.94-104) Gopinatha Acarya explained to Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya why sastra says that the Supreme Lord incarnates in only three of the four ages.

In His instructions to Sanatana Gosvami, Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu described the prabhava and vaibhava divisions of His original svayam-rupa (prabhava-prakasa and vaibhava-prakasa) and His vilasa expansions (prabhava-vilasa and vaibhava-vilasa). The explanation of Krsnas svayam-rupa and vilasa forms is recorded in Sri Caitanya-caritamrta (Madhya 20.167-243).

## Chapter 5 - Para-avasthas and Svayam-bhagavan

## Text l

*atha*  
*krsno nara-bhraturavatara iti kvacit*  
*upendrasyeti ca kvapi*  
*bhaty asau nati-kovidam*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha — next; krsnah — Krsna; nara — of Nara; bhratuh — of the brother; avatarah — an avatara; iti — thus; kvacit — sometimes; upendrasya — of Upendra; iti — thus; ca — and; kva api — sometimes; bhati — appears; asau — He; na ati-kovidam — for those who are not very expert.

**Перевод:**

**Now we will discuss how less expert thinkers sometimes consider Krsna an incarnation of Nara’s brother, and sometimes an incarnation of Lord Upendra.**

**Комментарий:**

The analysis of the divisions of Godhead that Srila Rupa Gosvami has presented establishes that Krsna is the original form of the Supreme, and that the husband of Goddess Sri and all other forms of God are His vilasa, svamsa, and avesa expansions. Some less expert thinkers, such as the followers of a teacher named Visvaksena, say either that Krsna expands from Nara-Narayana or that He expands from Vamana-deva.

### Text 2

*yatha skande,*  
*dharma-putrau harer amsau*  
*nara-narayanabhidhau*  
*candra-vamsam anuprapya*  
*jatau krsnarjunav ubhau*

**Пословный перевод:**

yatha — as; skande — in the Skanda Purana; dharma — of Dharma; putrau — two sons; hareh — of Lord Hari; amsau — expansions; nara-narayana-abhidhau — named Nara and Narayana; candra-vamsam — the dynasty of the moon god; anuprapya — joining; jatau — born; krsna-arjunau — Krsna and Arjuna; ubhau — both.

**Перевод:**

**We find in the Skanda Purana: “When Krsna and Arjuna took birth in the dynasty of the moon god, the expansions of Lord Hari known as Nara and Narayana, the sons of Dharma, joined with them.”**

**Комментарий:**

A follower of Visvaksena might mistakenly think that this verse supports the conclusion that Krsna expands from Nara-Narayana. But a closer study reveals a more accurate translation.

Krsna and Arjuna are the subjects of the sentence, and Nara and Narayana are the objects. Since the dual forms ending in -au can be either subject or object, we must consider logical and contextual factors to distinguish the subject from the object. In light of the unassailable presentation by Srimad-Bhagavatam that Krsna is svayam bhagavan, prapya can be taken to mean “accepting within themselves.” The verse indicates, then, that Krsna and Arjuna took birth in the candra-vamsa and that their partial expansions, Narayana and Nara Rsis, entered within them to take part in their pastimes.

### Text 3

*sri-caturthe ca,*  
*tav imau vai bhagavato*  
*harer amsav ihagatau*  
*bhara-vyayaya ca bhuvah*  
*krsnau yadu-kurudvahau*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-caturthe — in the Fourth Canto; ca — and; tau — both; imau — these; vai — indeed; bhagavatah — of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; hareh — Hari; amsau — part-and-parcel expansions; iha — here; agatau — appeared; bhara-vyayaya — for the mitigation of the burden; ca — and; bhuvah — of the earth; krsnau — the two Krsnas (Krsna and Arjuna); yadu-kuru-udvahau — the best of the Yadu and Kuru dynasties respectively.

**Перевод:**

**And in the Fourth Canto s4.1.59\]: “Those two expansions of Hari sNara and Narayana\] have now appeared in the forms of the two Krsnas, the best of the dynasties of Yadu and Kuru, to mitigate the burden of the world.”**

**Комментарий:**

This verse might seem to say that Narayana and Nara, the expansions of Lord Kslrodaka-sayi Visnu, appeared as Vasudeva and Arjuna to relieve the earth from the burden of demonic kings. The accurate reading, however, is that Nara and Narayana had now entered the bodies of Arjuna and Krsna.

### Text 4

*etad-upodbalakam sri-dasame,*  
*sampujya deva rsi-varyam rsih purano*  
*narayano nara-sakho vidhinoditena*  
*vanyabhibhasya mitayamrta-mistaya tam*  
*praha prabho bhagavate karavama he kim*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

etat — for this; upodbalakam — support; sri-dasame — in the Tenth Canto; sampujya — fully worshiping; devah — Lord Krsna; rsi — of sages; varyam — the greatest; rsih — the sage; puranah — primeval; narayanah —Lord Narayana; nara-sakhah — the friend of Nara; vidhina — by scripture; uditena — enjoined; vanya — with speech; abhibhasya — conversing; mitaya —measured; amrta —with nectar; mistaya — sweet; tam — him, Narada; praha — He addressed; prabho —o master; bhagavate —for the lord; karavama — We may do; he — O; kim — what; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**This evidence is found in the Tenth Canto s10.69.16\]: “After fully worshiping Narada, the best of sages, according to Vedic injunctions, Lord Krsna (who is the original sage, who is Narayana, and who is the friend of Nara) conversed with Narada in thoughtful words as sweet as nectar. Finally the Lord asked Narada, ‘What may We do for you, Our lord and master?’”**

**Комментарий:**

Even by definition Sri Krsna is Narayana because He is the source and shelter of everything that exists. He is the original sage because at the beginning of the kalpa He imparted knowledge to Lord Brahma (Gopala-tapani Upanisad, 1.23). He is nara-sakha, the friend of human beings, because He is eager to reveal His pleasure pastimes in His humanlike form. He is deva, a greatly effulgent Lord, especially in His lila as a ksatriya.

### Text 5

*upendravataratvam ca yatha hari-vamse sakra-vacane,*  
*aindram vaisnavam asyaiva*  
*ḍṝñṛ bhagam aham dadau*  
*yaviyamsam aham premna*  
*krsnam pasyami narada*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

upendra — of Upendra; avataratvam — the status of being an incarnation; ca — and; yatha — as; hari-vamse — in the Hari-vamsa; sakra — of Sakra (Indra); vacane — in the words; aindram — in the Indra sacrifice; vaisnavam — meant for Lord Visnu; asya — His; eva — indeed; ḍṝñṛ — o sage; bhagam — the portion of oblations; aham — I; dadau — gave; yaviyamsam — as my younger brother; aham — I; premna — with love; krsnam — to Krsna; pasyami — see; narada — o Narada; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**Indra speaks of Krsna as an incarnation of Upendra in the Hari-vamsa s2.70.34\]: “O sage, in the Aindra sacrifice I gave Krsna the portion of oblations meant for Lord Visnu. I love Krsna, o Narada, because I see Him as my younger brother.”**

**Комментарий:**

Since Krsna is Indras younger brother as Vamanadeva, Indra is affectionate toward Him even when there is cause for quarrel. The above statement was made during the incident when Krsna took the heavenly parijata tree from Svarga-loka to Dvaraka. It is forbidden to bring the parijata flower to earth. Therefore Indra felt obliged to refuse Krsnas request and oppose any attempt to take the tree by force.

The Vedic sacrifice known as Aindra was first performed by Indra. During this sacrifice, the portion of oblations that Indra previously offered to Lord Visnu he now offers to Vamana, whom he identifies with Krsna. Less intelligent persons may speculate that this indicates that Krsna expands from Lord Vamana, but Indra does not make clear which of the two he considers the original.

**Перевод:**

**Krsna’s identification with both these avataras is not at all contradictory. The two are said to be expansions of Krsna, the para-avastha (complete) form of the Supreme Lord.**

**Пословный перевод:**

nara-bhratuh— of the brother of Nara; iha — here; amsatvam — being the partial expansion; ete ca amsa iti— “These are partial expansions”; vaksyate— will be said; upendrasya — of Upendra; tathatvam— the same situation; ca — and; hari-vamse— in the Hari-vamsa; api — also; drsyate— is seen.

**That the brother of Nara is a partial expansion of Krsna can be understood from the verse beginning “ete camsa-kalah.” sBhagavatam 1.3.28) That Lord Upendra is a partial expansion can be seen in the Hari-vamsa.**

tatra — there; dharma-putrau — “The two sons of Dharma”; iti-adau— in reference to the verse beginning; karika — an explanatory verse; nara- narayanau— Nara and Narayana; prapya — obtaining; iti — thus; atma-sat- krtya — accepting for Themselves; tau — They two; svayam — Themselves; krsna-arjunau— Krsna and Arjuna; candra-vamsam— the dynasty of the moon god; anu — accepting; prakatatam gatau — manifested.

If the principal meaning of the word prapya (“obtaining”) is not suitable in a given context, then one must find another acceptable meaning.

*tathapi ksatra-lilaya*

**Пословный перевод:**

sampujya iti-adau — of the words beginning “worshiping”; karikah — explanatory verses; sarva-adau — in the very beginning; upadestrtvat — because of being the giver of instructions; yah — who; purana-rsih — the ancient sage; ucyate — is called; narainam — of the Naras; purusanam — namely the Purusa incarnations; yah — who; trayanam — of the three; asrayah — the shelter; sah — He; tu — and; naresu — among men; martya- lokesu— the inhabitants of the mortal world; saha-cari—the companion; bhavan — becoming; svayam — personally; tat — of them (mortal men); dharmam — the religious principles; anukrtya — imitating; atra — here; pujayam asa — worshiped; tam —that; munim — sage; narayana — Narayana; akhyena — with the name; amsena — by the partial expansion; krsnah — Krsna; yadi api — although; tat — his; guruh — spiritual preceptor; naradam — Narada; pujayam asa — He worshiped; tatha api — nevertheless; ksatra — of being a ksatriya; lilaya — as a pastime.

**Karikas on the verse beginning “sampujya”: Krsna is called the “most ancient of sages” because He gave spiritual instruction at the very beginning of the creation. He is called Narayana because He is the shelter of the three Naras, the Purusa incarnations. He is called “the friend of nara” because He joined with the human beings on the earth and executed dharma as if one of them, and thus He offered worship to the sage Narada. Although Krsna is Narada’s guru in His partial expansion as Narayana Rsi, during His ksatriya-lila He worshiped Narada.**

**Комментарий:**

According to Sri Gopala-tapani Upanisad (1.23) Krsna gave instructions to Brahma at the beginning of Brahmas day. Thus, at the beginning of a new phase of creation Krsna is the first spiritual authority, the purana-rsi.

Nara is a synonym for the word purusa, so the three Purusa incarnations who create the material world are sometimes called the Naras. Because Krsna is the shelter of the three Naras, as Sri Brahma-samhita describes, He is Narayana. He is, moreover, the friend of all naras, or human beings. Therefore, to set an example while playing the part of a human being, Krsna offers worship to the great sage Narada, even though Krsna's partial expansion Badari-narayana is Narada’s instructing spiritual master.

In the Kena Upanisad Indra, Agni, and Vayu are said to be knowers of the Absolute Truth. How then can Indra be called less intelligent? Srila Rupa Gosvami answers that to facilitate Krsnas pastime Indras wisdom became temporarily covered, and therefore he felt envious of Krsnas superiority.

The perfections of Godhead are exhibited to different degrees by the various expansions of Krsna, who alone fully exhibits all six categories of perfection. The three most glorious forms of the Supreme Person are designated in Vedic Texts as para-avastha, most perfect. The Lord exhibits His perfections in progressively greater completeness as Nrsimha, as Ramacandra, and finally in His ultimate form as Krsna.

### Text 28

*yatha,*  
*ucca-sthe graha-pancake sura-gurau sendau navamyam tithau*  
*lagne karkatake punarvasu-yute mesam gate pusani*  
*nirdagdhum nikhilah palasa-samidho medhyad ayodhyaraner*  
*avirbhutam abhud apurva-vibhavam yat kihcid ekam mahah*

**Пословный перевод:**

yatha— as; ucca-sthe — in exalted positions; graha — of planets; pancake — the group of five; sura-gurau — in the guru of the demigods (Brhaspati, or Jupiter); sa-indau — along with the moon; navamyam tithau — on the ninth lunar day; lagne—joined; karkatake — in the sign Cancer; punar- vasu — with the lunar mansion Punarvasu; yute—conjoined; mesam — the sign Aries; gate — reached; pusani — the sun; nirdagdhum — to burn to ashes; nikhilah — all; palasa-samidhah — kindling from palasa wood; medhyat — sanctified for sacrifices; ayodhya — of Ayodhya; araneh — fromthe forest; avirbhutam — manifest; abhut — became; apurva — unprecedented; vibhavam — whose powers; yat kincit — that certain; ekam — one; mahah — great person.

**Перевод:**

**“On the ninth lunar day, with five planets in exalted positions, with the moon and Jupiter conjoined on the horizon in Cancer and in the naksatra Punarvasu, and with the sun in Aries, a certain greatly effulgent person with unprecedented opulences appeared like a sacrificial fire from the pure arani wood of Ayodhya to burn to ashes all the palasa fuel-wood of the flesh-eating demons.”**

**Комментарий:**

The auspicious circumstances surrounding Lord Ramacandra's birth tell much about His divinity. Outlining the astrological configuration of the heavens at the moment of His advent, the guidebook on His worship, Sri Ramarcana-candrika, states that Lord Rama appeared from His blessed abode Ayodhya like a sacrificial fire ignited from sacred kindling wood. As the fire of sacrifice burns to ashes all the fuel-wood placed into it, so Lord Ramacandra destroyed the entire race of man-eaters. The word palasa means “meat-eater” but also refers to one of the seven kinds of wood used for fuel in Vedic yajnas.

Lord Ramacandra was born on the ninth lunar day of the bright half of the month of Caitra. At that time the sun, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn were each in the constellations of their exaltation - respectively Aries, Capricorn, Cancer, Pisces, and Libra. The sun was in the tenth degree of Aries, Mars in the third degree of Capricorn, Jupiter in the twenty-eighth degree of Cancer, Venus in the twenty-seventh degree of Pisces, and Saturn in the twentieth degree of Libra. Cancer ascending contained Jupiter conjunct with the moon.

His fame has endured for millions of years, but not because He managed to perform such feats as bridging the ocean. He accepted help from Sugriva and his monkey army only because it suited His pleasure.

**Комментарий:**

These karikas (Texts 32-33) elucidate the two verses quoted from the Ninth Canto. The word atta, which comes at the end of the first line of the first of these Ninth Canto verses, often means “assumed,” but this cannot be the intended meaning here. The Supreme did not assume the form of Lord Ramacandra, because that form is eternal. Therefore, in this context atta means “revealed.”

And when Krsna left Vraja to live in Mathura, the hearts of His intimate associates in Vraja were sustained only by the indelible image of His beauty, which is an even greater excellence.
