In this verse Srila Bilvamangala Thakura speaks of Krsnas lotus navel because he remembers his own personal experience with Krsna, who kindly revealed to him His unmanifest Vrndavana pastimes.

**This darling son of Devaki is an unprecedented ocean of nectar filled with supreme opulence and sweetness. Later we will focus on His characteristics in detail.**

**Комментарий:**

Srila Rupa Gosvami will later explain that Devaki is also a name of Yasoda, and that therefore Devaki-nandana is a name for Krsna both as the son of Nanda and as the son of Vasudeva. As Vasudeva-suta, Krsna performs pastimes that, for the most part, prominently reveal His power and opulence, while as Nanda-suta He performs only humanlike pastimes that prominently reveal His sweetness.

Vasudeva-sutas lila is clothed in opulence while decorated with sweetness, like an opulent mirror decorated with an attractive picture. By contrast, Nanda-sutas lila is clothed in sweetness while decorated with opulence, like a beautifully painted stage curtain decorated at the bottom with a row of opulent mirrors. Both these forms of Krsna are oceans of nectar, but the form of Krsna in Vraja is the most absolutely perfect.

It is only natural to enter a palace by walking up the staircase that leads to its entrance.

*sayujyam sasvate harau*

**Пословный перевод:**

**Перевод:**

**In Part Four of the Visnu Purana s4.15.1-2\] Maitreya asks this question: “After Visnu killed Hiranyakasipu, and later Ravana, the jiva who had taken birth as those demons achieved facilities for material enjoyment even the demigods cannot attain. Why, in those circumstances, did he not achieve the liberation of merging into the eternal Lord Hari, as he did after he took birth as Sisupala, who was killed by the Lord?”**

**Комментарий:**

The sayujya in this verse refers not to the imaginary obliteration of individual existence and merging into the Supreme but rather to saha-yoga, a union of intimate cooperation. Even the srutis sometimes use the word sayujya to mean close connection rather than complete merging, for example in the Maha-narayana Upanisad (25.1): yo daksine pramiyate pitrnam eva mahimanam gatva candramasah sayujyam sva-lokam apnoti. “One who dies during the suns movement toward the south achieves only the greatness of the Pitas and enters into the moon as his destination”

Maitreya is curious to know why Hiranyakasipu and Ravana did not achieve liberation when they were killed by the Supreme Lord, whereas Sisupala achieved it at once. Hiranyakasipu, Ravana, and Sisupala are three appearances of the same Vaikuntha gatekeeper, Jaya, while Nrsimhadeva, Ramacandra, and Krsna are three appearances of the same Personality of Godhead. Does this occurrence provide evidence of a measurable hierarchy of essential identity and personal qualities among these three para-avastha-rupas of the Supreme Person?

### Text 43

*sri-parasarottaram,*  
*daityesvarasya vadhayakhila-lokotpatti-sthiti-vinasa-karina apurva-tanu-*  
*grahanam kurvata nrsimha-rupam aviskrtam. tatra hiranyakasipor visnur*  
*ayam ity etan na manasy abhut. niratisaya-punya-jata-samudbimtam*  
*etat sattvam iti rajodreka-preritaikagra-matis tad-bhavana-yogat tato*  
*vapta-vadha-haitukim niratisayam evakhila-trailokyadhikya-dharinim*  
*dasananatve bhoga-sampadam avapa.*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-parasara — of Sri Parasara; uttaram — the answer; daitya — of the demons; isvarasya— of the ruler; vadhaya— for killing; akhila — all; loka — of the worlds; utpatti — the creation; sthiti — maintenance; vinasa — and destruction; karina — by Him who performs; apurva — unprecedented; tanu — of a body; grahanam — the acceptance; kurvata — who did; nrsimha-rupam— the form of Nrsimha; aviskrtam — revealed; tatra — in that instance; hiranyakasipoh— of Hiranyakasipu; visnuh ayam iti— “This is Visnu”; etat — this; na— not; manasi — in the mind; abhut— arose; niratisaya— unsurpassed; punya — by pious credits; jata — generated; samudbhutam — manifest; etat— this; sattvam — entity; iti — thus thinking; raja —of the mode of passion; udreka — by an excess; prerita — impelled; eka-agra — single-pointed; matih — whose mentality; tat — of that; bhavana — attitude; yogat — by the practice; tatah — subsequently; avapta — he obtained; vadha-haitukim — as a result of being killed; niratisayam — unequaled; eva — only; akhila — all; trai-lokya — the three worlds; adhikya-dharinim — surpassing; dasa-ananatve — as Ravana, who had ten heads; bhoga — for enjoyment; sampadam — facilities; avapa — he obtained.

**Перевод:**

**Sri Parasara answered: “To kill the king of the demons, He who is the creator, maintainer, and destroyer of all the worlds revealed His unparalleled form of Nrsimha. At that time Hiranyakasipu did not realize that Nrsimha was Visnu. Thinking that this powerful being had accumulated heaps of extremely pious credits, Hiranyakasipu focused his attention on Him under the strong impulsion of the mode of passion. By concentrating his mind on the Lord in this way while the Lord killed him, in his next life as ten-headed Ravana Hiranyakasipu was only given facilities for material enjoyment that are unequaled in the three worlds.**

**Комментарий:**

Lord Nrsimha is essentially the same person as Sri Krsna. They are not different in svarupa, or identity, but rather in guna, or manifest qualities. When a vaidurya stone changes color, it manifests a quality it already contains within itself. In a similar way, when the Personality of Godhead wanted to free the universe from the threat of Hiranyakasipu, He manifested His form as Nrsimha.

But if Lord Nrsimha is none other than Krsna Himself, why was Hiranyakasipu not liberated when killed by Him? Parasara Muni will explain that when Lord Krsna kills a demon He insinuates Himself into the heart of that particular soul by the charm of His personality, names, and other attractive qualities. Lord Nrsimha, however, does not exert this liberating, all-attracting influence on the fallen jivas who encounter Him.

Then what was Hiranyakasipu's awareness regarding the Lord in His form as Nrsimha? He saw Him as a powerful living being like himself, endowed with extraordinary qualities. Why? Because the strong influence of the mode of passion always distorts understanding. Nevertheless, in spite of his bewildered condition, by intensely focusing his attention on this amazing man-lion who would kill him with His own hands, Hiranyakasipu gained, in his next life, wealth and power beyond the reach of the demigods.

### Text 44

*natas tasminn anadi-nidhane para-brahma-bhute bhagavaty analambani-*  
*krte manasas tal-layam.*

**Пословный перевод:**

**Перевод:**

**“Because of Hiranyakasipu’s bewilderment, his mind did not actually take shelter of and unite with the Personality of Godhead, the Supreme Absolute Truth, without beginning or end.**

**Комментарий:**

Before ones mind can fully enter the transcendental shelter, one must become convinced that He is the Absolute Truth. Or, the mind may enter a similar state if one becomes extremely hateful toward Him. Hiranyakasipu, king of the demons, had neither of these prerequisites and so did not merge His mind fully in Lord Nrsimha. Thus, without accepting the Personality of Godhead as the exclusive resort of his mind, he could not attain liberation.

### Text 45

*dasananatve ’py ananga-paradhinataya janaki-samasakta-cetaso dasarathi-*  
*rupa-dharinas tad-rupa-darsanam evasit. nayam acyuta ity asaktir*  
*vipadyato 'ntah-karane manusa-buddhir eva kevalam asyabhut. punar apy*  
*acyuta-vinipatana-matra-phalam akhila-bhu-mandala-slaghyam cedi-raja-*  
*kule janma avyahatam caisvaryam sisupalatve cavapa.*

**Пословный перевод:**

dasa-ananatve — as ten-headed Ravana; api — moreover; ananga — of lust; para-adhinataya — because of being under the sway; janaki—with Janaki; samasakta — obsessed; cetasah — whose mind; dasarathi-rupa — the form of the son of Dasaratha; dharinah— of Him who assumed; tat — His; rupa — of the form; darsanam — the vision; eva — only; asit — there was; na — not; ayam acyutah iti — “This is the infallible Lord”; asaktih — attachment; vipadyatah — of Him who was unfortunate; antah-karane — in his mind; manusa — that He was a human being; buddhih — the idea; eva — indeed; kevalam — only; asya — for whom; abhut — there arose; punah api — then again; acyuta — by Lord Acyuta; vinipatana — of being brought down; matra — only; phalam — the fruit; akhila-bhu-mandala — throughout the earth; slaghyam — glorious; cedi-raja-kule — in the royal family of Cedi; janma — a birth; avyahatam — unrivaled; ca — and; aisvaryam — great power; sisupalatve — as Sisupala; ca — and; avapa — he obtained.

**Перевод:**

**“Then in his next life as Ravana, under the sway of Cupid he became obsessed with Janaki. Thus, although he saw the Lord in His form as the son of Dasaratha, he failed to become spiritually attracted to Him or to realize, ‘Here is the infallible Lord.' Instead, he conceived of Him as an ordinary human, and again he obtained diminished results from dying at Lord Acyuta’s hands. He next took birth as Sisupala in the glorious, world-renowned family of the kings of Cedi and enjoyed unimpeded power.**

**Комментарий:**

Why was this demonic individual not given liberation when he was killed a second time by the Lord, as Rama, who is also Krsna Himself? Because again, the specific relationship with the Lord that results in liberation did not become manifest. Ten-headed Ravana was enchanted by the divine goddess of fortune, but unfortunately he could see her only as an extremely attractive woman without knowing that she was the wife of the Supreme Lord. Ravana had the rare opportunity to see Lord Krsna in His form as Sri Dasarathi, but, thinking the Lords birth in a royal family a result of good karma, he again considered Him a finite creature.

Ravana failed to recognize infallible Visnu, the greatest of lords, personally endowed with all eternal excellences. Therefore he could not develop sufficient attraction to qualify for liberation. When Ravana's wife scolded Him for insisting on opposing Lord Rama, Ravana disclosed that he theoretically understood the Lords glories. This superficial knowledge, however, could not gain him liberation absent the ingredient of intense attraction. Therefore, when Ravana died from the arrow shot by Lord Rama, he again only attained great material opulence in his next life. From being killed personally by the Supreme Lord, Ravana took his next birth in the most powerful royal family of the Cedis.

The reward for seeing the Personality of Godhead, even with clouded vision, while dying at His hands is wealth and power greater than that of the demigods in heaven, as is confirmed in the Vedanta-sutras (3.3.53): na samanyad apy upalabdher mrtyu-van na hi lokapattih.

Liberation does not come from seeing the Supreme with ordinary vision, just as it does not come simply from dying. The result of seeing the Supreme with ordinary vision is elevation to higher worlds. This sutra sheds light on why some unenlightened persons can see the Supreme Lord when He incarnates and why many who see Him do not get liberation. Paraphrasing the sutra, the Narayana-tantra states, samanya-darsanal loka muktir yogyatma-darsanat. “By seeing the Supreme with ordinary vision one attains higher planets, but by seeing Him in the proper way one attains liberation.”

Krsnas enchantment potency becomes manifest primarily in two ways - through the charm of His names and the beauty of His transcendental body. Thus he became totally absorbed in this meditation. Attracted by the charm of Krsnas names and bodily form, Sisupala could not remove the image of His beauty from his mind for a moment.

**Комментарий:**

Thus, although the three para-avastha forms of the Supreme Lord are essentially equal, only the svayam-rupa, Krsna, always manifests the specific potency required for liberation. Demons killed by Lord Nrsimha and Lord Ramacandra do not generally obtain liberation. Therefore Sri Krsna, more than any other form of God, is Bhagavan. He alone intrinsically possesses all perfections (bhagas), completely fulfilling the significance of the suffix -van. Krsnas tu bhagavan svayam: He is the ultimate reservoir of everything. He rewards even demons with liberation, but the liberated state attained by those devotees who love Him purely is infinitely greater, for He becomes their sold-out servant.

In this passage the sage Parasara recommends devotion to the Supreme Lord rather than hatred for Him. Hatred is an undesirable emotion that demons express toward the Lord.

Sisupala attained liberation only because he absorbed his mind fully in Krsna consciousness. Devarsi Narada recommends tasmat kenapy upayena manah krsne nivesayet (Bhagavatam 7.1.32): “Therefore by whatever means possible one should absorb his mind in Krsna.”

*atah sarvesu kalpesu*

**Пословный перевод:**

**Перевод:**

**Therefore we cannot consider these demons, who appear every day of Brahma, incarnations of Visnu’s two associates, who would not realistically fall down every kalpa.**

**Комментарий:**

Someone may object, “How does this discourse between Parasara and Maitreya show that Krsna is the original Godhead? We know from the Third Canto of Srimad-Bhagavatam about the fall of Jaya and Vijaya from Vaikuntha due to the curse of the four Kumaras. We also know about their release from the curse and their return to service in Vaikuntha when Krsna killed them in their third incarnations. Their liberation after three births as demons was the realization of the terms of their curse. Where is the evidence of Krsna\`s unique power to liberate?”

This objection is countered by verses fifty and fifty-one. Parasara deliberately did not mention the two fallen associates of Vaikuntha because he understood they could not fall from Vaikuntha every day of Brahma. That would contradict the promises that Lord Hari is always kind to His devotees and that one who attains Vaikuntha never returns to this world. The Lord fights with demons in each kalpa, but not necessarily with Vaikuntha associates. The fall of Jaya and Vijaya from Vaikuntha related in the Third Canto is a special, rare event caused by the Lords own desire.

The Lord of Vaikuntha expresses this desire in the Third Canto (3.16.29) as follows:

*bhagavan anugav aha*  
*yatam ma bhaistam astu sam*  
*brahma-tejah samartho \`pi*  
*hantum necche matam tu me*

**“The Lord then said to His attendants, Jaya and Vijaya: ‘Depart this place, but fear not. All glories unto you. Though I am able to nullify the brahmanas\` curse, I will not do so. On the contrary, it has My approval.’”**

Commentaries on this verse explain that Jaya and Vijaya fell by their own desire. When they had heard bards in Lord Narayana\`s court singing about their masters prowess in fighting with demons, they wanted to see how He enjoyed this combat, and the Lord responded to the desires of His devotees. Krsna is thus glorified with the phrases sveccha-mayasya (Bhagavatam 10.14.2), “You appear according to the desires of Your dear devotees,” and bhaktecchopatta-dehaya (Bhagavatam 10.59.25), “You assume Your various forms to fulfill Your devotees desires.”

Someone may then object, “Don’t these glorifications contradict the declaration that no one returns from Vaikuntha?” Certainly no one ever returns from Vaikuntha impelled by karma, but someone can return if he wants to. If it were considered improper to come down from Vaikuntha by one\`s own desire, then Lord Hari Himself would be guilty of that impropriety.

On the other hand, we also learn from the Bhagavatam (10.88.25-26) that one does not even have to return from the region of Vaikuntha present within Satyaloka in the material world:

*tato vaikuntham agamad*  
*bhasvaram tamasah param*  
*yatra narayanah saksan*  
*nyasinam paramo gatih*  
*santanam nyasta-dandanam*  
*yato navartate gatah*

**“Then Lord Siva reached the luminous realm of Vaikuntha, beyond all darkness, where the Supreme Lord Narayana resides. That realm is the destination of renunciants who have attained peace and given up all violence against other creatures. Going there, one never returns.”**

**At that moment, his demon’s body annihilated by the stroke of Krsna’s cakra, he achieved union with the Absolute Truth.**

**Комментарий:**

Along with uttering Krsnas names, such as Pundarikaksa, Sisupala also directly noticed Krsnas faultlessly beautiful lotus-petal eyes and His other uniquely exquisite features. The attractive power of Krsnas names and bodily beauty burned up Sisupala\`s hatred and the accumulated sinfulness that his hatred had caused. At the final moment, as his demonic body was killed by the sharp edge of Krsnas Sudarsana disc, he could realize Krsna as the Supreme Truth. Endowed then with pure love for Krsna, Sisupala attained the sayujya of entering into his eternal intimate relation with Him.

Here is the evidence that Krsna is the svayam-rupa, the original Supreme Personality of Godhead. He alone manifests to the fullest extent the power to attract fallen souls back to His loving service.

### Text 65

*ity uktvapy atra baky-ader*  
*moksam apy arbha-lilaya*  
*amoksam kalanemy-ader*  
*anyatrapisa-cestaya*  
*munih smrtva punah prakhyad*  
*ayam hi bhagavan iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti — thus; uktva — speaking; api — also; atra — in this context; baki-adeh— of the sister of Baka (Putana) and others; moksam — the liberation; api — also; arbha-lilaya — as His childhood pastimes; amoksam — not liberating; kalanemi-adeh— of others like Kalanemi; anyatra — in other (incarnations); api — and; isa-cestaya — as His pastimes in the role of the Supreme Lord; munih — the sage (Parasara); smrtva — recollecting; punah — again; prakhyat— spoke; ayam — He; hi— indeed; bhagavan — the Personality of Godhead; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**Reaching this point in his narration, the sage Parasara recalled how Krsna awarded liberation to Putana and others during His early childhood pastimes, and how He withheld liberation from persons like Kalanemi when He dispatched them during His pastimes as the powerful Supreme Lord in other forms. Thinking thus, the sage spoke the words beginning “ayam hi bhagavan,” “Certainly He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” sText 49\]**

**Комментарий:**

To answer Maitreya\`s inquiry, Parasara cited evidence to show that Krsna alone exhibits the potency of attraction that results in liberation for an enemy who meets death at His hands. This evidence included the negative examples of Hiranyakasipu and Ravana, and the positive example of Sisupala. Parasara concludes that Krsna is the svayam-rupa, the original Godhead. Krsna liberated many demons even in his infancy, beginning with Bakasura\`s sister Putana, but His other incarnations did not liberate the demons They killed, as for example when Lord Ajita killed Kalanemi.

**Комментарий:**

Putana disguised herself as a beautiful gopi so she could approach Krsna and offer to nurse Him. When she arrived, Yasoda and the other simple cowherd women did not stop her. At that time baby Krsna was lying in a crib under the axle (aksa) of a cart. Because He seemed reborn (punar-jata) after the attack of this poison-bearing witch, the village women gave Him the name Adhoksaja. Adhoksaja, of course, is one of Krsnas eternal names, and, for other reasons, one of Lord Narayana\`s names as well.

Srila Sridhara Svami wrote a commentary on Srimad-Bhagavatam before the time of Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Lord Caitanya accepted his authority as impeccable, and His followers often respectfully referred to him simply as “the commentator” (tika-kara).

Indra rules the demigods who control the forces of nature in this universe, but the name Indra, “the chief,” better suits Krsna, who rules the kama-dhenus, the mystical cows of Goloka, who supply Krsnas devotees whatever they desire.

*tasmat trayanam evayam*

Of the three para-avastha avataras of God - Nrsimha, Ramacandra, and Krsna - Krsna exhibits the energies of the Supreme most completely. Only He has the compassion and attractive power to give spiritual perfection to His enemies. Lord Nrsimha and Lord Ramacandra are, like Krsna, Personalities of Godhead, but They do not exhibit His unique sakti.

Srila Rupa Gosvami was not the first to point out that among all the forms of God only Krsna awards liberation to demons. Rupa's older brother Sanatana Gosvami presented the same conclusion in Sri Brhad-bhagavatamrta (1.5.15-21). That Krsna is the supreme form of Godhead is also confirmed elsewhere in Brhad-bhagavatamrta (2.4.185-87) and in Caitanya-caritamrta (Adi 2.8 and 104-115).

## Text 86 (b)

*sarve nityah sasvatas ca*

*naiva prakrti-jah kvacit*  
*paramananda-sandoha*  
*jnana-matras ca sarvatah*

*sarva-dosa-vivarjitah iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

maha-varahe — in the Maha-varaha Purana; sarve — all; nityah — eternal; sasvatah — unchanging; ca — and; dehah— bodies; tasya — of Him; para-atmanah — the Supreme Soul; hana — of loss; upadana — and increase; rahitah— devoid; na — not; eva — indeed; prakrti-jah — born from material nature; kvacit — at any time; parama-ananda — with supreme bliss; sandohah— full; jnana-matrah — fully aware; ca — and; sarvatah — in all situations; sarve — all; sarva-gunaih — in transcendental qualities; purnah — complete; sarva — all; dosa — of faults; vivarjitah— devoid; iti — thus.

The Gopala-tapani Upanisad (Purva 19) tells us that the Supreme Lord Krsna chooses to expand Himself into many forms: eko ’pi san bahudha yo ’vibhati. “Although one, He appears as many.” The Vedas also establish that in all conditions the Supreme Lord is always complete and perfect. He never becomes incomplete, nor does He splinter into fragments like a stone.

The Mahd-vardha Purana is here cited as evidence that in all His expanded forms the Supreme is complete. All the incarnations of God are eternal, but They periodically appear and disappear in the material realm. They are called “His bodies” even though in essence They are nondifferent from Him. It is an accepted practice in the philosophical use of Sanskrit to employ the possessive case even when there is no real distinction between possessor and possessed. For example, one may say caitanyam atmanah svarupam, “Pure consciousness is identical to the self”

Thus because all the expanded forms of God are identical with the original, none of them ever undergo increase or loss.

### Text 87

*atrocyate paresatvat*  
*purna yady api te \`khilah*  
*tathapy akhila-saktinam*  
*prakatyam tatra no bhavet*

**Пословный перевод:**

atra — in answer to this; ucyate — it is said; para-isatvat — because of being the Supreme Lord; purnah — complete; yadi api —although; te — they; akhilah — all; tatha api — nonetheless; akhila — of all; saktinam — potencies; prakatyam — exhibition; tatra — in them; na u — not; bhavet— may be.

**Перевод:**

**Our response to this question is that although all these forms are complete because of their being the Supreme Lord, they do not completely exhibit His potencies.**

**Комментарий:**

The expanded forms of God, both Vilasa and svamsa, are all as complete as the svayam-rupa. These expansions, however, do not exhibit all His potencies completely. The scriptural statements describing all these forms of God as eternal and perfect are augmented by other statements attesting to the difference between amsi and amsas. For example, ete camsa-kalah pumsah: “These incarnations are plenary and partial expansions, amsas and kalas, of the Purusa” (Bhagavatam 1.3.28)

The objectors argument establishes that each form of Godhead possesses all the perfections of His essential identity. The counter-argument establishes that some of His forms reveal more of these perfections than others. These arguments do not contradict one another, but overemphasis on the first obscures the truth of the second.

### Text 88

*amsatvam nama saktinam*  
*sadalpamsa-prakasita*  
*purnatvam ca svecchayaiva*  
*nana-sakti-prakasita*

**Пословный перевод:**

amsatvam — the status of a partial expansion; nama — namely; saktinam — of His potencies; sada — always; alpa-amsa — in small part; prakasita— exhibition; purnatvam — completeness; ca — and; sva-icchaya — by His sweet will; eva — only; nana — of many; sakti — potencies; prakasita — exhibition.

**Перевод:**

**An expanded form of the Lord is called an amsa when it always exhibits only a small part of His potencies; by contrast, a form is called purna, “complete,” when by His sweet will it exhibits the full range of His potencies.**

**Комментарий:**

Someone might again object, “If the Supreme\`s vilasa and svamsa expansions possess all the qualities of the svayam-rupa, then at some time or other all of these qualities will be manifest. This will cancel out the difference between amsi and amsas.” To counter this argument, this verse clarifies the definition of the term amsa. The implication is that the amsas of the svayam-rupa Krsna are His tad-ekatma-rupa expansions, both vilasa and svamsa. When Sri Krsna assumes the identities and moods of Narayana and other expansions, He exhibits not all of His qualities but only appropriate ones, which the scriptures have described. This fact upholds the conclusion of differentiation between amsi and amsas. Sri Nrsimha and the Lords other expansions do not display Krsnas qualities of enchanting His enemies and granting liberation to those He kills.

To propose that all the Supreme\`s self-same expansions exhibit every one of His powers, one must disregard scriptural authority. If Lord Narayana exhibited all of Krsnas qualities, Srimad-Bhagavatam would not describe how Narayana’s consorts long for the dust of Krsnas feet. If Raghupati Rama manifested the same qualities as Krsna, the Padma Purana would not inform us about the sages who, despite seeing Lord Ramacandra in person, prayed for Krsnas association. If the three Purusas showed the same quali- ties as Krsna, the Brahma-samhita would not depict Them as Krsnas amsas.

Various scriptures describe how Lord Sankarsana honors Lord Vasudeva as the source of His existence and the object of His reverence. We also learn from the scriptures that Lord Ramacandra\`s brothers considered Him their master and served Him with humble devotion. These descriptions would be senseless if there were no hierarchy among the expansions of the Lord.

The amsas are always subordinate to the amsi. Thus Lord Balarama, even though Krsnas elder brother, thinks Himself Krsnas servant and speaks accordingly:

*kim etad adbhutam iva*  
*vasudeve \`khilatmani*  
*vrajasya satmanas tokesv*  
*apurvam prema vardhate*  
*keyam va kuta ayata*  
*daivi va nary utasuri*  
*prayo mayastu me bhartur*  
*nanya me \`pi vimohini*

**“What is this wonderful phenomenon? The affection of all the inhabitants of Vraja, including Me, toward these boys and calves is increasing as never before, just like our affection for Lord Krsna, the Supersoul of all living entities. Who is this mystic power and where has she come from? Is she a demigod or a demoness? Who can bewilder Me other than the illusory energy of My master, Lord Krsna?” (Bhagavatam 10.13.36-37)**

Complete exhibition of all perfections is the essential characteristic of the amsi, who, by His sweet will, unfolds the unlimited aspects of His personality. Krsna also partially expands His personality into the amsas, but none of Them expands into Him. He is not an emanation of anyone else.

### Text 92

**Пословный перевод:**

**In a similar way, according to how extensively the Lord reveals His qualities and powers, devotees and others are freed from material entanglement and become happy.**

**Комментарий:**

One can attain the highest happiness only from the complete manifestation of Truth, not from partial manifestations, although They may be His plenary expansions. We can understand this by comparing the power of a small lamp\`s flame with that of a large fire. Both the flame and the large fire can set a city ablaze, but only the large fire can provide enough heat to warm a person suffering from cold. Similarly, although amsas such as Nrsimha are equally as powerful as the amsi Krsna when it conies to annihilating Their demonic antagonists and eradicating Their devotees' ignorance, only Krsna, the “large fire,” always manifests the unique powers of liberating those He kills and filling His devotees with bliss. Lord Nrsimha and other amsas give the materialistic demons They kill great opportunities for material enjoyment, but They do not deliver them from material existence. As fully as the Supreme Lord reveals His personal potencies in any incarnation, to that extent His devotees and the mystic yogis derive pleasure from hearing about His exploits.

### Text 98

*tathapi dosah parame*  
*naivaharyah kathancana*  
*guna viruddha apy ete*  
*samaharyah samantatah*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

**“Nonetheless, no one should ever ascribe any faults to the transcendental Lord. All kinds of contradictory qualities like these are completely reconciled in Him.”**

**Комментарий:**

After hearing that the Personality of Godhead is the Supreme Absolute Truth, full of knowledge and bliss, one might presume that He is without qualities such as largeness and minuteness. But the revealed scriptures describe Him as both large and small and claim that He possesses these qualities as aspects of His eternal self. The Vedas glorify Him as the gigantic Purusa with thousands of heads, as Trivikrama, who spanned the universe with three steps, and also as the minute witness in the hearts of the atomic living beings.

One might propose that as pure spirit He should not have any color, but the scriptures say meghabham vaidyutambaram: “He has the complexion of a rain cloud and wears a yellow garment.” (Gopala-tapani Upanisad 1.10) And also sa mam rsabho lohitaksah: “That most eminent person has reddish eyes.” The resolution is that Krsnas colors are purely spiritual.

Since we find so many contradictory qualities in the Supreme Lord, one might ask whether He is also noneternal as well as eternal, and imperfect as well as perfect. No. According to the Kurma Purana, undesirable qualities such as birth, change, decay, and death are never present in Him.

### Text 99

*sri-sastha-skandhe ca mitho-viruddhacintya-saktitvam yatha gadyesu,*  
*duravabodha ivayam tava vihara-yogo yad asarano sarira idam*  
*anaveksitasmat-samavaya atmanaivavikriyamanena sa-gunam agunah*  
*srjasi harasi pasi.*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sastha-skandhe— in the Sixth Canto; ca — and; mithah — mutually; viruddha — contrary; acintya — inconceivable; saktitvam — possessing qualities; yatha — as; gadyesu — in prose texts; duravabodhah — difficult to understand; iva — quite; ayam — this; tava — Your; vihara-yogah — engagement in pastimes (of material creation, maintenance, and annihilation); yat — since; asaranah— not dependent on any other support; asarirah — without a material body; idam — this; anaveksita — without waiting; asmat — of us; samavayah— for the cooperation; atmana — by Your own self; eva — only; avikriya-manena— without being transformed; sa-gunam — the manifestation of the material modes of nature; agunah — although transcendental to such material qualities; srjasi — You create; harasi — You annihilate; pasi — You maintain.

**Перевод:**

**Prose statements in the Sixth Canto s6.9.34-37\] describe His possessing inconceivable, mutually contradictory qualities: “O Lord, You need no support, and although You have no material body, You do not need cooperation from us. Since You are the cause of the cosmic manifestation and You supply its material ingredients without being transformed, You create, maintain, and annihilate this cosmic manifestation by Yourself. Nevertheless, although You appear to be engaged in material activity, You are transcendental to all material qualities. Consequently these transcendental activities of Yours are extremely difficult to understand.**

**Комментарий:**

Terrified of Vrtrasura, the demigods offered these prayers to Lord Visnu for protection. They told Him they could not understand His playful connection (vihara-yoga) with the material creation. He seemed impossible to comprehend. Those who have been blessed with insight into His mysterious potencies can understand Him, but those who acquire knowledge only through direct perception and logic cannot.

Because the modes of nature cannot touch the Personality of Godhead, He has no material body or support, He takes no help from anyone, and He performs no activity that generates reactions. Simply on His own He creates this world with all its varieties by mixing the modes of nature (sattva, rajas, and tamas).

Usually only a person with material qualities can create something material. A potter, for example, has a body made by the three modes and needs the support of the earth as a place to stand. To manufacture the products of his trade he must take help not only from his stock of clay but from his potters wheel, modeling stick, and other tools. By contrast, the Supreme Lord enacts His pastime of creating the universe in a different and mysterious way. He manifests the three modes, the material elements, and the living beings and thus evolves from Himself the entire cosmos. Yet even while effecting this drastic transformation of His energies, He maintains His absolute, unchangeable position. Simply by His limitless free will His transcendental potencies undergo the changes necessary for creation.

### Text 100

*atha tatra bhavan kim devadatta-vad iha guna-visarga-patitah*

*atmarama upasama-silah samanjasa-darsana udasta iti ha vava na*  
*vidamah.*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha —and furthermore; tatra — in that regard; bhavan — Your Lordship; kim — whether; deva-datta-vat—like “Devadatta,” an ordinary human being; iha — in this material world; guna-visarga-patitah — fallen into a material body impelled by the modes of material nature; paratantryena — by dependence on the external conditions (of time, space, activity, and nature); sva-krta— executed by oneself; kusala— auspicious; akusalam— inauspicious; phalam — results of action; upadadati— accepts; aho svit — or else; atma-aramah — completely self-satisfied; upasama-silah — self-controlled in nature; samanjasa-darsanah — having equal vision; udaste—remains neutral (as the witness); iti — thus; ha vava — certainly; na vidamah — we do not understand.

**Перевод:**

**“These are our inquiries. The ordinary conditioned soul is subject to the material laws, and he thus receives the fruits of his actions. Does Your Lordship, like an ordinary human being, exist within this material world in a body produced by the material modes? Do You enjoy or suffer the good or bad results of actions under the influence of time, past work, and so forth? Or, on the contrary, are You present here only as a neutral witness who is self-sufficient, free from all material desires, and always full of spiritual potency? We certainly cannot understand Your actual position.**

**Комментарий:**

The demigods mentioned that Lord Visnu maintains the cosmic manifestation. His maintenance is also inconceivable, as they are now describing.

An ordinary person (the “Devadatta” of numerous examples in textbooks of Vedic logic) builds a house and cultivates a field for himself. He resides in a district populated by friends, enemies, and indifferent parties, where he enjoys and suffers the fruits of his lawful and illegal activities. Is Lord Visnu just another such person? Has He fallen under the influence of the material modes when He participates in the wars between the demigods and demons? Has He lost His independence when He appears to be partial and shows compassion for the demigods? Does He also enjoy and suffer the results of auspicious and inauspicious acts? Does He accrue reactions for His work? Or does He remain always impartial and undiminished in His potency, a neutral and self-satisfied witness taking no part in the happiness and misery of this world? The demigods cannot determine the truth of the matter.

**Пословный перевод:**

na — not; hi — certainly; virodhah — contradiction; ubhayam — both; bhagavati — in the Supreme Personality of Godhead; apariganita — immeasurable; guna-gane — whose transcendental attributes; isvare— in the supreme controller; anavagdhya — unfathomable; mahatmye— whose glories; arvacina— recent; vikalpa — of equivocal calculations; vitarka— opposing arguments; vicara — and judgments; pramana-abhasa— of the imperfect evidence; kutarka — containing faulty logic; sastra — by texts; kalila — agitated; antah-karana — of whose minds; asraya — whose shelter; duravagraha — wicked obstinacies; vadinam— of those who propose; vivada— of controversies; anavasare— who is not within the range; uparata — withdrawn; samasta — from whom all; maya-maye — manifestations of the illusory energy; kevale — who is without a second; eva — indeed; atma-mayam— the illusory energy; antardhaya — causing to disappear; kah — what; nu — indeed; arthah — feat; durghatah— impossible to accomplish; iva — as it were; bhavati — is there; svarupa-dvaya— two different natures; abhavat — due to there not being; sama — proper; visama— or mistaken; matinam— of those whose opinions; matam — the conclusions; anusarasi — You follow; yatha— just as; rajju-khandah — a piece of rope; sarpa-adi — as a snake and so on; dhiyam — of those who perceive.

**Перевод:**

**“O Supreme Personality of Godhead, all contradictions can be reconciled in You. Î Lord, since You are the Supreme Person, the reservoir of immeasurable spiritual qualities, and the supreme controller, Your unlimited glories are inconceivable to the conditioned souls. Many argue about right and wrong without knowing the truth. Their arguments are false and their judgments inconclusive. They have no authorized means by which to gain knowledge of You. Because their minds are agitated by scriptures containing ambiguous conclusions, they are unable to understand the truth concerning You. Furthermore, because of polluted ambition to present the right conclusion, their theories are incapable of revealing You, who are transcendental to their material conceptions.**

**“You are one without a second, and therefore apparent contradictions in You, such as doing and not doing and being one and being many, are not contradictory. Your potency is so great that You can do and undo anything, as You like. With the help of that potency, what is impossible for You? Since there is no duality in Your constitutional position, You can do everything by the influence of Your energy.**

**“A rope may frighten a bewildered person who considers it a snake, but it will not frighten a person who correctly perceives it as only a rope. Similarly, You, as the Supersoul in everyone’s heart, inspire fear or fearlessness according to one’s intelligence, but in You there is no duality.”**

**Комментарий:**

If the Personality of Godhead is a silent witness and protector of everyone, then why in many instances does He take sides to curb the influence of demonic persons? From the mundane viewpoint this behavior seems contradictory, but we can reconcile everything by taking into account His acintya-sakti. Through this divine sakti He can create (producing everything from His own substance), subdue evildoers, and protect the pious, all while remaining impartial and satisfied within Himself. The limitations of ordinary persons should not be applied to the Supreme Lord, whose infinite glories are beyond comprehension.

To reconcile the apparent contradictions, the demigods use several adjectives to describe the Lord: bhagavati - He eternally possesses the six praiseworthy assets, beginning with sovereign authority; apariganita-guna- gane - He has innumerable good qualities, such as always fulfilling His intentions and always looking after the welfare of His devotees; isvare - He rules over all living beings; anavagahya-mahatmye - His glories perplex those who lack devotion.

Because whatever He wills automatically comes to pass, He does not have to exert Himself even in the formidable project of creating universes. Out of concern for His devotees, He understandably puts down those who are inimical to them. As the supreme ruler, He wields the rod of punishment over unruly elements. The word bhagavati indicates that He is the eternal master of Laksmi, the source of all opulence, and thus He always remains detached, free of all material aspirations. He creates and maintains this world for the benefit of others, not for Himself.

Lord Visnu might ask the demigods, “But why do learned scholars avoid acknowledging these facts about Me?”

In reply, the demigods describe such scholars as arvacina, unqualified to approach essential truth. They use guesswork and hypothetical logic, citing scriptures of questionable authority to support their opinions. Because such scholars are always in the embrace of illusion, their minds remain asleep on the bed of ignorance. Proudly arguing among one another, they can never understand the Supreme Person. These philosophers use speculative methods such as vikalpa, weighing alternatives (“Is it this way or that?”); vitarka, indecision (“What is actually going on here?”); and vicara, presumption (“It must be like this”). All these are considered dubious methods of reasoning, pramanabhasa.

Lord Visnu might then object, “But I have a deluding power, maya, that enchants people. This maya conjures these contradictory appearances, but they have no reality.”

The demigods reply with the statement: uparata-samasta-maya-maye, “You are above indulging in any kind of illusion.”

The Supreme Lords energies are real, not illusory, and everything they produce is real. The sruti authority (Isopanisad 8) confirms this: yathathyato rthan vyadadhat. “The products of His creation are factual.” No delusion of cosmic hallucination plays within Him; rather, He displays the real creative force of His atma-maya. The Sabda-mahodadhi dictionary identifies this atma-maya with His own personal desire (atma-maya tad-iccha syat). There is nothing that this atma-maya cannot do on His behalf.

Lord Visnu may object, “But my dear demigods, are you suggesting that I have two different identities, one derived from the mode of goodness (santodita), and the other eternal and unchanging (nityodita)?” The demigods answer, “No, You have only one identity, but You are understood differently by different observers. To those who can see Your personal qualities You are known as the Personality of Godhead, and to those who cannot see them You are known as one without a second.” As Badarayana Vyasa, the author of the Vedanta-sutras, states: gati-samanyat. “The various conceptions derive equally from Him.” (VS 1.1.10) Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana, recognized as the foremost Gaudiya Vaisnava commentator on Vedanta, takes this sutra as evidence that the Supreme Truth is one, not many, because it confirms that all the different ideas about Him presented in the Upanisads are equivalent to one another. Even Narada, as he was approaching from a distance, was perceived by Krsna in different ways:

*cayas tvisam ity avadharitam*  
*pura tatah saririti vibhavitakrtim*  
*vibhur vibhaktavayavam puman iti*  
*kramad amum narada ity avabodhi sah*

**“The all-powerful one first saw a brilliant mass of light. He then discerned that some embodied person approached. Gradually He began to distinguish the persons bodily features, and finally He saw that Narada had arrived.” (Sisupala-vadha 13)**

As the sage of the demigods was seen differently from various distances, so the one Absolute is seen differently from the viewpoints of jnana and bhakti. Through jnana He is seen as the formless One, and through bhakti as the Supreme Person, but there is no duality in the transcendental reality.

Lord Visnu may challenge, “But if the various conceptions derive equally from Me, why do people put forward so many conflicting theories about what I am?”

The devas respond, “All these theories actually come from You. Just as in the dark a rope might cause people think of a snake, a stick, a stream of water, or a necklace, so You cause faithless persons to imagine You in various ways.” The Supreme Lord inspires those who cannot see Him to devise various hypotheses about Him, some more and some less accurate. In His own words,

*bhavanti bhava bhutanam*  
*matta eva prthag-vidhah*

**“All the different conceptions of the living beings come from Me alone.” (Bhagavad-gita 10.5)**

**Комментарий:**

That the energies of the Supreme are inconceivable can be known by deduction (as indicated in the previous verse), and also by the evidence of authoritative scripture, sabda-pramana.

A sutra of Vedanta (2.1.27) answers the following question: “In this world performers of activities, like potters and carpenters, are subject to such imperfections as bodily transformation and distress. If the Supreme is also such a performer, isn’t He subject to the same imperfections?” This sutra rejects this idea with the word srutes, “because of what the revealed scripture tells us.” The implication is that even while engaged in all kinds of activities the Supreme Soul remains unchanged and untouched by imperfection.

The Svetasvatara Upanisad makes the following two statements, one closely following the other (6.16 and 19): sa visva-krd visva-vid atma-yonih. “He is the producer of the universe and the knower of the universe, but He is His own source.” And niskalam niskriyam santam niravadyam niranjanam. “He has no parts and no activity. He is at peace, irreproachable, and faultless.” It may be asked why scriptures contradict themselves like this. The reply is that these are not actually contradictions but rather inconceivable truths. Sabda-mulatvat: inconceivable truths can be understood only through the authority of transcendental sound. This declaration is further confirmed by smrti scriptures and by the occurrence of inconceivable potencies in gems, mantras, and medicinal herbs. Since even familiar objects of this world have acintya-sakti, how can we deny the Supreme His inconceivable powers?

**We find similar contradictory language in the Third Canto s3.4.16\]: “My Lord, even the most learned sages in the world become disturbed in their intelligence when they see that Your Greatness engages in fruitive work although You are free from all desires, that You take birth although You are unborn, that You flee out of fear of the enemy and take shelter in a fort although You are the controller of invincible time, and that You enjoy householder life surrounded by many women although You enjoy in Your Self.”**

**Having thus discussed this side issue we now return to elucidating the main topic.**

The main course of discussion up to text 92 was establishing Krsna as the original form of God. Text 93 began a secondary discussion of His incorporating contradictory qualities such as being one and being many. Now the author resumes giving evidence that Krsna is the svayam-rupa.

The prakrti-svami, master of material nature, is the first Purusa, who lies on the Causal Ocean. The antar-yami, or Supersoul of the universe, is the second Purusa resting on the Garbha Ocean. In texts 120 through 140 the purva-paksa, or opposing view, will be presented, arguing that Krsna is inferior to both Karanodaka-sayi Visnu and Garbhodaka-sayi Visnu.

**Комментарий:**

This verse glorifies Karanodaka-sayi Visnu. In the beginning of creation, before the appearance of anyone else, the Lord of the spiritual sky manifested this form of the Purusa for the purpose of creating the worlds from the mahat and the other elements of matter. All sixteen primary material elements existed first in Him.

**Комментарий:**

This and the next three verses, cited from Srimad-Bhagavatam (1.3.2-5), describe the second Purusa. Assuming this form, the Lord of the spiritual sky lies down within the egglike shell of each universe on the “Fetal Ocean,” or Garbhodaka. He is the expansion of Lord Narayana called Pradyumna.

### Text 123

*yasyavayava-samsthanaih*  
*kalpito loka-vistarah*  
*tad vai bhagavato rupam*  
*visuddham sattvam urjitam*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya — whose; avayava — of the limbs; samsthanaih— by the configurations; kalpitah — is imagined; loka — of planets and their inhabitants; vistarah— the expansion; tat — that; vai — indeed; bhagavatah— of the Personality of Godhead; rupam — a form; visuddham — pure; sattvam — existence; urjitam — excellent.

**Перевод:**

**“It is believed that all the universal planetary systems are situated on the extensive body of the Purusa, but He has nothing to do with the created material ingredients. His body is eternally in spiritual existence par excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

The various material planetary systems expand from Garbhodaka-sayi Visnu and then assume their proper places, arranging themselves to resemble the limbs of His body, Thus it is stated, patalam etasya hi pada-mulam (Bhagavatam 2.1.26), “Patala-loka constitutes the soles of His feet,” and so on.

However, the scriptures describe these worlds as the Purusa's limbs only to help purify the minds of materialistic persons. In truth the Supreme Lords transcendental body is always pure, untouched by matter. It is composed of suddha-sattva, the self-manifested living substance of the spiritual realm. Therefore the Purusas actual body eludes all of Maya's influence.

It is a critical mistake to assume that the suddha-sattva composing Lord Visnu's body is simply the sattva of the material creation unmixed with the lower modes of rajas and tamas. Actually, we never find the material sattva completely unmixed with the other modes, as we hear from the Pancaratra agama:

*anyonya-mithunah sarve*  
*sarve sarvatra-gaminah*

**“Each of the modes is always in intimate combination with the others. Each can always be found everywhere.”**

**Комментарий:**

Materialistic thinkers have their various conceptions of the Supreme, but those with refined intelligence free from misconceptions meditate on the expansive form of the Purusa. Adabhra-caksusa, “with unrestricted eyes,” means with the vision of spiritual knowledge. The description of Lord Garbhodaka-sayi having “thousands” of hands and heads indicates that He has these limbs in infinite number. This is also implied by such scriptural statements as:

**“His eyes, mouths, arms, and feet are everywhere.” (Svetasvatara Upanisad 3.3 and Maha-narayana Upanisad 2.2)**

His amsa is Brahma, and Brahma's amsas are his sons, the Prajapatis headed by Marici, who send forth within the creation the eternal jivas’ temporary identities as demigods, human beings, and animals.

The word bhuta has many different meanings, as we see in its definition in the Medini dictionary:

### Text 142

*vasudeva-grhe saksad*  
*bhagavan purusah parah*  
*janisyate tat-priyartham*  
*sambhavantu sura-striyah*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

vasudeva-grhe — in the house of Vasudeva; saksat — personally; bhagavan — the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has full potency; purusah — the original person; parah — transcendental; janisyate — will appear; tat-priya- artham — for His satisfaction; sambhavantu — should take birth; sura- striyah — the wives of the demigods; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**“The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, who has full potency, will personally appear as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore all the wives of the demigods should also appear in order to satisfy Him.”**

**Комментарий:**

The purva-paksas idea that the Lord of the Milk Ocean appeared as Krsna in response to the demigods prayer must have been conceived in haste because it fails to recognize the clear meaning of the Bhagavatam's text. Brahma spoke this verse to the demigods, repeating what he had heard from Ksirodaka-sayi Visnu through mental communication. We know this from the preceding statement:

*giram samadhau gagane samiritam*  
*nisamya vedhas tridasan uvaca ha*  
*gam paurusim me srnutamarah punar*  
*vidhiyatam asu tathaiva ḍṁ ciram*

**“While in trance, Lord Brahma heard the words of Lord Visnu vibrating in the sky. Thus he told the demigods: Î demigods, hear from me the order of the Supreme Person, and execute it attentively without delay.” (Bhagavatam 10.1.21)**

Brahma is relaying Ksirodaka-sayi Visnu’s message to the demigods:

“Not I but the Purusa will take birth in Vasudeva's house.”

“Do you mean Garbhodaka-sayi Visnu?”

“No, the Supreme Purusa.”

“Then do you mean Karanodaka-sayi Visnu?”

“No, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

“Oh, you mean the Lord of Vaikuntha?”

“No, the original Supreme Personality.”

In other words, the person who will appear in Vasudeva's house is saksad bhagavan, whose status as God is not dependent on anyone else. A similar status is expressed by the words svayam-dasas tapasvinah, “Great ascetics are their own servants.”

The demigods’ wives who are members of Lord Vamana’s entourage should descend to the earth for the Lord’s pleasure, to become the maidservants of His beloved consorts.

Indeed, Lord Narayana is Your expansion, and He is called Narayana because He is the generating source of the primeval water of the universe. He is real, not a product of Your illusory Ṅṁóa.” sBhagavatam 10.14.14\]**

**Комментарий:**

In this verse Lord Brahma tells Krsna that he realizes that Karanodaka-sayi Visnu and Garbhodaka-sayi Visnu are His amsas.

Just before this, Brahma had said:

*jagat-trayantodadhi-samplavode*  
*narayanasyodara-nabhi-nalat*  
*vinirgato ’jas tv iti van na vai mrsa*  
*kintv Isvara tvan na vinirgato 'smi*

**“My dear Lord, it is said that when the three planetary systems are merged into the water at the time of dissolution, Lord Narayana lies down on the water, gradually a lotus flower grows from His navel, and Brahma takes birth upon that lotus flower. Certainly, these words are not false. Thus am I not born from You?” (Bhagavatam 10.14.13)**

In effect Brahma is saying, “Dear Lord, You are my father, Narayana. 'Therefore, please excuse my offenses.”

However, having just seen Krsna’s unequaled power, Brahma now understands that Krsna is not only His father, Garbhodaka-sayi Visnu; He is something more. Afraid of committing further offense, he carefully qualifies this connection by addressing Krsna as adhisa, the ultimate Lord. The Garbhodaka-sayi Visnus who serve as Supersouls of each universe are Supreme Lords, and Brahmas father is one of Them. But Krsna is superior to Them.

Krsna gives life and the power to act not only to all embodied beings who inhabit every universe, but also to the inhabitants of Vaikuntha, including Garuda, Visvaksena, and all the other eternally liberated souls. He is the direct witness of every realm of existence, material and spiritual. He is Maha-narayana, greater than all other Personalities of Godhead, and the first and second Purusas are His partial expansions. It is thus neither myth nor poetic exaggeration but eternal truth that Krsna is Narayana, the Purusa who creates this universe.

Krsna can still be expected to excuse Brahma, because He is indeed Brahmas father, even if a few generations removed.

It is a symptom of ignorance to think that the boundless opulence of the Supreme Person is limited to the finite quadrant of material creation.

### Text 158

*kim va yah kalayamsena*  
*syat sita-syama-kesakah*

**Пословный перевод:**

kim va — or else; yah — who; kalaya — “as a partial expansion”; amsena — as an amsa; syat — is; sita-syama— white and black; kesakah — having hair; sah — He; eva — indeed; atra — here; avatirnah — descended; abhut— has become; sri-lila-purusa-uttamah — the Supreme Personality who enjoys pastimes.

**Перевод:**

**Or an alternative explanation: That same Lord who has white and black hair in His partial expansion, has now descended as Sri Lila-purusottama.**

**Комментарий:**

“But,” the purva-paksi persists, “you have not shed light on the Mahabharata's description of Lord Visnu creating Krsna and Balarama from His black and white hairs.”

Here is the explanation: The Hari mentioned in the verses from Mahabharata is Ksirodaka-sayi Visnu, who, according to Srimad-Bhagavatam (Canto Two, chapter seven), appears as a kala, an expansion of an expansion of the svayam-rupa Lord. The svayam-rupa whose kala is Ksirodaka-sayi Visnu appears on the earth as Krsna and exhibits His incomparable pastimes.

“But how do you explain the statement that Lord Visnu pulled out two of His hairs, which entered women of the Yadu dynasty?” asks the purva-paksi.

There is a simple explanation: In this context the word kesa can be understood in its less common sense as “ray of light.” The Mahabharata also supports this idea in the Narayaniya section, where Krsna tells Arjuna,

*amsavo ye prakasante*  
*mama te kesa-samjitah*  
*sarva-jnah kesavam tasmat*  
*mam ahur muni-sattamah*

**“The rays of effulgence that emanate from Me are called kesas, and for this reason I am called Kesava by the all-knowing best of sages.” (Mahabharata, Santi-parva 328.43).**

The purva-paksa is thus finally revealed as a mistaken interpretation when we understand what Lord Brahma says in the Second Canto: two rays of Ksirodaka-sayi Visnu, one white and one black, entered into Balarama and Krsna while They were present in Their mothers wombs.

The Mahabharata consistently uses the word kesa in the sense of “ray.” Two examples are its description of Krsna-Balarama's descent, and its account of Narada Munis seeing multicolored rays of light entering the two Lords. And Srimad-Bhagavatam (3.2.15) states unequivocally, using the phrase mahad-amsa-yuktah, that Krsna’s Purusa amsas enter Him when He comes down to this world:

*sva-santa-rupesv itaraih sva-rupair*  
*abhyardyamanesv anukampitatma*  
*paravareso mahad-amsa-yukto*  
*hy ajo 'pi jato bhagavan yathagnih*

**“The Personality of Godhead, the all-compassionate controller of both the spiritual and material creations, is unborn, but when His peaceful devotees are abused by antagonists, He takes birth just like fire, accompanied by His mighty amsas.”**

For all his good intentions, this Vaisnava is less than one hundred percent straightforward in his attitude toward Krsna, disrespecting Him by offering faint praise.

### Text 182

*sri-dasame caivam evoktam,*

*nese mahi tv avasitum manasantarena*  
*saksat tavaiva kim utatma-sukhanubhuteh*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-dasame — in the Tenth Canto; ca — and; evam — thus; eva — indeed; uktam — said; asya — of this; api — even; deva — called Deva (Vasudeva); vapusah — of one whose body; mat-anugrahasya — which has shown mercy to me; sva-iccha-mayasya — which appears in response to the desires of Your pure devotees; na — not; tu — on the other hand; bhuta- mayasya — which comprises the created beings; kah — Brahma; api — even; na ise — I am not able; mahi — the greatness; tu — but; avasitum — to estimate; manasa — with my mind; antarena — which is controlled and withdrawn; saksat — directly; tava — Your; eva — indeed; kim uta — what to speak of; atma-sukha — of the happiness of impersonal realization; anubhuteh — the experience; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**There is also this statement in the Tenth Canto s10.14.2\], “My dear Lord who have shown great mercy to me, You appear just to fulfill the desires of Your pure devotees, not to contain the conditioned souls. Although I directly see You, with my mind completely withdrawn from material affairs, I cannot understand the greatness of Your form as Krsna, which is greater than the form of Vasudeva. Then what to speak of the extent to which realizing You is superior to the happiness of impersonal self-realization?”**

**Комментарий:**

This is more evidence from Srimad-Bhagavatam of Krsna’s superiority to Vasudeva. Brahma has come down to the earth and seen with his own eyes the original Personality of Godhead in the role of the young son of the king of the cowherds. He has seen that Krsna is greater than even Lord Vasudeva, who holds the title Deva, Supreme Lord. He asserts that even with his strictly disciplined mind he cannot understand Krsna’s glories.

He then mentions Krsna’s great compassion for him. According to Sri Gopala-tapani Upanisad, Krsna very kindly gave Brahma His own eighteen-syllable mantra, and by chanting this mantra Brahma was empowered to create the universe. Krsna showed kindness to Brahma again recently when He revealed His amazing mystic power by expanding Himself into duplicates of all the cowherd boys and calves.

Brahma also states that Krsna appears by sveccha, the desire of His devotees. He comes to this world when and how His devotees want Him to.

### Text 189

*sveccha-mayasya bhaktanam*  
*kamayakhila-karmanah*  
*na tu bhuta-mayasyeti*  
*purusatvam ca khanditam*  
*yad esa sarva-jivanam*  
*purusah paramasrayah*

**Пословный перевод:**

*sva-iccha-mayasya —* “which appears by the desire of Your own”; *bhaktanam* — of the devotees; *kamaya*— for fulfilling the desires; *akhila* — all; *karmanah*— activities; *na* — not; *tu* — rather; *bhuta-mayasya*— “which comprises the created beings”; *iti* — thus; *purusatvam* — being the Purusa; *ca* — and; *khanditam* — refuted; *yat* — since; *esah* — He; *sarva* — of all; *jivanam*— finite souls; *purusah* — the Purusa; *parama* — supreme; *asrayah —* the shelter.

**Перевод:**

**“Which appears by the desire of Your own” means that all His activities are performed to fulfill the desires of His devotees. “Whose body does not contain the conditioned souls,” defeats the idea that He is the Purusa, since the Purusa is the supreme shelter of all conditioned jivas.**

**Комментарий:**

In Brahma’s prayer the word *bhuta* refers to the living entities who take birth in the material world. The *Medini-kosa* states, *bhutam ksmadau pisacadau jantau klibam: “Bhuta* can mean ‘earth and the other elements,’ ‘Pisacas and other ghostly spirits,’ or any ‘creature.’ In these definitions the word has a neuter gender.”

Brahma refers to the Purusa resting on the Causal Ocean as *bhuta-maya* because the *jivas* who have fallen into material existence repose in His body prior to the creation and are maintained by His potencies during their active life in this world. Krsna delegates to His *amsa* the pastime of supervising the creation, so that Krsna Himself can remain uninvolved.

### Text 190

*antarena niruddhena*  
*manasety ekatanata*  
*jnatum syan mahima sakyo*  
*yady apy ebhir visesanaih*  
*jnatum tathapi nese smity*  
*acintyaisvaryatodita*

**Пословный перевод:**

*antarena* — “turned inward”; *niruddhena* — subdued; *manasa* — “with a mind”; *iti* — thus; *ekatanata* — single-pointedness; *jnatum* — to understand; *syat*— is; *mahima* — the greatness; *sakyah* — possible; *yadi api* — although; *ebhih* — by these; *visesanaih* — qualifiers; *jnatum* — to understand; *tatha api* — nonetheless; *na ise*— “I am not able”; *asmi* — am I; *iti* — thus; *acintya* — inconceivable; *aisvaryata* — possession of powers; *udita* — stated.

**Перевод:**

**“Even with my mind subdued and completely withdrawn from material affairs” indicates exclusive concentration. Although it is possible to know something of His greatness by these qualifications, Brahma nonetheless says, “I am not able to know it.” In this way Brahma implies that Krsna possesses inconceivable powers.**

**Комментарий:**

Brahmas wisdom is not only book knowledge. He is a great master of self-control. He can keenly focus his mind for understanding any subject, as this *karika* expresses with the word *ekatanata* (“one-pointedness”). According to the *Amara-kosa*, *ekatano ‘nanya-vrttih:* “*Ekatana* means ‘exclusively engaged without deviation.”' One might think, therefore, that Brahma’s mind should be fit for understanding Krsna’s glories, but Brahma says that he cannot comprehend them. Thus Brahma recognizes Krsna’s glories to be *acintya* - beyond the mind’s grasp.

### Text 193

*kramadi-dipikayam ca*  
*vasv-aksara-manor vidhau*  
*gokulesavrtitvena*  
*vasudevadayo matah*  
*iti vasudevadi-bhrama-nirasah.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*krama-adi-dipikayam*— In the *Krama-dipika; ca* — and; *vasu-aksara*— which has eight syllables; *manoh*— for the *mantra; vidhau* — in the injunctions; *gokula-isa*— of the Lord of Gokula; *avrtitvena* — as the entourage; *vasudeva-adayah*— Vasudeva and the others; *matah* — considered; *iti —* thus; *vasudeva-adi* — about Vasudeva and so on; *bhrama —* of the misunderstandings; *nirasah* — the refutation.

**Комментарий:**

There are fourteen Manus in each day of Brahma, and eight Vasus among the principal demigods. Thus the words *manu* and *vasu* poetically represent the numbers fourteen and eight.

The *Pahcaratra agamas* are respected as authoritative scripture by Vaisnavas of the four orthodox *sampradayas.* The Vaisnavas of the Madhva-Gaudiya *sampradaya* also accept the authority of the *Krama-dipika* textbook on worship of Krsna, written by Kesava Bhatta of the Nimbarka *sampradaya.* Srila Rupa Gosvami reasons that we should not entertain a view that goes against the statements of these texts.

**Пословный перевод:**

*nanu* — but, it may be asked; *sraisthyam* — the superiority; *mukundasya* — of Mukunda; *brahmatah*— to Brahman*; yujyate*— is correct; *katham* — how; *yat* — since; *brahma* — of Brahman; *sri-bhagavatoh*— and the divine Personality of Godhead; *aikyam* — oneness; *eva* — indeed; *prasidhyate*—is an established fact.

How can someone hope to swim across an ocean if he cannot even cross a small lake? Similarly, how can someone accept Krsna as superior to Lord Narayana if he cannot even tolerate the impersonal Brahman as subordinate to Krsna.

The impersonalist presenting this *purva-paksa* argues that Brahman and Bhagavan are the same. How can someone correctly be called superior to himself?

*tatha* — thus; *ca* — and; *skande* — in the *Skanda Purana; bhagavan* — the Personality of Godhead; *parama-atma* — the Supersoul; *iti* — thus; *procyate* — is called; *asta-anga* — of the eightfold system; *yogibhih* — by the *yogis; brahma* — Brahman; *iti* — thus; *upanisad-nisthaih* — by the devotees of the *Upanisads; jnanam* — consciousness; *ca* — and; *jnana-yogibhih* — by the *jnana-yogis.*

**“Thus the Skanda Purana states: ‘Thṛ Personality of Godhead is called Supersoul by the yogis of the eightfold system, Brahman by the followers of the Upanisads, and consciousness by the jnana-yogis.”**

**Комментарий:**

Just as one might refer to the same object with the terms “pot,” “vessel,” and “container,” the *purva-paksi* reads this statement as indicating that the terms *brahman*, *paramatma*, and *bhagavan* refer to one and the same entity.

### Text 197

*sri-prathame ca,*  
*vadanti tat tattva-vidas*  
*tattvam yaj jnanam advayam*  
*brahmeti paramatmeti*  
*bhagavan iti sabdyate*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*sri-prathame* — in the First Canto; *ca* — and; *vadanti* — they call; *tat* — that; *tattva-vidah*— learned souls; *tattvam* — the Absolute Truth; *yat* — which; *jnanam* — consciousness; *advayam* — nondual; *brahma iti* — known as Brahman; *paramatma iti* — known as Paramatma; *bhagavan iti* — known as Bhagavan; *sabdyate*— is so termed; *iti* — thus.

**Перевод:**

**“And the First Canto s1.2.11\] states, ‘Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth call this nondual consciousness Brahman, Paramatma, or Bhagavan’’’**

**Комментарий:**

The impersonal students of *Vedanta* call the Supreme by the name Brahman, *yogis* call Him Paramatma, and devotees call Him Bhagavan.

The *purva-paksi* presents these two verses from the *Skanda* and *Bhagavata Puranas* to conclude his argument. One of them states that the Truth known as Bhagavan and so on is pure consciousness, and the other one states, conversely, that pure consciousness is Brahman, Paramatma, and Bhagavan. With this presentation he wants to establish the complete equivalence of consciousness with the Absolute Truth in His impersonal, localized, and fully personal features. He wants to rule out any differentiation in the Supreme.

### Text 198

*satyam uktam srnu tatas*  
*trtiye kapilam vacah*

**Пословный перевод:**

*satyam* — true; *uktam —* spoken; *srnu —* please hear; *tatah —* then; *trtiye —* in the Third Canto; *kapilam* — of Lord Kapila; *vacah* — the words.

**Перевод:**

**Yes, what you say is true, but now listen to Lord Kapila’s words in the Third Canto s3.32.33\]:**

**Комментарий:**

The first part of the response to the *purva-paksa* is that it is half correct. Brahman and Bhagavan are indeed different ways of looking at the same Truth.

Why then talk about degrees of superiority among these aspects? Because there are authoritative statements of scripture to that effect; for example Lord Kapila speaks the following in *Srimad-Bhagavatam.*

**Перевод:**

**“A single object is appreciated differently by different senses due to its having different qualities. Similarly, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is one, but according to different scriptural explanations He appears to be different”**

**Some karikas explaining this: The essential character of the Personality of Godhead has many facets, and thus He appears differently to various seekers of the Truth according to their individual methods of realization.**

**Перевод:**

**This phenomenon is similar to the way an object such as milk, which possesses qualities of form, taste, and so on, remains always one although perceived in various ways by the senses.**

**By the sense of sight one perceives milk as white, and by the sense of taste one perceives it as sweet. Similarly, although the Personality of Godhead is one, a person perceives Him in manifold forms by means of various methods of realization.**

### Text 203

**Пословный перевод:**

*jihvaya* — by the tongue; *eva —* only; *yatha* — as; *grahyam* — is perceivable; *madhuryam* — sweetness; *tasya* — of that (object); *na* — not; *aparaih*— by the other (senses); *yatha —* as; *ca —* and; *caksuh-adini*— the eyes and so on; *grhnanti* — perceive; *artham* — object; *nijam nijam* — each their own.

**Перевод:**

**One discerns sweetness by the tongue alone and none of the other senses. Each of the other senses, such as sight, has access to only its own appropriate object.**

### Text 204

*tathanya bahya-karana-*  
*sthaniyopasanakhila*  
*bhaktis tu cetah-sthaniya*  
*tat-tat-sarvartha-labhatah*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tatha —* similarly; *anya —* other; *bahya —* external; *karana —* in the senses; *sthaniya*— having its place; *upasana*— method of meditation; *akhila* — each; *bhaktih*— devotional service; *tu*— but; *cetah*— the mind; *sthaniya —* representing; *tat-tat* — various; *sarva —* all; *artha —* of objects; *labhatah* — because of receiving.

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, all other methods of meditation on the Supreme are like the external senses. Bhakti, however, is like the mind, which receives the sensory input of all the senses.**

**Комментарий:**

In ordinary experience we find that objects like milk possess various qualities perceivable by different senses. The same object evokes one perception in one sense and a different perception in another sense. Similarly, the Supreme Lord’s complex personality, although one, has many aspects. Spiritual disciplines taught in the *Vedas* enable one to approach Him in various ways. Thus those seekers of the Truth who cannot comprehend His personal qualities say that He has no qualities. This natural limitation of the impersonal viewpoint is similar to how the eyes are naturally limited to perceiving only the whiteness of milk but not its sweetness, and the tongue is limited to perceiving only its sweetness but not its whiteness.

The mind, however, is considered the ruler of all the senses. It can perceive all of milk’s qualities - color, taste, smell, and so on. Analogously, pure devotion has the power to reveal all the aspects of the Absolute Truth, including both His personal and impersonal features. Other *sadhanas* can deliver only various partial realizations.

### Text 205

*iti pravara-sastresu*  
*tasya brahma-svarupatah*  
*madhuryadi-gunadhikyat*  
*krsnasya sresthatocyate*

**Пословный перевод:**

*iti* — thus; *pravara* — the most venerable; *sastresu* — in the scriptures; *tasya* — His; *brahma* — of Brahman; *svarupatah*— than the identity; *madhurya-adi*— sweetness and so on; *guna —* of the qualities; *adhikyat —* because of the greater quantity; *krsnasya* — of Krsna; *sresthata* — superiority; *ucyate* — is stated.

**Перевод:**

**Thus the most venerable scriptures describe Krsna as superior to His own form of impersonal Brahman because He possesses sweetness and an abundance of other qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

Even though formless, undifferentiated Brahman is Krsna Himself and nothing other than Him, we must conclude that because Krsna’s personal feature possesses qualities He is superior to His qualityless impersonal feature. In Srila Baladeva’s commentary to text 101 of this chapter, he cited the verse beginning *cayas tvisam* to compare *bhakti* to other *sadhanas* in terms of how closely they approach the supreme goal. Now *bhakti* has been compared to other *sadhanas* in terms of how much of the supreme goal they reveal, using the analogy of the relative powers of the internal and external senses.

### Text 206

*tatha ca sri-dasame,*  
*tathapi bhuman mahimagunasya te*  
*viboddhum arhaty amalantar-atmabhih*  
*avikriyat svanubhavad arupato*  
*hy ananya-bodhyatmataya na canyatha*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tatha* — so; *ca* — and; *sri-dasame*—in the Tenth Canto; *tatha api* — nevertheless; *bhuman —* O limitless one; *mahima —* the greatness; *agunasya*— who has no material qualities; *te* — of You; *viboddhum* — to understand; *arhati* — one is able; *amala* — spotless; *antah-atmabhih*— with mind and senses; *avikriyat* — because of being unchanging; *sva- anubhavat* — because of having perception of one’s true Self; *arupatah* — because of being formless; *hi —* indeed; *ananya* — in no other way; *bodhya* — understandable; *atmataya*— because of being the Soul of everything; *na* — not; *ca* — and; *anyatha* — otherwise.

**Перевод:**

**The Tenth Canto thus states: “O limitless one, it is possible, however, to realize the glory of Your impersonal aspect simply by applying one’s purified mind in the practice of spiritual perception that transcends the scope of material activity and forms, and by focusing on one’s true Self. One can realize the impersonal Supreme only by employing these means and by understanding It as the Soul of everything, and not otherwise.**

**Комментарий:**

Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana explains in his commentary that this verse and the following one, from Brahma’s prayers to Krsna (*Bhagavatam* 10.14.6-7), further clarify Lord Kapila’s statement cited above. Brahma is saying to Krsna, “O limitless one, You have aspects with qualities and aspects without qualities *(aguna),* but it is easier to understand the greatness of Your qualityless Brahman aspect than to understand the qualities of your absolute personality.”

In this statement the phrase *viboddhum arhati* (“can understand” or “can be understood”) is a type of verbal expression midway between active and passive usage wherein the subject of the action is its own object. For example, in the statement “the rice is cooking,” rice is both the subject and the object of the action, cooking.

Why is it easier to understand the Supreme Lord’s impersonal feature? Because one must only apply the purified mind and perceive the real Self. But since perception is a mental function, requiring a change to the mind’s state, how can changeless Brahman become its object? Lord Brahma answers this with the word *avikriyat.* Realization of the impersonal Supreme is a special kind of perception in which nothing changes. Then again, only things that have form can become objects of the mind’s perception, but Brahman has no form. Therefore Lord Brahma uses the word *arupatah.* One in Brahman realization perceives formless Truth, much as the ordinary eye can perceive even colorless objects.

In conclusion, Lord Brahma says *ananya-bodhyatmataya:* “One can realize Brahman by the self-revealing nature of Brahman itself.” And he says *na canyatha:* “There is no other way to understand the impersonal Supreme.” In other words, when one’s mind is correctly disposed, Brahman reveals Itself. No practices or mental exercises can capture It.

### Text 207

*gunatmanas te ’pi gunan vimatum*  
*hitavatirnasya ka isire ‘sya*  
*kalena yair va vimitah su-kalpair*  
*bhu-pamsavah khe mihika dyu-bhasah*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

*guna-atmanah*— who is the possessor of all superior qualities; *te* — of You; *api* — and *gunan* — the qualities; *vimatum* — to count; *hita- avatirnasya* ***—*** who has descended for the benefit of all living entities; *ke* — who; *isire* — are able; *asya* — of the universe; *kalena* — in due course of time; *yaih* — by whom; *va* — or; *vimitah* — counted; *su-kalpaih* — who are great scientists; *bhu-pamsavah* — the atoms of an earthly planet; *khe—* in the sky; *mihikah* — the particles of snow; *dyu-bhasah* ***—*** the light rays of the stars and planets; *iti* — thus.

**Перевод:**

**“In time, learned philosophers or scientists might be able to count all the atoms of the earth, the particles of snow, or perhaps even the shining rays of the sun, the stars, and other luminaries. But among these learned men, who could possibly count the unlimited transcendental qualities possessed by You, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who have descended onto the surface of the earth for the benefit of all living entities?”**

**Комментарий:**

Just as it is far easier to look at the rays of the sun than to stare directly at the sun itself, so it is far easier to realize the Supreme as changeless, formless, pure consciousness than as the Supreme Person with His innumerable qualities.

*Sri Visnu Purana* (6.5.84) tells us, *ananta-kalyana-gunatmako ‘sau:* “He possesses unlimited auspicious qualities.” The Personality of Godhead has more transcendental qualities than anyone can ever count. Among His qualities, just to name a few general categories, are His omniscience, omnipotence, friendliness, and compassion, and His all-attractive beauty, charm, and youthful luster. Not even great demigods like Lord Siva and Lord Brahma can estimate the qualities of the Supreme Lord. He greatly benefits this world by appearing as His *avataras* to display those qualities.

*nanu —* but; *prakrta-rupatvat —* because of being material; *mrga-trsna* — to the mirages in the desert; *upama* — comparison; *jusam*— which merit; *gunanam —* of the qualities; *ganana —* the counting; *na syat —* cannot happen; *iti* — thus; *kah —* what; *atra —* in this regard; *vicitrata* — wonder.

**“But what is surprising about this? Because His form is material, like a mirage, there is no way to count His qualities.”**

**Комментарий:**

This is another attempt by the impersonal Brahma-vadi to deny the excellence of the Personality of Godhead. Assuming that the unique qualities of the Supreme cannot be real, he imagines that they must be superimposed on Brahman, like the blueness imposed on colorless ether.

One can disregard material qualities as imaginary, but an eternal entity like Krsna possesses only real qualities. Such spiritual qualities are nondifferent from the perfect spiritual being who possesses them. They belong to his *svarupa.*
