*atah* — thus; *krsnah* — Krsna; *aprakrtanam* — transcendental; *gunanam* — of qualities; *niyuta-ayutaih*— with countless millions; *visistah*— endowed; *ayam* — He; *maha-saktih* — possessing supreme potencies; *purna-ananda* — of perfect ecstasy; *ghana-akrtih* — the full embodiment.

### Text 216

*brahma nirdharmakam vastu*  
*nirvisesam amurtikam*  
*iti suryopamasyasya*  
*kathyate tat-prabhopamam*

**Пословный перевод:**

*brahma* — Brahman; *nirdharmakam* — lacking qualities; *vastu* — an entity; *nirvisesam* — undifferentiated; *amurtikam*— formless; *iti* — thus; *surya*— to the sun; *upamasya —* who is comparable; *asya —* of Him (Krsna); *kathyate —* is said to be; *tat—* His; *prabha —* to the effulgence; *upamam —* comparable.

**Перевод:**

**Brahman is an entity lacking qualities. It is undifferentiated and formless. If we compare Krsna to the sun, Brahman is like His effulgence.**

**Комментарий:**

Someone may object, “But we read in scripture that the *svarupa* of Brahman is pure consciousness. Does *Sri Hari-vamsa* not recount that when Arjuna and Krsna traveled outside the universe to retrieve the sons of a *brahmana*, Arjuna saw Brahman as pure light?”

Srila Rupa Gosvami replies to this objection by specifying the nature of Brahman. Brahman is *nirdharmaka,* without perceivable qualities like taste and color. Unlike matter, it is *nirvisesa,* not separated into distinct elements like earth and water. And it is *amurtika,* formless. As such, the relationship of Brahman to the original Supreme resembles the relationship of sunrays to the sun.

As from a distance one might see sage Narada as a mass of light, in general everyone sees the sun as a fiery globe. Only a few of the sun’s worshipers see him as a god mounted on a wonderful chariot. Those who are motivated by the pursuit of knowledge are like ordinary people observing the sun: they see the Supreme Soul as a mass of pure consciousness. But those who strive for pure devotion are like the few successful sun worshipers, for they realize the personal form behind the mass of pure consciousness.

Brahman and Bhagavan are certainly not two separate realities, but the Bhagavan conception is far superior to that of Brahman because through His personality the Supreme reveals His all-attractive sweetness and other qualities. Krsna consciousness is undoubtedly more complete than Brahman consciousness.

### Text 217

*tatha ca sri-gitasu,*  
*yo mam avyabhicarena*  
*bhakti-yogena sevate*  
*sa gunan samatityaitan*  
*brahma-bhuyaya kalpate*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tatha —thus; ca* — and; *sri-gitasu* — in *Sri Bhagavad-gita; yah* — who; *mam* — unto Me; *avyabhicarena* — without fail; *bhakti-yogena* — by devotional service; *sevate* — renders service; *sah* — he; *gunan* — the modes of material nature; *samatitya* — transcending; *etan* — all these; *brahma- bhuyaya*— for elevation to the Brahman platform; *kalpate* — is fit.

**Перевод:**

**As Sri Krsna states in Bhagavad-gita: “One who engages in full devotional service to Me, unfailing in all circumstances, at once transcends the modes of material nature and thus comes to the level of Brahman.”**

**Комментарий:**

This and the following verse appear as verses 26 and 27 in chapter 14 of *Sri Bhagavad-gita.*

Texts 200-204 above compared the relationship between Brahman realization and Bhagavan realization to the relationship between perception by the senses and perception by the mind. Just as the mind amalgamates the partial input of each sense into a complete image of perception, so *bhakti-yoga* includes Brahman realization and all other partial ways of understanding.

In this verse and the next Sri Krsna explains that one who faithfully worships Him earns promotion to the level of Brahman. Although impersonal ists may presume that this Brahman status is undifferentiated oneness with the formless infinity of divine light, the *Vedas* and Krsna Himself have a different idea. They consider it the state of becoming qualitatively one with the Supreme. *Niranjanah paramam samyam upaiti:* “One who has washed off all contamination attains complete equality swith the Supreme\].” *(Mundaka Upanisad* 3.1.3)

Achieving the Brahman status does not include loss of one’s individual identity.

*paramatmatmanor yogah*  
*paramartha itisyate*  
*mithyaitad anya-dravyam hi*  
*naity anya-dravyatam yatah*

**“Some may take the union of soul and Supersoul literally, but their understanding is wrong. After all, one distinct thing never changes into another, separate thing”  (Visnu Purana 2.14.27)**

The infinitesimal soul can never attain the identity of the infinite Supreme Soul.

**Пословный перевод:**

*brahmanah* — of the impersonal *brahma-jyotir; hi —* certainly; *pratistha —* the basis; *aham* — I; *amrtasya* — which is immortal; *avyayasya* — imperishable; *ca* — and; *sasvatasya* — which is eternal; *ca* — and; *dharmasya* — the constitutional position; *sukhasya —* of happiness; *aikantikasya* — ultimate; *ca* — also; *iti* — thus.

How can devotion to the son of Vasudeva lead to the state of equality with Brahman?

This is possible because Krsna is the foundation and ultimate shelter of the eternally perfect Brahman. Moreover, Krsna is the source of the soul’s eternal occupation, *bhakti-yoga*, and of the most sublime happiness of serving Him in pure love.

On the strength of having practiced *bhakti-yoga* without deviation, a devotee of the Supreme Lord attains the pure nature of Brahman existence. Then, situated in transcendence, the devotee can proceed to take shelter of Krsna in His *lila-vigraha.* One thus progresses from the level of Brahman to pure love of God.

### Text 220

*bhakter avyabhicarayah*  
*prema-sevaiva yat phalam*  
*kevalam brahma-bhavas tu*  
*vidvesenapi labhyate*

**Пословный перевод:**

*bhakteh*— of devotion; *avyabhicarayah*— undeviating; *prema-seva*— service in pure love; *eva —* indeed; *yat —* which; *phalam —* the fruit; *kevalam —* mere; *brahma-bhavah —* Brahman realization; *tu* — but; *vidvesena*— by hatred; *api —* even; *labhyate —* is obtained.

**Перевод:**

**The fruit of undeviating bhakti is elevation to service in pure love. On the other hand, one can obtain mere Brahman realization even by hating the Lord.**

**Комментарий:**

“But when the particle of pure spirit merges back into the totality of spirit, isn’t that his ultimate perfection? How can the soul emerge out of that happy perfection to again engage in an external activity like serving Krsna?”

This doubt arises from the failure to accept the superiority of *krsna-bhakti* over the *mukti* of merging into Brahman, which even enemies killed by Krsna obtain. *Bhakti-yoga* gives far greater benefits than mere merging into the impersonal existence of Brahman.

According to *Sri Brahmanda Purana:*

*siddha-lokas tu tamasah-*  
*pare yatra vasanti hi*  
*siddha brahma-sukhe magna*  
*daityas ca harina hatah*

**“Siddhaloka lies beyond material darkness. Accomplished mystics live there, absorbed in the bliss of the Supreme, and demons killed by Lord Hari also reside there”**

Siddhaloka, also called Brahmaloka, is the place where one experiences the formless mass of spiritual radiance called *brahma-jyotir.* It is beyond the realm of darkness, outside the eighth covering shell of the universe, the shell of *prakrti.* Although this *brahma-jyotir* is nothing but the effulgence of the Supreme Person’s transcendental form, those who don’t know this think that it is just formless light, as in the example of Narada looking like a mass of light from a distance.

Sincere seekers of the truth who meditate on this impersonal Brahman,

but who do not know of the nectar found at the Supreme Lord’s feet, find relief from all material designations, gaining residence in the *brahma-jyotir.* Demons killed by Sri Krsna are also given this favor. Those who disrespect the Lord’s feet, however, lose every trace of knowledge they have and fall again into darkness. The demigods who prayed to Krsna while He stayed in Devaki’s womb maintain:

*ye \`nye \`ravindaksa vimukta-maninas*  
*tvayy asta-bhavad avisuddha-buddhayah*  
*aruhya krcchrena param padam tatah*  
*patanty adho ‘nadrta-yusmad-anghrayah*

**“O lotus-eyed Lord, although nondevotees who accept severe austerities and penances to achieve the highest position may think themselves liberated, their intelligence is impure. They fall down from their position of imagined superiority because they have no regard for Your lotus feet.”** ***(Bhagavatam*** **10.2.32)**

### Text 221

*nanu te yadavasyasya*

*ity aha brahmano hiti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*nanu* — but, it may be asked; *te* — of You; *yadavasya*— the descendant of Yadu; *asya* ***—*** the same; *bhajanat* ***—*** by worshiping; *brahmata* ***—*** Brahman realization; *katham* ***—*** how; *iti* — in answer to this; *aha* ***—*** is said; *brahmanah* ***—*** of the impersonal Supreme; *hi* — certainly; *iti* — thus; *hi* — “indeed”; *yatah* — because; *aham* — I; *purah*— in front; *tava* — of you; *sthitah* — standing; *ayam* — the same; *vividha* — of manifold varieties; *ananda-purna*— full of ecstasy; *cit-ghana* — of concentrated spirit; *vigrahah* ***—*** the embodiment; *brahmanah* ***—*** of Brahman; *cit-svarupasya* ***—*** whose identity is purely spiritual; *pratistha* ***—*** the foundation; *parama- asrayah* — the ultimate shelter; *ravih* — the sun; *tejah-ghana*— of a concentrated mass of light; a*karah* ***—*** having the form; *kara-oghasya* — of its multitude of rays; *yatha* ***—*** as; *bhavet* ***—*** is.

**Перевод:**

**“But how can one achieve Brahman realization just by worshiping this chief of the Yadavas?”**

**Krsna answers, “Because I who stand before you am the basis of Brahman. Fully embodying all the manifold varieties of ecstasy, I am the foundation and ultimate shelter of Brahman’s pure spiritual identity, just as the sun, embodying concentrated light, is the source of a multitude of rays.”**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing Sri Krsna’s statement about liberation and devotion, Arjuna might question Him, “How can anyone become one with the Supreme by worshiping You?” Playing devil’s advocate, Arjuna might insinuate that Krsna, having taken birth in Devaki’s womb, is just a human being. Like any other fortunate son of a royal family, He is enjoying the results of His past good karma. Krsna unequivocally refutes this idea in the second of the two verses just cited, where He explains that He causes and maintains impersonal Brahman.

When Krsna takes birth from Devaki, by His sweet will the unchanging Absolute appears from a pure devotee, herself qualitatively one with the Absolute. As *Sri Visnu Purana* (5.2.7) says, *tvam para prakrtih suksma:* “You, Devaki, are of the sublime spiritual nature.” The birth of Krsna, the unchanging Absolute, is thus likened to the sun’s appearing from the eastern horizon.

Krsna says about Himself,

*ajo ‘ði sann avyayatma*  
*bhutanam isvaro ‘pi san*  
*prakrtim svam adhisthaya*  
*sambhavamy atma-mayaya*

**“Although I am unborn and My transcendental body never deteriorates, and although I am the Lord of all living entities, by My internal energy I still appear in every millennium in My original transcendental form” (*****Bhagavad-gita*** **4.6)**

The Supreme Lord does not take a new body as a king’s son might, having lost all His learning and other assets from His previous life. Krsna is eternal and unchanging, and therefore by worshiping Him one can at least achieve His impersonal aspect. This is no more surprising than it would be for a space vehicle approaching the sun to come in contact with its effulgence.

### Text 225

*atra karike,*  
*niskaladi-svarupam tad*  
*brahmandarbuda-kotisu*  
*vibhutibhir dharadyabhir*  
*bhinnam bhedam upagatam*  
*sada prabhava-yuktasya*  
*brahma yasya prabha bhavet*  
*tam govindam bhajamiti*  
*padyasyarthah sphuti-krtah*

**Пословный перевод:**

*atra —* in this regard; *karike* — two *karikas; niskala*— “having no parts”; *adi*— and so on; *svarupam* — whose essential nature; *tat* — that; *brahma- anda* — of universes; *arbuda* — millions; *kotisu*— and tens of millions; *vibhutibhih* — by the expansions; *dhara-adyabhih* — the earth and so on; *bhinnam* — “differentiated”; *bhedam* — difference; *upagatam* — having acquired; *sada* — always; *prabhava* — with power; *óuktasya* — who is endowed; *brahma* — Brahman; *yasya —* whose; *prabha —* effulgence; *bhavet —* is; *tam* — Him; *govindam* — Govinda; *bhajami* — I worship; *iti* — thus; *padyasya* — of the verse; *arthah* — the meaning; *sphuti-krtah* — clarified.

**Перевод:**

**Karikas explaining this:**

**That which is characterized as essentially without parts, and so on, becomes differentiated into varieties of opulent expansions, like earthly planets, in millions and billions of universes.**

**“I worship Govinda, always endowed with great power, of whom Brahman is the effulgence”**

**Such is the essential meaning of the verse.**

**Комментарий:**

The divine light of the *brahma-jyotir* is properly described as the amorphous radiance of Sri Krsna’s humanlike body, which is the concentrated source of all light. Brahman is conceived as formless, but it becomes differentiated with infinite varieties of form in countless universes. As the cause it is one, but its effects are unlimitedly many.

Someone may raise this doubt: “But we hear from *sruti* that the Supreme Lord Himself, not His effulgence, created the universe. The *Taittiriya Upanisad* (2.6) thus states, *so ‘kamayata bahu syam.* ‘He desired, “Let Me become many.””’

According to Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana, the verses of the *Brahma- samhita* resolve this doubt by indicating that the Supreme Lords effulgence serves as His creative agent. The *brahma-jyotir* agitates dormant *prakrti,*who then gives birth to the material universes.

The Kevaladvaita-vadis’ concept of Brahman as devoid of qualities, inexpressible in words, and one without a second is incompatible with the *Brahma-samhita's* description, which is altogether different from this conception. First of all, Brahman has qualities since it is a radiant emanation of the Supreme Person. Secondly, it is expressible since the Vedic scriptures describe it elaborately. And thirdly, it has “a second,” since the material creation arises from it.

The Kevaladvaita-vadis' version of Brahman is altogether untenable, with no support from any reliable means of acquiring knowledge. Empirical knowledge from the senses does not help in knowing their Brahman, which has no form or qualities to sense. Logic cannot discover it because it has no characteristics to serve as elements of premises. Verbal testimony of authority cannot prove this version of Brahman because as inexpressible truth it belongs to no categories and has no name. Metaphorical descriptions (*laksana*) cannot comprehend it because words cannot designate it, and so cannot refer to it even indirectly.

Nor can this Kevaladvaita version of Brahman be the cause of universal creation, because it lacks will, which must be exercised before any act of creation. Nor can it be the subject of spiritual instruction, since in this impersonal view of existence there is no real person to instruct, no real person to be instructed, and no real instructions to give.

The Kevaladvaita-vadis say, “All these apparent phenomena arise from delusion.” But this is also not feasible. Whose delusion would this be? Brahman’s? Or the individual soul’s? Neither case is possible. Perfect Brahman cannot become deluded. Nor can the *jiva* be deluded, because there was no *jiva* before the delusion started.

Thus, without much reflection, one can understand the flimsiness of the Kevaladvaita theory of Brahman.

### Text 226

*nanu bhos tava bhavo 'yam*  
*jnata eva maya dhruvam*  
*para-vyoma-pateh saurir*  
*avataras tvayocyate*

**Пословный перевод:**

*nanu* — but; *bhoh* — my dear friend; *tava* — your; *bhavah* — mood; *ayam* — this; *jnatah* — understood; *eva —* indeed; *maya —* by me; *dhruvam —* certainly; *para-vyoma* — of the spiritual sky; *pateh —* of the Lord; *saurih*— Krsna; *avatarah* — an incarnation; *tvaya* — by you; *ucyate* — is said to be.

**Перевод:**

**“But, dear friend,” someone else may say, “I do understand the idea behind what you say. You mean that Krsna is an incarnation of the Lord of the spiritual sky.**

**Комментарий:**

This *purva-paksa* is put forward by the Sri Vaisnavas, followers of the *sampradaya* established by Goddess Laksmi and directed in the modern age by the teachings of Acarya Ramanuja. In their opinion, the Supreme Soul assumes five kinds of forms - *para*, *vyuha*, *vibhava*, *antar-yami,* and *arca.* The *para* is the original Personality of Godhead, Narayana. His *vyuha* consists of His four expansions Vasudeva, Sankarsana, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha. His *vibhava* forms are Matsya, Kurma, and His other *avataras.* The *antar-yami* is the Supersoul in every living being’s heart, assuming the size of the living being’s thumb. And His *arca* is the Deity who appears for His devotees’ worship, like Sri Ranganatha and Jagannatha.

In the Sri Vaisnavas' view the personal forms of all the *vibhavas* are eternal, but three of Them are superior - Nrsimha, Raghunatha, and Krsna. Among the three, Krsna displays the opulences of God most completely, placing Him right after Lord Narayana in rank of importance.

This *purva-paksa* will continue up to text 299, after which Srila Rupa Gosvami will respond. The Sri Vaisnava spokesman begins by acknowledging the claim regarding Krsna's supremacy and proceeds to interpret it according to his own understanding.

*janma-adi*— of birth and so on; *lila* — pastimes; *prakatyat* — by being displayed; *avatarataya* — as an incarnation; *api* — and; *asau* — He; *proktah* — is described; *vilasah*— a *vilasa* expansion; *eva* — only; *syat* — is; *sarva —* all; *utkarsa —* with excellences; *ati-bhumatah* — because of being extremely full.

**“Krsna is generally called an avatara because He displays pastimes of birth and so on, but actually He is the direct expansion of Narayana, fully possessing all supreme excellences.**

**Комментарий:**

If Krsna is Narayana's expansion, is He just like Lord Matsya and Lord Kurma? “No,” says the Sri Vaisnava. “Although Krsna can be called an *avatara* because He performs the pastime of taking birth and does other things *avataras* do, factually He is Narayana Himself. Although He does not exhibit some of Narayana's unique excellences, He is greater than even Lord Nrsimha and Lord Ramacandra.”

### Text 229

*tatha hi sri-dvitiya-skandhe,*  
*tasmai sva-lokam bhagavan sabhajitah*  
*sandarsayam asa param na yat param*  
*vyapeta-sanklesa-vimoha-sadhvasam*  
*sva-drstavadbhih purusair abhistutam*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tatha hi —* thus; *sri-dvitiya-skandhe —* in the Second Canto; *tasmai —* to him; *sva-lokam* — His own planet or abode; *bhagavan* — the Personality of Godhead; *sabhajitah* — being pleased by the penance; *sandarsay m sa* — manifested; *param* — supreme; *na* — not; *yat* — to which; *param* — anything more supreme; *vyapeta* — devoid; *saEklesa* — of affliction; *vimoha —* illusion; *s dhvasam —* and fear; *sva-dscma-vadbhih —* who have perfectly realized the self; *purucaih* — by persons; *abhicmutam* — worshiped.

**Перевод:**

**“This incident is described in the Second Canto: ‘The Personality of Godhead, being thus very much satisfied with the penance of Lord Brahma, was pleased to reveal His personal abode, Vaikuṇṭha, the supreme region above all others. This transcendental abode of the Lord is freed from all kinds of miseries, illusion, and fear and is adored by all self-realized persons.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse and the subsequent five appear as verses 9-17 of chapter nine of the Second Canto of Sri*mad Bhagavatam.*

At the beginning of his life, before the creation, Brahma had no clue how to create the universe. At that time he heard a voice articulate the two syllables *ta-pa,* which he understood as guidance to practice serious spiritual discipline to gain the intelligence he needed for his work of creation. After he meditated carefully for one thousand celestial years, Lord Narayana showed His pleasure by allowing Brahma a vision of His personal abode, Vaikuṇṭha.

*Na yat param:* “There is no higher world” than Vaikuṇṭha, the kingdom of God. In that place there are no miseries, such as those caused by ignorance, egoism, attachment, hatred, and addictive obsessions. The residents of Vaikuṇṭha never fail in correct discrimination and have no fear of ever having to leave. It is populated by the exalted, self-realized persons who are its worshipers.

### Text 230

*pravartate yatra rajas tamas tayoh*  
*sattvaṁ ca miśraṁ na ca kāla-vikramah*  
*na yatra māyā kim utāpare harer*

**Пословный перевод:**

*pravartate —* prevail; *yatra —* where; *rajas tamas —* the modes of passion and ignorance; *tayoh —* with both of them; *sattvam —* the mode of goodness; *ca* — and; *misram* — mixed; *na —* not; *ca —* and; *k la —* of time; *vikramah* — the influence; *na* — neither; *yatra —* where; *m y*  — the illusory, external energy; *kim uta* — what to speak of; *apare* — others; *harer* — of the Personality of Godhead; *anuvrata* — devotees; *yatra* — where; *sura —* by the demigods; *asura —* and the demons; *arcitah —* worshiped.

**“In the spiritual world there is neither the mode of passion nor the mode of ignorance, nor any mixture of the two. Only the pure devotees of the Lord, who are worshiped by both demigods and demons, reside in the spiritual world as the Lord’s associates.**

**Комментарий:**

In Vaikuṇṭha the modes of matter are absent, including goodness, which is always mixed with passion and ignorance. There is also no influence of time and no illusion created by M y . Certainly, therefore, the elements that expanded from M y - the *mahat,* false ego, and so on - are also absent. Without time and illusion, the Vaikuṇṭha world is perpetually illumined by perfect bliss, and all its inhabitants are auspicious, cultured, and gentle.

*śyāma*— sky-bluish; *avadātāḥ*— glowing;  *śata-patra* — like a lotus flower; *locanāḥ* — whose eyes; *piśaṅga*— yellowish; *vastrāḥ*— whose clothing; *su-rucaḥ* — greatly attractive; *su-peśasaḥ* — youthful; *sarve* — all of them; *catuḥ* — four; *bāhavaḥ —* having hands; *unmicat* —with rising luster; maṇi — of pearls; *praveka* — with superior quality; *niska-ābharaṇāḥ* — wearing ornamental medallions; *su-varcasaḥ* — very effulgent; *pravāla* — of coral; *vaidkrya —* a special diamond; *mṛṇāla* — and celestial lotuses; *varcasaḥ* — whose radiance; *parisphurat —* gleaming; *kuṇdala —* with earrings; *mauli* — headdresses; *mālinaḥ* — and garlands.

**Перевод:**

**“‘The inhabitants of the Vaikuṇṭha planets have radiant, sky-blue complexions, and their eyes resemble lotus flowers. Their dress is a yellowish color, and their bodily features are very attractive. Just the age of growing youths, they are effulgent, endowed with four hands, and nicely decorated with pearl-studded ornamental medallions. They wear earrings, headdresses, and garlands. Some Vaikuṇṭha residents have effulgent complexions resembling coral, vaidkrya, and celestial lotuses.**

**Комментарий:**

*Su-peśasaḥ* means “endowed with the gentleness of youth.” *Mani-praveka* means “the best of jewels,” which the Vaikuṇṭha wear mounted on medallions (*nickas*) that adorn their chests and on other ornaments. Each of those who worship a form of Lord Narayana that has a complexion other than blue has a body of the same color as the form he worships.

In this analogy, the sky represents the blue *s ris* worn by many of the Vaikuṇṭha women.

Sri Laksmi’s expanded opulences attend her as maidservants and paraphernalia, yet with all the powers of control and enjoyment at her disposal she constantly attends to the service of her husband.

## Text 234 (c)

*adhyarhaṇīyāsanam āsthitaṁ paraṁ*

*sva eva dhāman ramamānām īśvaram*  
*iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*adhyarhaniya —* greatly worshipable; *asanam —* on His throne; *asthitam —* seated; *param* — the Supreme; *vrtam* — surrounded; *ctuh —* by the four *(prakiti*, *puruca, mahat,* and ego); *sodasa —* the sixteen; *panca —* and the five; *saktibhih* — energies; *yuktam —* endowed; *bhagaih* — with His opulences; *svaih* — personal; *itaratra* — in other persons; *ca* — and; *adhruvaih* — temporary; *sve* — in His own; *eva* — indeed; *dhaman* — abode; *ramamanam* — enjoying; *isvaram* — the Supreme Lord; *iti* — thus.

**Перевод:**

**Комментарий:**

Lord Narayana’s four energies are named Hl dini, Kirti, KaruG , and Tucmi. His sixteen energies (mentioned also in text 129 of this chapter) are Sri, Bhk, Kirti, Il , Lil , K nti, Vidy , Vimal , UtkarciGi, Jṣ n , Kriy , Yog , Prahvi, Saty , \*s n , and Anugrah . And His five energies are S Ekhya, Yoga, Vair gya, Tapas, and Bhakti. These potencies surrounded Narayana’s throne. The special opulences of the Supreme Lord are Dharma, Jṣ na, Aisvarya, and Vair gya; only He possesses these in full. The portions of Lord Narayana’s energies found in Brahm , other demigods, and ordinary mortals are impermanent reflections of the originals.

“Your transcendental form, a manifestation of pure goodness, is undisturbed by change, shining with knowledge, and devoid of passion and ignorance.” *(Bhagavatam* 10.27.4) The *visuddha-sattva* of Vaikuṇṭha cannot be a type of matter; otherwise Sukadeva Gosvami would not specifically say *na yatra m y :* “There is no material nature in Vaikuṇṭha”

VaicGava theologians explain *visuddha-sattva* in various ways. For example, some describe it as a self-manifesting, conscious, nonmaterial substance. Others describe it as a manifestation of the threefold tr

### Text 238

*srih sampad-rupini mūrtā*  
*yatra padmāṁśa-sambhava*  
*mānaṁ sevāṁ racayati*  
*vividhābhir vibhūtibhiḥ*  
*kusumākāra-śabdena*  
*ṛtūnām adhipo mataḥ*  
*tena tasyānugair grīśma-*  
*varśādyair ṛtubhis ca ya*  
*viśeṣād gīyamānāpi*  
*priya-karmaiva gāyati*  
*satrantena padenātra*  
*tinantā lakṣitā kriyā*

**Пословный перевод:**

*srih* — the goddess of fortune; *sampat-rupini* — who embodies opulence; *murta* — in person; *yatra* — where; *padm*  — of Padm (Laksmi); *amsa* — as a partial expansion; *sambhav*  — manifested; *manam* — “honor”; *sevam* — service; *racayati* — carries out; *vividhabhih* — with various; *vibhktibhih* — opulences; *kusuma- kara-sabdena* — by the word “spring”; *stknam* — of the seasons; *adhipah* — the ruler; *matah* — is understood; *tena —* with Him; *tasyah* — her; *anugaih* — with the followers; *gricma-varc*  — with the summer and rainy time;  *dyaih* — and so on; *stubhih* — the seasons; *ca* — and; *ya—* who; *visecat* — in a special way; *giyaman*  — being sung; *api* — although; *priya —* of her beloved; *karma —* about the activities; *eva* — indeed; *gayati* —“singing”; *sats-antena* — which has the present participle suffix; *padena* — by the word; *atra* — here; *tin-anta* — a form with a regular tense suffix; *lakcit*  — is implied; *kriy*  — verb.

**Перевод:**

**“Personally present there is Goddess Sri, a partial expansion of Padm embodying all opulence. With her various potent expansions she honors the Lord by serving Him. The word kusum kara is understood to refer to the leader of the seasons, personified spring. He is present with his followers - summer, the monsoon, and the other seasons – singing of Goddess Sri in a special way. She, however, sings of her beloved’s activities. Although her ‘singing’ is expressed as a present participle, the action of a regular verb is implied.**

**Комментарий:**

In the verse under discussion, the second clause, beginning *preEkh srit y* , has no regular verb, only three present participles: *preEkh srit* (“sitting on a swing”), *giyaman*  (“being sung about”), and *gayati* (“singing”). Each of them can serve as an adjective to describe Goddess Sri, but one of them must serve as the verb of the clause. Srila Rkpa here describes *gayati,* “she sings,” as the verb, expressing the main action of the clause.

*tatha ca* — and also; *bhargava-tantre* — in the *Bhargava-tantra; sakti-saktimatoh —* of the energy and the possessor of energy; *ca* — and; *api* — and; *na* — no; *vibhedah* — difference; *kathancana* — in any way; *avibhinna*  — nondifferent; *api* — although; *sva-iccha*  — His own desire; *adi* — and so on; *sabdaih* — by the terms; *api* — also; *vibhacyate*— is described; *iti* — thus.

**Перевод:**

**“Also, the Bhargava-tantra states, ‘There is never any difference between the energy and the possessor of the energy. But even though the Lord’s energy is not different from Him, she is described as if she were different, with terms such as sva-icch , “His own desire.’”**

**Комментарий:**

Someone who thinks that the Supreme has no individual body might object to the expression “Lord Haris *dhama*” on the grounds that *dhama* means “personal form.” According to the *Medini* dictionary, *dhama dehe gshe rasmau: “dhama* means ‘body,’ ‘house,’ or ‘ray.’” We can answer this objection by citing the *Bhargava-tantra*’*s* hint about the simultaneous difference and nondifference of the Personality of Godhead and His potencies.

Goddess Sri is the Lord’s *hladini-sakti*, His pleasure potency. Since she is nondifferent from Him, it is appropriate to think of her as His *dhama,* not only in the sense of His “radiance” but also in the sense of His “body.” By the transcendental principle of *viseca,* acknowledging variety in the changeless Supreme, the *sakti* that is identical with *saktim n* can also be said to be “His own.”

**Комментарий:**

In the opinion of some, the three lords Brahma, Visnu, and Siva are equal. They cite statements from smrti to support this opinion. For example, eko murtis trayo deva brahma-visnu-sivatmakah: “From the original singular form of the Supreme come the three gods Brahma, Visnu, and Siva.”

Someone with this view will question the wisdom of considering Visnu supreme. The purva-paksi explains that these Lords are avataras of the Garbhodaka-sayl Purusa, and that Visnu is greater than Rudra and Padmabhava Brahma. As proof of this he cites Bhrgu Munis testing each of the three deities, recorded in Srimad-Bhdgavatam (Canto Ten, chapter 89).

Visnu is superior among the three guna-avataras, and certainly the Purusas sGarbhodaka-sayl and Karanodaka-sayl\] are greater than He. Since Vasudeva of the catur-vyuha is the origin of the Purusas, He is superior to Them. And since this vyuha originates from the Lord of Maha-vaikuntha, He is supreme. The Vaisnava presenting this purva-paksa concludes, “Narayana of Maha-vaikuntha is the amsi from whom all forms of God originate. He is the svayam-rupa”

### Text 298

*sada-sivakhyo yah sambhuh*  
*sa caisanyavrtir mata*

**Пословный перевод:**

sada-siva-akhyah — named Sadasiva; yah — who; sambhuh — Sambhu; sah — he; ca — and; aisanya — in the northeast direction; avrtih — (member of) the surrounding entourage; mata — is considered.

**Перевод:**

**“The Sambhu called Sadasiva is also considered a member of Lord Narayana's entourage. He resides in the northeast.**

**Комментарий:**

A group of Saivites calling themselves the Maha-saivas refer to the Linga Purana as authority for their conviction about Lord Sadasiva. He is described there as the source of the many incarnations of Siva and the root cause of all existence: sada-sivah karana-karanam param tasmac ca sarve prabhavanti devah. “Sadasiva is the supreme cause of all causes. All gods arise from Him” Considering this, how can Narayana be called the svayam-rupa?

To answer this challenge, our purva-paksi cites the Padma Puranas unequivocal statement describing Sadasiva as a member of Lord Narayana s entourage. The original Sadasiva, mentioned in Sri Brahma-samhita, is Lord Narayana, a vilasa of Krsna, whereas the Sadasiva described in the Linga Purana is a subsequent expansion, an amsa of Narayana. This second Sadasiva is the one who has a place among the avaranas of Maha-narayana.

**“Therefore I contend that the original Lord Narayana and His expansion, Krsna, do not differ essentially from one another. After all, when one lamp is lit from another, the two are equally powerful.”**

**Комментарий:**

The purva-paksa concludes with these words. Having demonstrated Lord Narayanas glories, His worshiper makes a final statement about Krsnas essential equality with Narayana. His basic argument is that there is no evidence that Krsna is svayam bhagavan, whereas there is an abundance of evidence that Sri Narayanas divine personality is complete with all eternal transcendental perfections. Therefore, the subtle distinction of original and expansion must be recognized between the two. Sharing almost all the qualities of the Lord of Vaikuntha, Krsna is practically equal to Narayana, like a second lamp lit from the first. Still, the second lamp owes its existence to the first. Therefore, Krsna is a vilasa expansion of Lord Narayana.

Srila Rupa begins his reply to the purva-paksa. Maha-vadi indicates someone who has much to say but has not thought out his argument with perfect clarity. In this context, apesala means “not expert.”

But what evidence do we have to prove the supremacy of Krsna and service to Him? Srila Rupa answers this question in the next verse.

**Пословный перевод:**

Badarayana Veda-vyasa was dissatisfied even after editing the entire Vedic corpus and making his personal contributions, the Vedanta-sutras and the Mahabharata. He felt something wanting because he had not explicitly revealed the Personality of Godhead, His wonderful pastimes, and the methods of approaching Him through pure devotion. Only when Srila Vyasa compiled the Bhagavatam on the order of his guru, Narada, did the pain in his heart subside.

Srimad-Bhagavatam is the most reliable authority on the identity of the Supreme and on how to realize Him, and it is especially intended for the confused persons of the modern age.

### Text 302

*tatha hi sri-trtiye,*  
*svayam tv asamyatisayas try-adhisah*  
*svarajya-laksmyapta-samasta-kamah*  
*balim haradbhis cira-loka-palaih*  
*kirita-kotyedita-pada-pithah*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha hi — thus; sri-trtiye—in the Third Canto; svayam — Himself; tu — but; asamya — without equal; atisayah — or greater; tri-adhisah— the Lord of the three; svarajya — of independent supremacy; laksmya— by the opulence; apta — achieved by whom; samasta-kamah — all desires; balim — paraphernalia of worship; haradbhih— who are offering; cira-loka-palaih — by the eternal maintainers of the order of creation; kirita-kotya — by the millions of helmets; idita— honored by prayers; pada-pithah — whose shoes; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**There in the Third Canto s3.2.21\]; “Lord Sri Krsna has no equal or superior. He is the Lord of all kinds of threes. With His supreme and independent opulence He fulfills all His desires. He is worshiped by the long-lived rulers of the planets, who offer Him tribute by touching His shoes with their millions of helmets.”**

**Комментарий:**

To answer the narayana-bhaktas purva-paksa, Srila Rupa is going to demonstrate by two main arguments that Krsna is superior even to the husband of Goddess Sri. His first argument, given with the authority of the independent voice of sruti, is that Goddess Sri hankered to obtain Krsnas association. His second argument uses inference based on the evidence that Krsnas name is supremely potent.

Srila Rupa begins by citing this statement of Uddhavas from Srimad- Bhagavatam. The Bhagavatam is as authoritative as the srutisyand whatever Sri Uddhava says should be regarded as extremely reliable, because he is the best of learned scholars.

Krsna Himself said about him,

*noddhavo ‘nv api man-nyuno*  
*óad gun air narditah prabhuh*  
*ato mad-vayunam lokam*  
*grahayann iha listhatṝ*

**“Uddhava is not inferior to Me in any way, because he is never affected by the modes of material nature. Therefore he may remain in this world to disseminate specific knowledge of the Personality of Godhead.” (Bhagavatam 3.4.31)**

The words tu (“but”) and svayam (“Himself”) at the beginning of Uddhavas statement indicate that Krsna alone is supreme. Tu expresses exclusion, and svayam implies that Krsna has innate opulences that do not depend on anyone else. Because Krsnas position is unique and absolutely independent, no one can be greater than or equal to Him, including the Lord of Vaikuntha.

Krsna is the master of Gokula and His other two personal abodes, Mathura and Dvaraka, located in the highest region of the Vaikuntha sky. Uddhava calls Krsnas personal opulence svarajya, which means that He rules by means of His internal energy, or by His supreme and innate qualifications. Krsna thus gratifies His desires without restriction, enjoying wonderful tastes, fragrances, and other pleasures. His opulences are thus supreme and independent.

Uddhava mentions the cira-loka-palas, the rulers of distant universes, who come to Krsna bearing gifts of tribute, indicating their obedience to His rule. These are the Brahmas and other demigods who manage these other universes more expansive and opulent than our own. Who but the original Personality of Godhead would have the helmets of many Brahmas from far-off universes offered at His feet?

*ramo ‘py adhika-samyabhyam*

*tatra svayam-padabhavat*

**Пословный перевод:**

ramah — Lord Rama; api — also; adhika — of greater; samyabhyam — and equal; mukta — free; dhama — whose glories; iti — thus; avadi — said; yat — which; tatra — in that regard; svayam-pada — of the word “Himself”; abhavat — because of the absence; krsnena — with Krsna; aikyena — sameness; tasya — His; tat— that; nara-lila — human pastimes; adi — and so on; sadharmyat — due to sharing the similarities; prestham — favorite; rupam — form; tat — that; asya — His; yat — which.

Sharing similar personal qualities, They both have human pastimes. Ramacandra is a most favorite form of Krsna’s.**

**Комментарий:**

In the Ninth Canto of Srimad-Bhagavatam (9.11.20), Sukadeva Gosvami glorifies Sri Rama as follows:

*nedam yaso raghupateh sura-yacnayatta-*  
*lila-tanor adhika-samya-vimukta-dhamnah*

**“Assuming His transcendental form at the request of the demigods, killing Ravana with showers of arrows, and building a bridge over the ocean do not represent the actual glory of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Ramacandra, whose spiritual body always engages in various transcendental pastimes. Lord Ramacandras essential potency cannot be surpassed or even equaled, and therefore He is not in need of help from the monkeys to gain victory over Ravana.”**

This statement might seem to indicate that the son of Dasaratha is the svayam-rupa Supreme Godhead. Srila Rupa rejects this interpretation, however, on the grounds that Sukadeva has not used the word svayam in describing Lord Ramacandras supremacy.

Why, then, are Sri Rama's glories described as unexcelled and unequaled? Because Ramacandra is considered nondifferent from Krsna. They both behave like human beings and have very similar bodily appearances and personalities. Therefore Krsnas personal perfections are also found in Ramacandra. For this reason also Brahma addresses Sri Rama in Valmikis Ramayana as adi-karta svayam-prabhuh, “the first creator and original Supreme Lord.” (Yuddha-kanda 119.7)

svayam — Himself; tu — indeed; asamya — unequaled; atisayah — unexcelled; krsnah — Krsna; tu — indeed; bhagavan — the Supreme Personality of Godhead; svayam — Himself; iti — thus; asya — His; parama-aisvarya — of the supreme power; visesasya — specific; anuvarnane—in the description; padasya — of the word; svayam iti — “Himself”; asya — this; dvih— two times; uktih — the saying; bodhayati — indicates; asau — it; krsnasya — from Krsna; anya — of other; svarupa— forms; aikyat — because of the nondiffer- ence; adhikyam — superiority; na — not; iti — thus; sarvatha — in all ways.

**In the Bhagavatam’s specific descriptions of Krsna’s supremacy - “who has no equal or superior” and “but Lord Sri Krsna is the original Personality of Godhead” - the use of the word “svayam” in both verses indicates that Krsna’s exalted position is not due to His being identified with some other form of God.**

**Комментарий:**

The Bhagavatam drives home the conclusion that Krsna is the svayam-rupa by repeating the word svayam several times. This repetition accords with the standard methods of Mimamsa by which scriptural texts are interpreted. The repetition of a word is one of the conclusive signs of a compositions main idea.

*upakramopasamharav*  
*abhyaso purvata phalam*  
*arthavadopapatti ca*  
*lingam tatparya-nirnaye*

**“To distinguish the purport of a composition, one can look at the beginning and the end and check for repetition, novelty, an indicated consequence, glorification, and logical reasoning.” (Brhat-samhita)**

We find the word svayam used in reference to Krsna a number of times in Srimad-Bhagavatam. The First Canto (1.3.28) contains the famous words krsnas tu bhagavan svayam (cited in text 180). The 'third Canto (3.2.21) contains the verse beginning svayam tv asamyatisayah (cited in text 302). And the Ninth Canto (9.24.55) contains the verse beginning astamas tu tayor asit svayam eva harih kila. “'The eighth son sof Vasudeva and Devaki\] was the original Lord Hari Himself.”

Thus dvir uktih (“being mentioned twice”) here really means “being mentioned more than once.” The clear emphasis on Krsnas uniqueness precludes the possibility that scriptures refer to Krsna as svayam-rupa merely because He resembles Lord Narayana. Krsnas supremacy is altogether independent.

### Text 327

*yatah sri-kaurme,*  
*virodho vakyayor yatra*  
*napramanyam tad isyate*  
*yathaviruddhata ca syat*  
*tathdrthah kalpyate tayoh*  
*iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*yatah*— as; *sri-kaurme*— in *Sri Kurma Purdna; virodhah*— conflict; *vakyayoh* — of statements; *yatra* — where; *na* — not; *apramdnyam*— lack of authority; *tat* — that; *isyate* — should be considered; *yathd* — so that; *aviruddhata*— non-contradiction; *ca* — and; *syat*—there may be; *tathd*— thus; *arthah*— the meaning; *kalpyate* — should be interpreted; *tayoh* — of both; *iti* — thus.

**Перевод:**

**According to Sri Kurma Purana, “When two scriptural statements conflict, one should not assume that one or the other lacks authority. Rather, one should seek an elucidation that reconciles the two statements.”**

**Комментарий:**

In the *Brahmana* section of the *Vedas* we find two injunctions: one says that a certain fire sacrifice should be performed after sunrise, and the other says that the same sacrifice should be performed before sunrise. Since both injunctions are spoken by *sruti*, the authority of neither can be denied. Some way has to be found to reconcile them.

The apparently contradictory statements found in various *Purdnasy* which sometimes describe the universes as different and sometimes as similar, are all equally authoritative testimony from omniscient sages. The truth of both points of view needs to be respected.

Some Vaisnava scholars, even if they accept that these two contradictory descriptions can somehow be harmonized satisfactorily, might not accept that in some universes the Brahmas and other demigods live for many *maha-kalpas.* They might cite scriptures saying that when the worlds are annihilated at the end of each *maha-kalpa* all created beings are destroyed. Those who maintain this view will say that “long-lived” simply refers to the fantastic durations of the demigods’ lives and serves to highlight the Supreme Lords glories.

### Text 329

*tatha hi* — thus; *sri-visnu-dharmottare* — in *Sri Visnu-dharmottara Purana anantani* — unlimited; *tava* — to you; *uktani* — described; *yani* — which *andani* — universes; *maya —* by me; *pura —* before; *sarvani —* all; *tani* — them; *samhrtya* — destroying; *sama-kalam* — at the same time; *jagat-patih* — the Lord of the universe; *prakrtau*— in His nature; *tisthati*—He remains; *tada* — then; *sa* — that; *ratrih* — the night; *tasya —* His; *kirtitd* — called; *iti* — thus.

In this context *prakrti* does not mean “material nature” but rather “His own nature,” and the word especially refers to His perpetual self-satisfaction. According to Dhananjayas dictionary, the three words *svabhavatprakrti*, and *sila* can be used as synonyms.

### Text 331

*itó aupodghatikam procya*  
*prakrtam parilikhyate*

**Пословный перевод:**

*iti* — thus; *aupodghatikam* — the side topic; *procya* — having spoken on; *prakrtam* — the main topic; *parilikhyate* — will be written about.

**Перевод:**

**Having dealt with this side topic, we can now return to our main discussion.**

**Комментарий:**

The main topic is Krsnas supremacy as the original Personality of Godhead. To support the main premise the author digressed, discussing Krsnas relationship with the multitude of universes and their rulers.

The logician Jagadlsa defines *upodghata* as follows: *cintam prakrti-siddhy-artham / upodghatam vidur budhah.* “The wise understand a side topic' to be a consideration presented to help establish the main idea.”

### Text 332

*kim ca tatraiva,*  
*yan martya-lilaupayikam sva-yoga-*  
*mayd-balam darsayatd grhltam*  
*vismdpanam svasya ca saubhagarddheh*  
*param padam bhiisana-bhusandhgam*  
*iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*kim ca* — furthermore; *tatra eva —* there also; *yat* — which; *martya —* of the mortal world; *lila-aupayikam* — suitable for the pastimes; *sva-yoga-maya- balam* — the potency of the internal energy; *darsayata —* by Him who is manifesting; *grhltam* — accepted; *vismdpanam* — cause of wonder; *svasya* — His own; *ca —* and; *saubhaga-rddheh* — of the treasure of good fortune; *param* — supreme; *padam* — position; *bhusana*— of His ornaments; *bhusana*— the ornaments; *ahgam* — whose limbs; *iti* — thus.

**Перевод:**

**Also in the same chapter we find: “The Lord decided to appear to show the power of His internal potency, Yogamaya. He came in His original form, just suitable for His pastimes among the human beings. That form amazed even the Lord Himself in His form as the Lord of Vaikuntha. Thus His sSri Krsna’s\] transcendental body is the treasure of good fortune and the ornament of all ornaments” sSrlmad-Bhagavatam 3.2.12\]**

**Комментарий:**

Sri Uddhava begins this verse with the word *yat,* referring to Krsnas form *(bimbam),* of which he had spoken in the previous verse.

*pradarsyatapta-tapasam*  
*avitrpta-drsam nrnam*  
*adayantaradhad yas tu*  
*sva-bimbam loka-locanam*

**“Lord Sri Krsna, who manifested His original form before the vision of all on the earth, performed His disappearance by removing that form from the sight of those who could not actually see Him due to not having executed the required penance.” (*****Bhdgavatam*** **3.2.11)**

In this verse the word *grhltam* (“accepted”) indicates that Krsna decided to exhibit for some time His original form on earth. By doing this He revealed the influence of His divine enchanting potency, Yogamaya.

The form of Krsna is exactly suitable for His pastimes among human beings. If He did not appear human, His loving reciprocations with human beings, which attracted all who witnessed them, could not have come to light. When Krsna restrains His omnipotence and behaves like an ordinary mortal, His activities are supremely enchanting. His omnipotence becomes like a row of attractive mirrors attached to the beautifully painted curtain of His humanlike pastimes.

Although Krsna is aware of everything that exists and sees all beautiful things, He is still amazed by Himself. His form is the prime repository of all opulences. His handsome limbs, rather than being decorated by their ornaments, decorate the ornaments.

Krsna performs the pastimes of Narayana, one of His *vilasa* expansions, but His original humanlike pastimes are more pleasing to His devotees and Himself. Yogamaya. The word *grhitam\>* from the Third Canto verse being explained here, is glossed as *prakati-krtam* (‘‘made visible”). The Supreme Lords personal forms are not guises that He dons for temporary occasions; they are eternal, for any form of the Lord is His *svariipa* (essential identity) and is never assumed. Yet they are occasionally made visible in the material world. According to the words of the *Brahmanda Purana,* which Srila RCipa Gosvami will cite in text 396, *anadeyam aheyam ca:* “The Personality of Godhead never assumes or gives up His bodily form ”

### Text 342

*tat ha ca sn-kaurme,*  
*deha-dehi-bhida catra*  
*nesvare vidyate kvacit*  
*iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tatha ca* — and thus; *sri-kaurme* — in *Kurtna Purana; deha* — of the body; *dehi* — and the possessor of the body; *bhida*— difference; *ca* — and; *atra —* in Him; *na —* not; *isvare —* the Supreme Lord; *vidyate —* exists; *kvacit* — ever; *iti* — thus.

**Перевод:**

**As Sri Kurma Purana states, “In the Supreme Lord there is never any difference between the body and the possessor of the body”**

**Комментарий:**

Because of the inconceivable, simultaneous oneness and variety within the Lord, despite the oneness of His body and self we can speak of them as separate. We can even describe Him as struck with wonder at contemplating His body's beauty. In the realm of transcendence such conceptions do not violate the laws of nature and logic.

In the same way that philosophers make statements such as ‘existence is” without contradicting themselves, by the principle of *visesa,* or spiritual variety, we can talk about the Absolute Truths having a body, qualities, and activities.

### Text 344

*tat ha hi sri-baladevath prati sri-krsnoktau,*  
*dhanyeyam adya dharani trna-virudhas tvat-*  
*pada-sprso druma-latah karajabhimrstah*  
*nadyo drayah khaga-mrgah sadayavalokair*  
*gopyo ntarena bhujayor api yat-sprha srih*  
*iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tatha hi* — also; *sri-baladevam prati* — to Sri Baladeva; *sri-krsna*— of Sri Krsna; *uktau* — in the statement; *dhanya* — fortunate; *iyatn* — this; *adya* — now; *dharani* — the earth; *trim* — her grasses; *virudhah*— and bushes; *tvat* — Your; *pada* — of the feet; *sprsah* — receiving the touch; *druma* — the trees; *latah* — and creepers; *kara-ja* — by Your fingernails; *abhimrstdh*— touched; *nadyah*— the rivers; *adrayah*— and mountains; *khaga —* the birds; *mrgah* — and animals; *sa-daya* — merciful; *avalokaih —* by Your glances; *gopyah* — the *gopis; antarena* — in between; *bhujayoh —* Your two arms; *api*—indeed; *yat* — for which; *sprha* — maintaining the desire; *srih —* the goddess of fortune; *iti* — thus.

**Перевод:**

**There are also these words spoken by Sri Krsna to Sri Baladeva: “This earth has now become most fortunate because You have touched her grass and bushes with Your feet and her trees and creepers with Your fingernails, and because You have graced her rivers, mountains, birds, and animals with Your merciful glances. But above all, You have embraced the young cowherd women between Your two arms - a favor hankered after by the goddess of fortune herself” sBhagavatam 10.15.8\]**

**Комментарий:**

Out of respect for His elder brother Balarama, Krsna describes Him as having Krsnas own unparalleled and unsurpassable qualities. The land of Vrndavana is most fortunate because her grass and bushes have touched Krsnas feet, and because her trees and creepers have touched His hands when He picked their flowers, and because the rivers (like Sri Yamuna) and mountains (like Sri Govardhana) have received His glances. The *syama-lata* creepers, also known as the *gopi* plants, have felt His arms’ embrace. Alternatively, Krsnas cowherd girlfriends have felt His embraces. Even the Queen of Vaikuntha aspires to be embraced to Krsnas chest.

It is said that *prdyo vira-ratdh striyah:* “Women generally become attracted to heroes.” Based on this dictum, we can understand from Krsnas statement the magnitude of Sri Baladevas heroism in having killed such mighty demons as Pralamba.

This verse depicts the symptoms of *purva-rdga.* When He spoke this verse to His elder brother in the company of Their cowherd friends, Krsna had not yet passed His *pauganda* age and had not yet begun His intimate dealings with the young *gopis.*

### Text 346

*ato ‘tra tiaiva tdtparyam*

Why did Krsna divulge such private matters to Lord Baladeva? Because the two brothers are always completely open with one another, related eternally in the transcendental mood of *sakhya*.

### Text 354

*tatha sri-brahmande,*  
*sahasra-namnam pṝnyanarh*  
*trir dvrttya tu óat phalam*  
*ekdvrttyd tu krsnasya*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tatha* — thus; *sri-brahmande*— in the *Brahmanda Purana; sahasra* — one thousand; *namndm* — names; *punyanam* — holy; *trih* — three times; *avrttya*— by repetition; *tu*— and; *yat* — which; *phalam* — fruit; *eka- avrttya* — by a single repetition; *tu —* but; *krsnasya* — of Krsna; *nama- ekam —* a single name; *tat —* that; *prayacchati* — bestows.

**Перевод:**

**Thus in Sri Brahmanda Purana: “The fruit attained by chanting the thousand holy names of Visnu three times is bestowed by one recitation of a single name of Krsna.”**

**Комментарий:**

Srila Veda-vyasas disciple Vaisampayana recited the thousand names of Visnu, and these are recorded in the *Mahabharata.* Vaisnavas consider the chanting of this *Visnu-sahasra-nama* a potent form of devotional service, and many repeat the thousand names daily.

A list of 108 names of Krsna found in the *Brahmanda Parana* is accom panied by the statement that any of these 108 names chanted just once will bestow the same good results as three recitations of the thousand names of Visnu. The names in Vaisampayana s recitation describe many of the Supreme Lords incarnations, but the *Brahmanda Purana* specifically lists names of the *svayam-rupa.* Thus Krsnas names are much more potent than Visnu s. Similarly, the *Bhagavad-glta* is more valuable than words spoken by other forms of the Supreme Lord.

### Text 363

*maivam asyadi-sunyasya*  
*janma-lilapy anadika*  
*svacchandato mukundena*  
*prakatyam niyate muhuh*

**Пословный перевод:**

*md evam* — don’t say like this; *asya* — of Him; *adi-sunyasya*— who has no beginning; *jantna —* of birth; *lila*— the pastime; *api —* also; *anadika* — beginningless; *svacchandatah*— by His sweet will; *mukundena* — by Lord Mukunda; *prdkatyam* — to manifestation; *niyate* — are brought; *muhuh* — repeatedly.

**Перевод:**

**No, it is not like this. This Supreme Lord has no beginning, and similarly His pastimes of taking birth have no beginning. By His own sweet will Lord Mukunda manifests these pastimes repeatedly.**

**Комментарий:**

The *Gopala-tdpani Upanisad* describes how at the beginning of creation newly born Brahma turned to Krsna as his worshipable Lord. The *smrti* scriptures speak of other ancient personalities like Prahlada and Priyavrata also worshiping Krsna. This is evidence that there is no time before which Krsna was not yet born. He accepts and enjoys pastimes of taking birth, and these pastimes also go on eternally. He appears wherever and whenever He and His devotees desire.

In the excitement of narrating Krsna’s *janma-lila,* sages may become careless and use such expressions as *dvaparavasane* (“at the end of the Dvapara Age”), as if Krsna didn’t exist before His apparent birth.

### Text 364

*tatha ca sri-trtiye,*  
*sva-santa-rupesv itaraih sv-arupair*  
*abhyardyamanesv anukampitatma*  
*pardvareso mahad-amsa-yukto*  
*hy ajo ‘pi jato bhagavan yathagnih*  
*iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tatha* — so; *ca* — and; *sri-trtiye* — in the Third Canto; *sva-santa-riipesu* when His own devotees, whose forms are peaceful; *itaraih* — by others (nondevotees); *su-arupaih* — whose forms are ugly; *abhyardyamanesu* — are being abused; *anukampita-atma* — being all-compassionate by nature; *para-avara —* of everything spiritual and material; *isah — lhe* controller; *mahat-amsa-yuktah* — accompanied by the plenary portion of *rnahat- tattva; hi* — indeed; *ajah* — the unborn; *api* — although; *jatah* — is born; *bhagavan* — the Personality of Godhead; *yatha* — as; *agnih* — fire; *iti* — thus.

**Перевод:**

**The Third Canto s3.2.15\] also states: “The Personality of Godhead Sri Krsna is all-compassionate. He controls both the spiritual and material creations. Although He is unborn, when antagonists abuse His peaceful devotees, He arises like fire, accompanied by His mighty ariisas.”**

**Комментарий:**

Sri Krsna is *bhagavan*, the Supreme Person, full in the six kinds of perfections.

Because of His heartfelt concern for His devotees, He appears in this world. As fire appears to arise from wood, He seems to take birth, but He does not require a new body and set of senses, as the finite souls do when they take birth in this world.

Krsna is the controller of all worlds in both the superior realm of pure spirit and the inferior realm of matter. When He appears in the material world, He brings with Him all other forms of God, His expansions. When an emperor goes out for conquest, he is accompanied by the lesser kings who are his vassals; similarly, when the original Personality of Godhead, Krsna, displays His *avatdra,* He is accompanied by His *vilasas* and *amsas.*

Residing eternally in His abode beyond Vaikuntha, Sri Krsna only appears to take birth, just as lire, already dormant in kindling wood, only appears to arise from it.

With all the evidence presented, only an envious person will still say that Krsnas existence has a beginning.

Texts 368 and 369 explain the phrase *mahad-amsa-yuktah*. The eight expansions include both *catur-vyuhas* of Vasudeva, Sankarsana, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha, the first of which appears in Mathura and Dvaraka from Krsna and Balarama, and the second of which appears in Vaikuntha from Lord Narayana.

**Комментарий:**

Since Lord Badari-narayana and other incarnations exhibited their pastimes from within Sri Krsna, a sage who had focused his attention on one of these particular avataras might assume that Krsna had expanded from Him. But those who understand the essence of devotional philosophy explain that Srila Veda-vyasa simply recorded these sages’ opinions in his compilations. His doing so is similar to his recording, in the Karna-parva of the Mahabharata, Kama’s opinion that Salya was superior to Krsna and that he, Kama, was superior to Arjuna.

### Text 387

*tatra tatra yatha vahnis*  
*tejo-rupena sann api*  
*jayate mani-kasthader*  
*hetum kancid avapya sah*  
*anadim eva janmadi-*  
*lilam eva tathadbhutam*  
*hetuna kenacit krsnah*  
*praduskuryat kadacana*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatra tatra — in various locations; yatha — as; vahnih— fire; tejah-rupena— with its luminous essence; san — existing; api — although; jayate — is generated; mani— from jewels; kastha — pieces of wood; adeh— and so on; hetum — cause; kancit— some; avapya — obtaining; sah — it; anadim — beginningless; eva — indeed; janma-adi— of birth and so on; lilam — pastimes; eva — indeed; tatha — so; adbhutam — amazing; hetuna — through a cause; kenacit — certain; krsnah — Krsna; praduskuryat — reveals; kadacana — at certain times.

**Перевод:**

**Fire’s luminous essence is present in various objects, such as flintstones and the kindling wood used to ignite sacrificial fires, but the fire becomes manifest only with the application of appropriate agents. Similarly, Krsna’s amazing birth and other pastimes are beginningless, but they are revealed only at certain times when there is a suitable cause.**

**Комментарий:**

Because the Supreme Lord and His identity, qualities, powers, and personality are absolutely indestructible, He is never compelled to take birth by coming into contact with the elements of a created body. Nonetheless, by His inconceivable energies He appears in this world, as the moon appears on the eastern horizon.

Fire is present in its potential form in many objects, but it becomes manifest only under certain circumstances, such as when one stone is struck by another to produce sparks that then come in contact with something flammable, or when sacrificial kindling wood is ignited by friction. Similarly, the Personality of Godheads pastime of taking birth is eternal, but it is manifest in the material cosmos only on certain occasions, such as at the completion of the twenty-eighth Dvapara-yuga of the Vaivasvata manvantara. Thus the santodita theory and other similar theories about Krsnas appearing temporarily have no basis in fact.

### Text 389

*tatha bhayan-kara-taraih*  
*pidyamanesu danavaih*  
*priyesu karunapy atra*  
*hetur ity uktam eva hi*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha — also; bhayam-kara-taraih— who (the demons) are most horrifying; pidyamanesu — who (the devotees) are being oppressed; danavaih— by the demons; priyesu— for those (the devotees) whom He loves; karuna— compassion; api — also; atra — of this; hetuh — a cause; iti — thus; uktam — said; eva hi — indeed.

**Перевод:**

**It is also said that when horrible demons oppress those dear to Him, His compassion for His devotees causes Him to appear.**

**Комментарий:**

Why did Krsna descend to the earth? He came first of all to reclaim the aspiring devotees who are awaiting His mercy. Removing the earths burden of unruly kings was not the main purpose of Krsnas avatara. He easily could have accomplished that through empowered jivas, as shown, for example, in the Puranic descriptions of Parasara and Dhruva killing many Raksasas.

Rather, Krsna was motivated by His compassionate desire to relieve the anxiety of His Sadhaka devotees like Srutadeva and Bahulasva, who were incessantly thinking about His beautiful form and divine qualities, and who were extremely anxious to see Him in person. Furthermore, Krsna had sent many of His most beloved devotees to the earth before Him, including His parents Vasudeva and Devaki. They were being harassed by Kamsa and other enemies. Krsna wanted to show His affection for these devotees and destroy the demons disturbing them.

### Text 393

*kim casya parsadadinam*  
*apy ukta nitya-murtita*  
*tasyesvaresitur nitya-*

**Пословный перевод:**

kim ca — moreover; asya — His; parsada-adinam — of the associates and so on; api — also; ukta — said; nitya — eternal; murtita— having personal forms; tasya — His; isvara-isituh — of the Lord of lords; nitya — eternal; murtitve — in having a personal form; ka — what; vicitrata — novelty.

**Комментарий:**

Reason tells us that Krsnas pastimes can continue eternally only if He who displays those pastimes lives eternally. The Personality of Godhead is described in more than one Upanisad as “the one eternal conscious being among many eternal conscious beings who supplies the needs of all of them.” (Katha Upanisad 5.3 and Svetasvatara Upanisad 6.13) These words are also found in the Gopala-tapani Upanisad (Purva 20-21), where they are elaborated upon with special reference to Sri Krsna:

*eko vasi sarva-gah krsna idya*  
*eko ’pi san bahudha yo vibhati*  
*tam pitha-stham ye nubhajanti dhiras*  
*tesam sukham sasvatam netaresam*  
*nityo nityanam cetanas cetananam*  
*eko bahunam yo vidadhati kaman*  
*tam pitha-gam ye \`nuyajanti vipras*  
*tesam siddhih sasvati netaresam*

**“Krsna alone is the supreme controller, the all-pervading worshipable Lord. Although one, He appears as many. The wise who worship Him properly on His royal throne achieve eternal happiness, but not others. That one eternal conscious being among many eternal conscious beings supplies the needs of all others. Again, the wise who worship Him properly on His royal throne achieve eternal perfection, but not others.”**

In a previous verse (Purva 12) the Gopala-tapani describes Krsna as gopa-gopi-gavavitam, “surrounded by cowherd boys, cowherd girls, and cows.” These associates are the “many eternal conscious beings” whose needs He supplies, fulfilling all their desires.

**Комментарий:**

Using the rhetorical principle sthuna-nikhata, “planting the pillar deeper,” Srila Rupa establishes the eternality of Krsnas personality even more solidly by considering another argument of the Mayavadis. The impersonalists argue that Krsna, as pure consciousness and bliss, has no visible form. They say that He comes into view by assuming bodies made from visuddha-sattva, which they consider the unmixed material mode of goodness. A number of statements from the Puranas and epics seem to corroborate this theory.

*sambandhena pradhanasya*  
*harer nasty eva kartrta*  
*akartaram atah prahuh*  
*puranam tam pura-vidah iti*

**Пословный перевод:**

atra — of this matter; samadhanam — resolution; yatha — as follows; sri-vasudeva-adhyatme — in Sri Vasudeva Adhyatma; aprasiddheh — because of being not well known; tat—His; gunanam — on the part of the qualities; anama — having no name; asau — He; prakirtitah —is called; aprakrtatvat— because of being nonmaterial; rupasya — of the form; api —and; arupah — as formless; asau — He; udiryate— is known; sambandhena — due to connection; pradhanasya— with material nature; hareh — of Lord Hari; na asti — there is not; eva — indeed; kartrta — activeness; akartaram — nondoer; atah — therefore; prahuh — call; puranam — ancient; tarn — Him; pura — of ancient reality; vidah — the knowers; iti — thus.

**These points are resolved as follows in Sri Vasudeva Adhyatma: ‘‘Because Lord Hari’s qualities are not completely known, He is called nameless. Because His form is not material, He is called formless. And because He is not connected with material nature, that ancient Lord is called inactive by the wise ancients who know Him.”**

**Комментарий:**

The scriptural evidence cited above is authoritative, but one is obliged to understand it correctly. The Supreme Lord is “nameless” in the sense that no one is able to describe everything about Him. Kartsnyena najo 'py abhidhatum isah: “Even unborn Brahma is unable to name all His qualities.” (Bhagavatam 12.4.39)

“Formless” should be understood to mean “without material form.” And “inactive” means that, unlike the conditioned souls, the Lord does not have to act under the sway of material nature. He is active, but on His own initiative.

Tad aiksata: “He glanced.” (Chandogya Upanisad 6.2.3) So \`kamayata: “He desired.” (Taittiriya Upanisad 2.6) Lord Visnu\`s glancing and His desiring to create are actions undertaken before He awakened His prakrti. Whether in creating the material world or in His loving dealings with His pure devotees, the Personality of Godhead always acts with absolute freedom. This has already been illustrated in the passage cited from the Bhagavatam\`s Second Canto describing Lord Brahmas vision of Vaikuntha (texts 229-34 of this chapter).

### Text 424

**Комментарий:**

Lord Haris pastimes are said to have no beginning or end. But a faithless person, thinking that only someone limited by space and time can perform actions, may doubt whether the all-pervading Supreme can have pastimes at all. And if we say that the Supreme is limited, wouldn’t that mean He has a beginning and His activities also have a beginning?

To resolve this doubt, one must understand that the Supreme Lord’s acts are inconceivable. In one place He can act as a small child for His mother’s pleasure, and simultaneously He can make Himself accessible to the meditation of countless mystics throughout the universe.

**As the Tenth Canto s10.9.13-14\] describes, “The Supreme Personality of Godhead has no beginning and no end, no exterior and no interior, no front and no rear. In other words, He is all-pervading. Because He is not under the influence of the element of time, for Him there is no difference between past, present, and future; He exists in His own transcendental form at all times. Being absolute, beyond relativity, He is free from distinctions between cause and effect, although He is the cause and effect of everything. That unmanifested person, who is beyond the perception of the senses, had now appeared as a human child, and Mother Yasoda, considering Him her own ordinary child, bound Him to the wooden mortar with a rope.”**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna has no spatial limits that could define His inside and outside. He is simultaneously present in each and every corner of the cosmos. He resides within the living beings, within material nature, and within the universe as a whole. But one unpretentious cowherd woman of Vraja, Yasoda, thinks of Him as her son and punishes Him for being naughty.

*As Queen Kunti remembers,*  
*gopy adade tvayi krtdgasi dama tavad*

*sa mam vimohayati bhir api yad bibheti*

**“My dear Krsna, the gopi took up a rope to bind You when You committed an offense, and Your perturbed eyes overflooded with tears that washed the mascara from Your eyes. And You were afraid, though fear personified is afraid of You. This sight is bewildering to me.” (Bhagavatam 1.8.31)**

This verse from the Tenth Canto describes Krsna, whom Mother Yasoda saw as her child, as martya-lingay“in the form of a human being.” The Gopala-tapani Upanisad (Purva 10) also describes Him in human form: dvi-bhujam mauna-mudradhyam. “He has two arms, beautifully held in a gesture of quiet contemplation.”

He is adhoksaja, uninterested in ordinary sense pleasure because He perpetually enjoys the pastimes that comprise His essential being.

### Text 427

*tathaiva ca puranesu*  
*srimad-bhagavatadisu*  
*sruyate krsna-lilanam*  
*nityata sphutam eva hi*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha eva — moreover; ca — and; puranesu — and Puranas; srimat-bhagavata-adisu— Srimad-Bhagavatam and others; sruyate — is heard; krsna-lilanam — of Krsnas pastimes; nityata — the eternality; sphutam — explicitly; eva hi — indeed.

**Перевод:**

**Moreover, we hear unequivocal statements in Srimad-Bhagavatam and other Puranas that describe the eternal nature of Krsna’s pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

Someone might reason that the Lords pastimes are just like any other activities. They can occur only if each action or movement in sequence has a start and a completion. Thus Krsnas pastimes must come to an end and cannot be eternal.

This objection is answered by considering the unique powers of the supreme controller. For one thing, He has unlimited forms, as many statements of the scripture attest. Eko ’pi san bahudha yo vibhati: “Although one, He appears as many.” (Gopala-tapani Upanisad, Purva 20) Ekaneka-svarupaya: “His real self is one and many.” (Visnu Purana 1.2.3) He also has unlimited associates, as the Chandogya Upanisad (7.26.2) states: sa ekadha bhavati dvidha. “He appears alone and in the company of many.” And He lives in countless transcendental abodes: paramam padam avabhati bhuri. “His supreme residence manifests itself in unlimited forms.” (Rg Veda 1.154.6)

Considering these points, we must conclude that His activities have no beginning. Each of His pastimes, in the association of particular devotees, appears in multiple places, and although each lila appears to have a beginning and an end, as it ends in one location it begins in another. Therefore there is no cessation of any of His pastimes and no impediment to calling them eternal.

One might still object, “We can grant that the pastimes continue without break, but when one of them repeats in another place that must be considered a different activity.”

No. We can even find examples of quite ordinary events in this world that repeat but are still the same action. For example, someone may shout, “Look, a cow, a cow!” He speaks the same word twice, not two different words with the same sound. Similarly, although the Supreme Lord may conclude the exhibition of a pastime in one place and commence it in another, it is still the same ongoing pastime. His forms, pastimes, devotees, and places of residence each have their own unified persistence.

The Purusa-bodhini Upanisad confirms the eternal nature of His pastimes: eko devo nitya-lilanurakto / bhakta-vyapi bhakta-hrdy antar-atma. “The one Supreme Lord is immersed in His eternal pleasure pastimes. He always stays with His devotees, seated in their hearts as their inner Self.”

The statement that Krsna is “the chief of the Purusas” (pumsam rsabhah) means that He is the chief of the three Purusa creators because He is the amsi from whom They expand.

He is the beloved consort of the goddess Laksmi of Vaikuntha, of Sri Radha of Vrndavana, and of Sri Rukmini of Dvaraka.

### Text 430

*sri-dasame sri-sukoktau,*  
*jayati jana-nivaso devaki-janma-vado*  
*yadu-vara-parisat svair dorbhir asyann adharmam*  
*sthira-cara-vrjina-ghnah su-smita-sri-mukhena*  
*vraja-pura-vanitanam vardhayan kama-devam*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-dasame — in the Tenth Canto; sri-suka — of Sri Sukadeva; uktau — in the statement; jayati — eternally lives gloriously; jana-nivasah — He who lives among human beings and is the ultimate resort of all living entities; devaki- janma-vadah — known as the son of Devaki; yadu-vara-parisat — served by the exalted members of the Yadu dynasty; svaih dorbhih — by His own arms; asyan — expelling; adharmam — irreligion; sthira-cara — of all living entities; vrjina-ghnah— the destroyer of all the ill fortune; su-smita — always smiling; sri-mukhena — by His beautiful face; vraja-pura-vanitanam— of the damsels of Vrndavana; vardhayan — increasing; kama-devam— the lusty desires.

**Перевод:**

**In the words of Sri Suka in the Tenth Canto s10.90.48\]: “Lord Sri Krsna, the ultimate resort of all living entities, is also known as Devaki-nandana or Yasoda-nandana, the son of Devaki and Yasoda. He is the guide of the Yadu dynasty. With His mighty arms He kills everything inauspicious and every impious man. By His presence He destroys all misfortune for all living entities, moving and inert. His blissful smiling face always increases the lusty desires of the gopis of Vrndavana. May He be all glorious and happy!”**

**Комментарий:**

When Sukadeva Gosvami was about to describe to Maharaja Pariksit the pastime of Krsna\`s disappearance, he first spoke this verse to encourage the king, who had no interest in life other than Krsna. That Krsna, who is glorified by Sukadeva, is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. As He was during His visible pastimes on earth, so He remains today. Sukadeva does not want Pariksit to become confused by the narration of the mausala-lila.People who have only the power of external sight may not see Him, but He always enjoys with His devotees in Vraja and His royal cities of Mathura and Dvaraka.

He always inspires amorous thoughts in the hearts of the women who love Him.

He is glorified here as devaki-janma-vada, “known for taking birth as the son of Devaki” and “as the son of Yasoda.” The Adi Purana explains that dve namni nanda-bharyaya yasoda devakiti ca: “Nanda\`s wife has two names, Yasoda and Devaki.”

Vada, “known,” is used here to indicate the impartial discussions of serious philosophers who want to discover the truth without promoting their own agenda. Even today the wisest philosophers conclude that Krsna took birth from both Yasoda and Devaki.

Krsna eternally reciprocates with His associates led by Sri Nanda in Vraja and Sri Vasudeva in the capital city of the Vrsnis. He unceasingly defeats the forces of irreligion through the agency of Sridama and His other friends in Vraja, and through the agency of Satyaki and the other Yadus in Dvaraka, all of whom He considers like His own mighty arms.

Krsna\`s pastimes are described by Sukadeva to Pariksit in the present tense, even though by the time Sukadeva narrated the Bhagavatam Krsna\`s manifest form had already been gone from this planet for some time. If Krsnas pastimes were not eternal, Sukadeva would not be justified in using the present tense.

To accomplish this they take birth from Surasena and others.**

**Комментарий:**

This is how Krsna arranges to make visible His pastimes with His eternal devotees. When the time came for Krsna to descend to the earth to relieve her burden, Lord Brahma ordered the demigods to join Krsna:

*giram samadhau gagane samiritam*  
*nisamya vedhas tridasan uvaca ha*

*vidhiyatam asu tathaiva ma ciram*

Thus he told the demigods: ‘O demigods, hear from me the order of Ksirodaka-sayi Visnu, the Supreme Person, and execute it attentively without delay. Before we submitted our petition to the Lord, He was already aware of the distress on earth. Consequently, for as long as the Lord moves on earth to diminish its burden by His own potency in the form of time, all of you demigods should appear through plenary portions as sons and grandsons in the family of the Yadus.’” (Bhagavatam 10.1.21-22)**

Some expansions of Krsnas eternal associates reside in heaven. Responding to Brahmas order, these expansions - such as Vasudeva\`s amsa Kasyapa and Nanda Maharajas amsa Drona - merged back into the originals from whom they expanded and took birth from fathers on the earth like Surasena and Parjanya Gopa.

In the Padma Purana Sri Krsna tells His wife Satyabhama,

*atha brahmadi-devanam*  
*tatha prarthanaya bhuvah*  
*agato ’ham ganah sarve*  
*jatas te ’pi maya saha*  
*ete hi yadavah sarve*  
*mad-gana eva bhamini*  
*sarvada mat-priya devi*  
*mat-tulya-guna-salinah*

**“Entreated by Mother Earth and the demigods led by Brahma, I have come here with all the members of my entourage, who have also taken birth. Thus, O radiant one, all these Yadavas are my personal associates. They are always very dear to Me, dear goddess, and their virtues are equal to Mine.”**

Also in the Padma Purana (Patala 73.18-19) Sri Vyasadeva says to Ambarisa Maharaja,

*pasya tvam darsayisyami*  
*svarupam veda-gopitam*  
*tato \`pasyam aham bhupa*  
*balam kalambuda-prabham*  
*gopa-kanyavrtam gopam*  
*hasantam gopa-balakaih*

**“The Lord told me, ‘Watch and I will show You My true form, which the Vedas keep secret.’**

**“I then saw a boy, O King, whose luster was like that of a black lotus flower. He was a cowherd boy surrounded by cowherd maidens and joking with other cowherd boys.”**

In this vision, Vyasadeva saw the original Personality of Godhead in the company of the young cowherds. Certainly Nanda Maharaja and the other elder gopas were not far away.

**Комментарий:**

Once Krsnas parents and other elders have come to earth in Gokula and Mathura, Krsna also comes.

Krsna is Lila-purusottama, the playful Supreme Personality of Godhead, and Lord Narayana of Vaikuntha is one of His vilasa expansions. Vasudeva is His first vyuha expansion. The second, Sankarsana, appears as His older brother Balarama. The other two, Pradyumna and Aniruddha, become Krsna\`s son and grandson.

Sukadeva Gosvami describes Krsna\`s appearing in Vasudeva\`s heart:

**“Thus the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Supersoul of all living entities, who vanquishes all fear for His devotees, entered the mind of Vasudeva in full opulence. While carrying the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead within the core of his heart, Vasudeva bore the Lords transcendentally illuminating effulgence, and thus he looked as bright as the sun. He was therefore very difficult to see or approach for all living entities, even for such formidable men as Kamsa.” (Bhagavatam 10.2.16-17)**

How is it that in Vraja Krsna exhibited pastimes of Ksirodaka-sayi Visnu? It was possible because that Purusa had united with Him. The original Aniruddha appeared as Pradyumna\`s son, but before He did, His expansion, the third Purusa, resided in Krsnas body.

The Matsya Purana specifies the time of Krsna\`s descent:
