**“After the current Rathantara-kalpa ends, the twenty-third day of Brahma, the Varaha-kalpa, will begin. During that kalpa, at the end of the twenty-eighth Dvapara Age of the auspicious seventh manvantara, called Vaivasvata, the maintainer of the seven worlds, Lord Vasudeva Janardana, the performer of wonderful pastimes, will appear in three forms to relieve the earth of her burden: as the sage Dvaipayana Vyasa, as Balarama, the son of Rohini, and as Kesava”**

Srila Sukadeva also describes Krsna\`s transfer from Vasudeva\`s heart to Devaki\`s, taking with Him His vyuha Ksirodaka-sayi Visnu and other amsas:

*tato jagan-mangalam acyutamsam*

*dadhara sarvatmakam atma-bhutam*  
*kastha yathananda-karam manastah*

**“Thereafter, accompanied by His plenary expansions, the fully opulent Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is all-auspicious for the entire universe, was transferred from the mind of Vasudeva to the mind of Devaki. Devaki, having thus been initiated by Vasudeva, became beautiful by carrying Lord Krsna, the original consciousness for everyone, the cause of all causes, within the core of her heart, just as the east becomes beautiful by carrying the rising moon.” (Bhagavatam 10.2.18)**

This verse describes Devaki carrying Krsna in her mind, but we should understand that Krsna also entered her womb. The demigods affirmed this by saying to Devaki: distyamba te kuksi-gatah parah puman “O mother, by good fortune the Supreme Personality of Godhead is now within your womb.” (Bhagavatam 10.2.41)

With the following statement, *Sri* Visnu Purana (4.11.2) indicates that the two-armed human form of Krsna is the original Supreme:

**“Any human being who hears about the Yadu dynasty becomes liberated from all past sins. The Supreme Truth, known by the name Krsna, descended in His human form as a member of that family.”**

Why then does Sri Sukadeva describe the Krsna who took birth from Devaki as catur-bhujam sankha-gadady-udayudham, “four-armed, holding conch, club, and other weapons”? (Bhagavatam 10.3. 9) Is there some contradiction here?

No. As explained in the verse under discussion, the same Krsna exhibits either two or four arms on various occasions. He has only two arms when He acts like an ordinary human, showing innocence despite His omniscience, and showing those capacities that suit His mood.

### Text 448

*tathapi dvi-bhujatvasya*

**Комментарий:**

The most sublime secret of the revealed scriptures is that God in His fullest glory acts and appears like an ordinary person, and therefore that Krsnas two-armed form is primary. To keep this confidential, the scriptures sometimes describe His humanlike appearance as secondary.

To make clear that Krsna in human form is indeed the original Godhead, Narada twice spoke the same words (cited in this verse) to Yudhisthira:

*yuyam nr-loke bata bhuri-bhaga lokam punana munayo ’bhiyanti yesam grhan avasatiti saksad*  
*gudham param brahma manusya-lingam*

**“You Pandavas are so very fortunate in this world that many, many great saints, who can purify all the planets in the universe, come to your house just like ordinary visitors. After all, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Krsna, is living confidentially in your home with you, appearing like a human being.” (Bhagavatam 7.10.48 and 7.15.75)**

### Text 450

*so yam nitya-sutatvena*  
*tasya rajaty anaditah*  
*krsnah prakata-lilayam*  
*tad-dvarenapy abhut tatha*

**Пословный перевод:**

sah — He; ayam — the same; nitya — always; sutatvena — as the son; tasyah —her (Yasoda\`s); rajati — appears; anaditah — without beginning; krsnah — Krsna; prakata-lilayam — in His visible pastimes; tat-dvarena— by this means; api — also; abhut — has appeared; tatha — and.

**Перевод:**

**This same Krsna is Yasoda’s son eternally, and thus in his visible pastimes he also took birth from her.**

**Комментарий:**

The Puranas call Krsna “the son” to indicate literal birth from both Devaki and Yasoda. Even accepting this as part of His sequential, visible pastimes, one may still question whether He acts as a son in His eternal, invisible pastimes. The answer is that Krsna eternally acts as the son of both Devaki and Yasoda. The word api in this verse indicates that He accepts both mothers also in His visible pastimes, and tatha indicates that He accepts them “in the same way,” indicating birth through the ordinary process as known in the material world.

Another doubt might be raised: In Krsna\`s aprakata-lila, He and both pairs of His parents exist eternally. How, then, do they enter into relationships as mother, father, and son, which seem dependent on temporal differences of older and younger? We resolve this doubt by understanding that Krsna accepts particular moods and relationships according to the various attitudes of His devotees. In the words of the Svetasvatara Upanisad (5.4), bhava-grahyam anidakhyam: “He is perceived according to one\`s affection for Him. He depends on no material support.”

Devaki's maternal love is not exactly the same as Yasoda\`s. Yasoda is not concerned whether or not Krsna is God. Her surrender as His mother has no conditions or inhibitions due to respect for His Godhood. Thus her love is described as purer than Devaki’s. Still, Krsna accepts both of them as His mothers. When a lotus flower grows, it produces many petals simultaneously; some of them may grow larger and more beautiful than others, but all of them belong to the lotus flower.

Sri Sukadeva does describe Krsna in His prakata-lila as taking birth from both Devaki and Yasoda. He mentions Krsna\`s birth from Devaki explicitly and His birth from Yasoda implicitly. It was the Lords desire that Sukadeva present His narration like this.

In his description of Krsna\`s birth Sukadeva says,

*nisithe tama-udbhute*  
*jayamane janardane*  
*devakyam deva-rupinyam*  
*visnuh sarva-guha-sayah*  
*avirasid yatha pracyam*  
*disindur iva puskalah*

**“Then the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Visnu, who is situated in the core of everyone’s heart, appeared from the heart of Devaki in the dense darkness of night, like the full moon rising on the eastern horizon, because Devaki was of the same category as Sri Krsna.” (Bhagavatam 10.3.8)**

*A little later he says,*  
*yasoda nanda-patni ca*  
*jatam param abudhyata*  
*na tal-lingam parisranta*  
*nidrayapagata-smrtih*

**“Exhausted by the labor of childbirth, Yasoda was overwhelmed with sleep. She understood that the child had taken birth, but didn't know whether it was a boy or a girl.” (Bhagavatam 10.3.53)**

The first of these two statements can be understood as follows. The word devakyam connects with both the phrase that precedes it and the one that follows it. Sitting in the middle of the two phrases, like a lamp sitting on a patio between two rooms, it shines in both.

The first phrase contains the participle jayamane (“being born”), which goes with devakyam meaning “from Yasoda.” “Lord Janardana, Krsna, was being born from Yasoda in the dense darkness of midnight on the eighth day in the dark half of Bhadrapada.”

The second phrase has its own corresponding verb, avirasit (“He appeared”). This indicates that Krsna appeared in two simultaneous births. The second phrase tells us, then, that “Lord Visnu, the same Krsna, appeared at the same moment from Devaki, the daughter of King Devaka.”

If this is not clear enough, please consider the words spoken in Sri Hari-vamsa:

*garbha-kale tv asampurne*  
*astame masi te striyau*  
*devaki ca yasoda ca*  
*susuvate samam tada*

**“In their eighth months, before the completion of the normal term of pregnancy, both women, Devaki and Yasoda, gave birth at the same time.”**

Since the daughter, Yogamaya, was born a little later, this must refer to the simultaneous birth of the same male son.

Srila Sukadeva helps us understand this in his account:

*tatas ca saurir bhagavat-pracoditah*  
*sutam samadaya sa sutika-grhat*  
*yada bahir gantum iyesa tarhy aja*  
*ya yogamayajani nanda-jayaya*

**“Thereafter, exactly when Vasudeva, being inspired by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, was about to take the newborn child from the delivery room, Yogamaya, the Lords spiritual energy, took birth as the daughter of the wife of Maharaja Nanda” (Bhagavatam 10.3.47)**

From this verse Yogamaya is known as Krsna\`s younger sister. Neither Vasudeva nor Yasoda, however, noticed that the boy and girl took birth a few hours apart.

Devaki and Yasoda are both deva-rupini, qualitatively one with the Personality of Godhead. Sri Krsna\`s supreme purity was therefore in no way out of place when He resided in their wombs. A king appears even more regal when sitting in a gem-bedecked palace refreshed by fragrant breezes. Indeed, Srila Sukadeva says that Krsna appeared puskala, in His full glory.

In Sukadeva\`s statement about Yasoda\`s being fatigued after giving birth, he directly says that she recognized the signs of the Godhead in her newborn child and understood that the Supreme Lord had taken birth from her. Why was she unaware that she had given birth to a second child, a girl, and that Vasudeva had taken the girl away? Because her fatigue prevented her from seeing the signs (tal-lingam). According to the Visva-locana dictionary, lingam cihnanumanayoh: “Linga means sign or 'deduction.'”

Narada Muni declares openly in the Adi Purana that Krsna also took birth from Yasoda:

*nanda-gopa-grhe putro*  
*yasoda-garbha-sambhavah*

**“This son took birth from the womb of Yasoda in the house of Nanda Gopa.”**

With this in mind, we can take literally Srimad-Bhagavatam\`s references to Krsna as the son of Nanda and Yasoda:

*nandas tv atmaja utpanne*  
*jatahlado maha-manah*  
*ahuya vipran veda-jnan*  
*snatah sucir alankrtah*

**“Nanda Maharaja was naturally very magnanimous, and when Lord Sri Krsna appeared as his son, he was overwhelmed by jubilation. Therefore, after bathing and purifying himself and dressing himself properly, he invited brahmanas who knew how to recite Vedic mantras.” (Bhagavatam 10.5.1)**

*nayam sukhapo bhagavan*  
*dehinam gopika-sutah*  
*jnaninam catma-bhutanam*  
*yatha bhaktimatam iha*

**“The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Krsna, the son of the gopi Yasoda, is accessible to devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but He is not as easily accessible to mental speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austerities and penances, or to those who consider the body the same as the self.” (Bhagavatam 10.9.21)**

When Kamsa rushed into the prison cell intending to kill Devaki\`s eighth child, Devaki pretended that her eighth child was a girl, Yogamaya, although she knew very well that Krsna was her eighth child. Srila Sukadeva should not be faulted when he supports this intentional deception meant to protect Krsna by speaking the words upaguhyatmajam, “embracing her daughter.” (Bhagavatam 10.4.7)

Why, then, does Srila Rupa only suggest that Krsna also took birth from Yasoda? Because the authors worshipable Lord Krsna wants this. Krsna desires, “I appear in the homes of both Nanda and Vasudeva, but remain visible in only one of those forms, living with Nanda. If both forms remain, Kamsa will take note and create distress for My parents, Vasudeva and Devaki. Therefore, O reciter of My pastimes, please do not divulge this secret when you sing your narration.” Srila Rupa nonetheless provides a hint in this text of Laghu-bhagavatamrta by using the word api (“also”) to indicate that Krsna took birth from Yasoda as well.

### Text 462

*dvi-bhujah sarvada so ’tra*  
*na kadacic catur-bhujah*  
*gopyaikaya yutas tatra*  
*parikridati nityada*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

dvi-bhujah — with two arms; sarvada — always; sah — He; atra — here; na kadacit— never; catuh-bhujah — four-armed; gopya — with the cowherd girl; ekaya — alone; yutah — joined; tatra — there; parikridati — He plays; nityada — constantly; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**“In Vrndavana He always has two hands, never four. He plays constantly in the exclusive company of His cowherd girlfriend”**

**Комментарий:**

Srila Rupa Gosvami is not saying that the Krsna in Vrndavana and the Krsna outside of Vrndavana are two different people. If Krsna never left Vrndavana, why did the Vraja-vasis suffer such pain of separation that Uddhava had to go there to console them? And why did the Vraja-vasis travel the great distance to Kuruksetra to meet Krsna? And why do some Puranas say that Krsna visited Vrndavana again?

With these questions in mind, someone may propose that Nandas son, with His vyuha Vasudeva merged within Him, left Vrndavana to go to Mathura and elsewhere and then later returned from Dvaraka to Vrndavana. This explanation would contradict the words of the Yamala-tantra. Srila Rupa, therefore, answers these questions with reference to Krsnas prakata and aprakata-lila.

*atha prakata-rupena*

*svam vyanjan vasudevatam*  
*yo vasudevo dvi-bhujas*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha — then; prakata-rupena — in His manifest form; krsnah — Krsna; yadu-purini — to the capital of Yadus; vrajet — travels; vraja-isa-jatvam — being the son of the king of Vraja; acchadya— giving up; svam— His own; vyanjan— manifesting; vasudevatam — being the son of Vasudeva; yah — who; vasudevah — Vasudeva; dvi-bhujah — two-armed; tatha — and; bhati — appears; catuh-bhujah — four-armed.

**Перевод:**

**Комментарий:**

This is Srila Rupa Gosvami\`s explanation of how Krsna leaves Vrndavana in His prakata-lila. In Mathura, Krsna keeps private His identity as the darling of Vraja to foster the particular loving relationships the Mathura-vasis have with Him. There He simply shows Himself as the son of Vasudeva.

### Text 464

*tas ta madhu-pure lilah*  
*prakatayya yadudvahah*  
*dvaravatyam tatha yati*  
*tam tam lilam prakasakah*

**Пословный перевод:**

tah tah — various; madhu-pure — in Mathura; lilah — pastimes; prakatayya — after displaying; yadu-udvahah — the great hero of the Yadus; dvaravatyam — to Dvaraka; tatha — and; yati — goes; tam tam — various; lilam — pastimes; prakasakah — to display.

**Перевод:**

**After displaying various pastimes in Mathura City, the great hero of the Yadus goes to Dvaraka to exhibit many pastimes there.**

**Комментарий:**

The word prakasaka indicates the agent of the action of displaying, but according to Panini\`s grammar, this suffix -aka can also sometimes be used as a substitute for the infinitive form (prakasitum). Tumun-nvulau kriyayam kriyarthayam: “When a verb form is used to refer to the action itself, -aka can be substituted for either of the suffixes -turn or -nvul.” (Panini\`s Astadhyayi 3.3.10) Thus the meaning of prakasaka in this verse is “in order to exhibit.”

### Text 467

*vraje prakata-lilayam*  
*trin masan viraho 'muna*  
*tatrapy ajani visphurtih*  
*pradurbhavopama hareh*  
*tri-masyah paratas tesam*

**Пословный перевод:**

vraje—in Vraja; prakata-lilayam — in His visible pastimes; trin — for three; masan — months; virahah — separation; amuna — from Him; tatra — there; api — also; ajani — occurred; visphurtih — the appearance; pradurbhava-upama — as if manifested anew; hareh — of Lord Hari; tri-masyah — the three months; paratah — after; tesam —of them; saksat — directly; krsnena — with Krsna; sangatih — association.

**Комментарий:**

How did the Vraja-vasis survive Krsna\`s absence after He left them to go to Mathura? They survived because they had to endure the fire of separation for only three months. Or, looking at this another way, they were able to bear the sweet ecstasy of love in separation for only three months. When Krsna again showed Himself in Vraja, He attracted the Vraja-vasis so intensely that they felt as if He had appeared for the first time. Just as dyeing cloth with an astringent alkali gives it a brilliant color, so the experience of separation from Krsna intensified the pleasure of the devotees' contact with Him. For this purpose Krsna made them remain without Him for some time.

While trying to leave Vraja on Akrura\`s chariot, Krsna sent a messenger to assure the gopis He would return very soon.

### Text 475

Nanda and the other cowherds had accompanied Krsna and Balarama to Mathura to pay their taxes and honor Kamsa\`s invitation to attend a festival. After the festival - during which Kamsa had hoped to see the end of His two young enemies but instead suffered his own end - Krsna asked His father to return home to look after His mother and all the other Vraja-vasis. He Himself would stay in Mathura a little longer to help Ugrasena and others.

### Text 478

**Комментарий:**

Krsna\`s devotees in Dvaraka confirm the veracity of Krsna\`s promises to the gopis and Nanda Maharaja.

Lord Krsna speaks the truth always, as He explains to Sri Narada in the Hari-vamsa (125.37):

*nanrtam hi vaco vipra*  
*prokta-purvam mayanagha*

**“O sinless brahmana, I have never spoken an untrue word.”**

The Krsna-nama-stotra of the Brahmanda Purana also describes Him as satya-vak satya-sankalpah, “true to His word and true to His resolve.” How could He who had never spoken a lie deceive His most beloved devotees?

goloka-namni — in the planet known as Goloka Vrndavana; nija-dhamni— the personal abode of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; tale — in the part underneath; ca —also; tasya— of that; devi—of the goddess Durga; maha-isa— of Lord Siva; hari — and of Narayana; dhamasu — in the planets; tesu tesu — in each of them; te te — those respective; prabhava-nicayah— numerous opulences; vihitah — established; ca — also; yena — by whom; govindam — Govinda; adi-purusam — the original person; lam — Him; aham — I; bhajami — worship; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**“Below the planet named Goloka Vrndavana are the planets known as Devi-dhama, Mahesa-dhama, and Hari-dhama. These are opulent in different ways. I adore the primeval Lord Govinda, who has alloted their respective authorities to the rulers of those graded realms”**

**Комментарий:**

This verse mentions the realms of Visnu, Siva, and Durga in reverse order of superiority. Lord Visnu rules the spiritual world Vaikuntha, Lord Siva presides in an intermediate region between those of spirit and matter, and Siva\`s consort Devi creates and controls the material world. Above all other worlds lies Krsna\`s Goloka.

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha — so; ca — and; agre — further on; sriyah — Laksmis, goddesses of fortune; kantah — loving consorts; kantah — the enjoyer, lover; parama-purusah — the Supreme Personality of Godhead; kalpa-taravah—desire trees; drumah — all the trees; bhumih — the land; cintamani-gana-mayi—made of the transcendental touchstone jewels; toyam — the water; amrtam — nectar; katha — talking; ganam — song; natyam — dancing; gamanam — walking; api — also; vamsi—the flute; priya-sakhi—constant companion; cit-anandam — transcendental bliss; jyotih — effulgence; param — the supreme; api — also; tat — that; asvadyam — everywhere perceived; api ca — also; — that; yatra — where; ksira-abdhih— ocean of milk; sarati — flows; surabhibhyah — from surabhi cows; ca — and; su-mahan— very great; nimesa-ardha — half a moment; akhyah — called; api — even; vrajati — passes; na — not; hi — certainly; yatra — where; api — even; samayah — time; bhaje — I worship; sveta-dvipam — Svetadvipa; tam — that; aham — I; iha — here; golokam — Goloka; iti — thus; yam —which; vidantah— know; te — they; santah — self-realized souls; ksiti— in this world; virala — seldom; carah — going; katipaye — few; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**And later in Sri Brahma-samhita (5.56): “I worship that transcendental realm known as Svetadvipa, where many loving consorts, Laksmi\`s in their unalloyed spiritual essence, perform amorous service to the Supreme Lord Krsna, their only lover. There every tree is wish-fulfilling, the soil is made of purpose gems, and the water is nectar. Every word is a song and every step a dance, and the flute is the dearmost friend. Everything in that realm, being of the nature of the supreme, is effulgent with transcendental bliss and highly relishable. A great ocean of milk flows from the numberless cows there, and no one experiences the passing away of even half a moment. That realm of Goloka is known to only a few self-realized souls in this world.”**

**Комментарий:**

In Goloka there is only one hero, and there are many heroines, the gopis, the supreme goddesses of fortune. There the light of the moon and other luminaries shines in its original form, as the Supreme Persons expanded effulgence, which contains all qualities. The inhabitants there not only enjoy seeing that effulgence but also enjoy relishing its taste, smelling its fragrance, and so on.

Time in Goloka does not contain the fixed divisions of days, months, years, and so on found in every material realm.

Goloka is called Svetadvipa because it is “white” (sveta) in the sense of spotlessly pure, untouched by any trace of illusion, and because it is an “island” (dvipa) in the sense of being above and separate from all other planets. It is not the same Svetadvipa as the residence of Lord Aniruddha in the Milk Ocean within this material universe.

### Text 505

*evam sapta-purinam tu*

*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam — thus; sapta — of the seven; purinam — holy cities; tu — but; sarva —than all; utkrstam — most excellent; tu — but; mathuram — Mathura; sruyatam — please hear; mahima — the glories; devi — O goddess; vaikuntha-bhuvana — the worlds of Vaikuntha; uttamah — exceeding; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**“But the most excellent of these seven holy cities is Mathura. O goddess, please hear Mathura’s glories, which exceed those of the Vaikuntha worlds.”**

**Комментарий:**

Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana confirms in his commentary that in this verse and verse 503 Goloka is included as a Vaikuntha region, the topmost region.

But how can the Mathura district on earth be even greater than Goloka? People go to Mathura and then return to their regular lives. And the residents suffer from old age and other miseries.

No, Vraja-bhumi is nonetheless the supreme abode. As by His inconceivable potency Lord Hari simultaneously stays in everyone\`s heart and yet remains transcendental, beyond all material existence, so despite superficial appearances Vraja-bhumi remains absolutely perfect and transcendental.

Those who reach there by fulfilling the prerequisites of sadhana never return. And, as materialists saw Krsna in His prakata-lila as a powerless young boy (nara-daraka), due to our faulty vision we see the residents of Vraja suffering from old age and other material impediments.

Gokula on the earth is at least as good as Goloka in the spiritual sky, and, as revealed in this authoritative verse cited by Srila Rupa Gosvami, it is sometimes considered superior. Srila Rupa will explain this point further in the remaining part of this chapter.

### Text 519

**Комментарий:**

In the material world, the sun, moon, and planets measure time, which rules the course of all events. The sun and moon visible in the Supreme Lord’s abode, however, are purely spiritual expansions of His internal potency. The movements of such spiritual planets are not dictated by the strictures of material time. Thus in Dvaraka Narada saw different times of day occurring simultaneously. But the arrangement for Gokula is special. There Krsna\`s lila-sakti disguises the supernatural powers of the transcendental sun and moon to protect the simplicity of Krsna\`s pastimes. In Gokula time seems to pass in the same order found in the material world.

The leading Vaisnavas in the line established by Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu consider Sri Gopala-tapani Upanisad the cream of revealed Vedic texts. This Upanisad describes the glories of Krsna as a young cowherd.

Tad hovaca hairanyo gopa-vesam abhrabham tarunam kalpa-drumasritam: “He said, ‘Brahma then saw a young boy with a complexion like a rain cloud. He was dressed as a cowherd and sat under a desire tree” (Gopala-tapani Upanisad, Purva 8) It is therefore not possible that this childhood appearance of the Supreme Godhead occurs only in His visible pastimes in the material world. Brahma heard the Gopala-tapani long before Krsna\`s avatara. Krsna\`s form as a young gopala is certainly eternal.

**Комментарий:**

In His gopala-lila, Krsna the cowherd boy enjoys the company of both cowherd boys and girls. Sage Panini considers that masculine nouns like gopala can refer to males and females due to the rule known as eka-sesa, by which one word can represent several. For example, pitarau literally means “two fathers,” but as an eka-sesa form it means “father and mother” This rule in Panini\`s grammar is stated as puman striya (Astadhyayi 1.2.67).

Krsna\`s gopala-lila is the most excellent of all His pastimes, even more wonderful than His activities in Mathura City and Dvaraka.

**The Tenth Canto s10.35.14-15\] states, “O pious Mother Yasoda, your son, who is expert in all the arts of herding cows, has invented many styles of flute-playing. When He takes His flute to His bimba-red lips and sends forth the tones of the harmonic scale in variegated melodies, Brahma, Siva, Indra, and other chief demigods become confused upon hearing the sound. Although they are the most learned authorities, they cannot ascertain the essence of that music, and thus they bow down their heads and hearts.”**

**Комментарий:**

This verse was spoken by the young gopis of Vraja. The musical scale contains only seven simple notes - nisadha, rsabha, and so on - but when Krsna artistically combines them in the song of His flute, the sound astounds the great demigods. Forgetting everything they know about the Absolute Truth from Vedanta philosophy, they wonder why the Supreme they had previously understood as pure sac-cid-ananda has now transformed into the form of a song. They bow their heads and minds in the direction of the sound. Such special “sweetness of the flute” (venu-madhurya) is not found in the pastimes of the Lord of Dvaraka.

In the words of Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.33.6) describing Krsna with the gopis in the rasa dance, tatrati-susubhe tabhir bhagavan devaki-sutah: “There, together with those women, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the son of Devaki, appeared in His most glorious feature.”

*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-dasame — in the Tenth Canto; ca — and; ka — which; stri—woman; anga — dear Krsna; te — Your; kala — sweet-sounding; pada — having melodies; amrta— nectarean; venu— of Your flute; gita — by the song; sammohita — completely bewildered; arya — of civilized people; caritat —from the proper behavior; na calet — does not deviate; tri-lokyam— within the three worlds; trai-lokya — of all the three worlds; saubhagam — the cause of auspiciousness; idam — this; ca — and; niriksya— seeing; rupam — the personal beauty; yat — because of which; go — the cows; dvija — birds; druma — trees; mrgah — and deer; pulakani — bodily hair standing on end; abibhran — they bore; iti — thus.

**It is also said in the Tenth Canto s10.29.40\]: “Dear Krsna, what woman in all three worlds wouldn’t deviate from religious behavior when bewildered by the nectarean melody of Your flute? Your beauty makes all three worlds auspicious. Indeed, even the cows, birds, trees, and deer manifest the ecstatic symptom of bodily hair standing on end when they see Your beautiful form.”**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna called the gopis with His flute-song to come dance with Him in the middle of the night, but when they arrived He pretended that He had no interest in enjoying with them. They responded with these words.

As mentioned above, even stalwart demigods like Siva and Indra are confused when they hear Krsnas flute song. How, then, can simple women who hear it be expected to retain their composure and remember their duties as respectable wives and mothers? And now that they actually see Krsna face to face, all hope of following their religious principles is lost forever. No one can fault them for accepting Krsna as their lover.

*iti sri-laghu-bhagavatamrte sri-krsnamrtam nama purva-khandam samaptam.*

**Перевод:**

**Thus ends the first part of Sri Laghu-bhagavatamrta, entitled Sri-krsnamrta.**

## Part II - Sri-Bhaktamrta (The Nectar of Krsna\`s Devotees)

### Text 1

*aradhanam mukundasya*  
*bhaved avasyakam yatha*  
*tatha tadiya-bhaktanam*  
*no ced doso \`sti dustarah*

**Пословный перевод:**

aradhanam — the worship; mukundasya — of Mukunda; bhavet — is; avasyakam — obligatory; yatha — as; tatha — so; tadiya — of His; bhaktanam — devotees; na u cet — otherwise; dosah — blame; asti — there is; dustarah — insurmountable.

**Перевод:**

**The worship of Mukunda is obligatory. So also, to avoid intractable blame, is the worship of His devotees.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the essential facts about the Supreme Lords identity, qualities, and powers, Srila Rupa Gosvami will now explain, in the brief second part of Sri Laghu-bhagavatamrta, the special nature of the Lords pure devotees. He presents the main theme with this statement, which follows the words atha sri-bhaktamrtam. Atha (“and now”) indicates immediate sequence: After completing ones study of the Supreme Lord, one should at once proceed to the study of His devotees. The word atha also underscores the undeniable difference between the Supreme Person and the persons who serve Him.

Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana begins his commentary on the Bhaktamrta section with this invocation:

*nityam nivasatu hrdaye*  
*caitanyakhyo murarir nah*  
*niravadyo nirvrtiman*  
*gaja-patir anukampaya yasya*

This verse translates in two ways:

“May Lord Murari, known as the source of all life, always reside in our hearts. By His mercy Gajendra, the chief of the elephants, became faultless and full of joy.”

And: “May Lord Murari, appearing as Caitanya Mahaprabhu, always reside in our hearts. By His mercy Gajapati Prataparudra became faultless and full of joy.”

A person who fails to do so will encounter severe sinful reactions”**

The Vasu mentioned here is Uparicara Vasu, whose pure devotion to Lord Visnu was mentioned in the previous chapter (text 415).

Those who try to approach Lord Visnu while neglecting His devotees are offenders. They do not serve the Lord to His satisfaction.

Lord Krsna also made this point while instructing the simple brahmana Srutadeva in Mithila.

Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana comments that this statement means that the worship of the Lord's devotees is superior even to the worship of the Lord Himself. One should offer Vaisnavas honor without prejudice, without scrutinizing their birth and other material qualifications. Rather, one should happily accept the water that has washed their feet and the remnants of their food.

The Personality of Godheads various forms as svayam-rupa, vilasa, vyuha, and so on can be graded according to how fully They exhibit the Lord\`s perfect qualities. Similarly, the devotees of Godhead can be graded according to the quality of their devotion.

### Text 9

Lord Siva rightly says that only pure devotees have the spiritual intelligence required to correctly understand the Supreme Lord Krsna. Describing himself as unfit to understand Krsna, however, is his ecstatic humility. He considers that because he falsely identifies with his own position in the material creation he is not qualified.

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-saptama-skandhe— in the Seventh Canto; sri-prahladasya — of Sri Prahlada; eva — himself; vakyam — the statement; kva — where; aham —I (am); rajah-prabhavah— being born in a body full of passion; isa — O my Lord; tamah — the mode of ignorance; adhike — surpassing in; asmin — in this; jatah — born; sura-itara-kule — in a family of atheists or demons; kva — where; tava — Your; anukampa — causeless mercy; na — not; brahmanah — of Lord Brahma; na — not; ca — and; bhavasya —of Lord Siva; na — nor; vai — even; ramayah — of the goddess of fortune; yat —which; me — to me; arpitah — offered; sirasi — on the head; padma-karah — lotus hand; prasadah — (the symbol of) mercy.

**Sri Prahlada himself says in the Seventh Canto s7.9.26\], “O my Lord, O Supreme, since I have been born in a family full of the hellish material qualities of passion and ignorance, what is my position? And what is to be said of Your causeless mercy upon me, which was never offered even to Lord Brahma, Lord Siva, or the goddess of fortune, Laksmi? Here Sri Prahlada shows the trademark Vaisnava quality of utter humility. Reflecting upon the fact that he was born in a family of godless demons, he is amazed that he can have an intimate relationship with the Supreme Lord. He also considers Lord Nrsimha unlimitedly kind to show mercy to a fallen soul like himself. Thus Prahlada is thrilled that Lord Nrsimha touched his head with His lotus hand.

After all, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Krsna, is living confidentially in your home with you, appearing like a human being.**

Narada wanted to encourage Yudhisthira Maharaja, to whom he had just narrated Sri Prahlada\`s glories. Yudhisthira was thinking himself unfortunate in comparison with Prahlada.

“How can that be so?”

“Because the Absolute Truth is a regular guest in your house! And therefore great sages like Markandeya are pleased to visit this same house.”

It is true that Prahlada remembered the Supreme Person constantly, but externally he was graced with the Lords association for only a few hours.

### Text 14

*sa va ayam brahma mahad-vimrgya-*  
*kaivalya-nirvana-sukhanubhutih*  
*priyah suhrd vah khalu matuleya*  
*atmarhaniyo vidhi-krd gurus ca*

**Пословный перевод:**

sah — that Supreme Personality of Godhead; va — and; ayam — He (Krsna); brahma — the Supreme Brahman; mahat-vimrgya— sought by great, great saintly persons (devotees of Krsna); kaivalya-nirvana-sukha — of liberation and transcendental bliss; anubhutih— for the realization; priyah — very dear; suhrt — the well-wisher; vah — of all of you (Pandavas); khalu — indeed; matuleyah— the son of your maternal uncle; atma— your heart and soul; arhaniyah — the most worshipable person; vidhi-krt— giving direction; guruh — your spiritual master; ca — and.

**Перевод:**

**“How wonderful that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Parabrahman, Krsna, who is sought by great sages for the sake of liberation and transcendental bliss, is acting as your well-wisher, your friend, your cousin, your heart and soul, your worshipable director, and your spiritual master.**

**Комментарий:**

Yudhisthira might protest, “Krsna is our mothers nephew. How can He be the Supreme Absolute Truth?”

Here Narada replies, “Your cousin, companion, confidant, and ordercarrier is also the Supreme Brahman, whom yogis and sages seek. From Him they receive their realization of pure bliss in liberation.”

This statement of Narada's is not surprising. Even Sisupala and other demons attained this brahmananda by Krsna\`s grace. Krsna is indeed the Supreme Truth revealed in the srutis and smrtis. Tam eva viditvati mrtyum eti: “Only by knowing Him can one transcend death.” (Svetasvatara Upanisad 3.8) Mukti-pradata sarvesam visnur eva na samsayah: “Without a doubt, Lord Visnu is the bestower of liberation for everyone.”

### Text 15

*na yasya saksad bhava-padmajadibhi*  
*rupam dhiya vastutayopavarnitam*  
*maunena bhaktyopasamena pujitah*  
*prasidatam esa sa satvatam patih*  
*iti.*

**Пословный перевод:**

na — not; yasya — of whom (Lord Sri Krsna); saksat — directly; bhava — by Lord Siva; padmaja-adibhih — Lord Brahma and others; rupam — the form; dhiya — by meditation; vastutaya — factually; upavarnitam — explained; maunena — by silence; bhaktya — by devotional service; upasamena — by finishing all material activities; pujitah — worshiped; prasidatam — may be pleased with us; esah — He; sah — the same Personality of Godhead; satvatam — of the devotees; patih— the maintainer, master, and guide; iti — thus.

**Перевод:**

**“Present here now is the same Supreme Personality of Godhead whose true form cannot be understood even by such great personalities as Lord Brahma and Lord Siva. He is realized by devotees because of their unflinching surrender. May that same Personality of Godhead, who is the maintainer of His devotees and who is worshiped by silence, by devotional service, and by cessation of material activities, be pleased with us.”**

**Комментарий:**

Yudhisthira may ask, “How can we understand Krsna as the self-satisfied Supreme when we see His attachment to Satyabhama and His other wives?” Narada replies with the above verse.

It is easy to be confused about Krsnas identity. In the presence of Krsna even Lord Brahma and Lord Siva find it difficult to understand that “here is the Absolute Truth.” Siva was confused about Krsna in a dispute concerning Banasura. Brahma was so confused that He stole Krsna\`s cowherd boyfriends. And Indra was thoroughly confused when Krsna convinced the cowherds to offer Indra\`s sacrifice to Govardhana Hill instead.

Only Krsna\`s unalloyed devotees can understand why the self-satisfied Supreme Brahman entangles Himself in loving dealings with Satyabhama and the other Vilasa expansions of His internal pleasure potency. The demigods who imagine themselves lords of the universe cannot understand.

Lord Krsna does not burden His exclusively devoted associates with inferior benefits such as elevation to heaven and impersonal liberation.

asya — of this; arthah — the meaning; yat-gunaih — “by whose qualities”; yasya — whose; uddhavasya — of Uddhava; gunaih — by the qualities; prabhuh — “the Lord”; api — although; aham — I; na arditah — “not entreated”; na — not; yacitah — requested; yad va — or, alternatively; yat — “since”; yasmat — because; uddhavah — Uddhava; gunaih — by the modes of material nature; sattva-adibhih — the mode of goodness and so on; na arditah — “not tormented”; na — not; piditah — troubled; guna-atitah — transcendental to the material modes; iti — thus; arthah — the meaning; tatra — for that; hetuh — the reason; prabhuh — “master”; bhakti-rasa— the rasas of devotional service; asvade — in the matter of tasting; prabhavisnuh — powerfully competent.

**Despite all of Uddhava\`s good qualities, however, the young goddesses of Vraja are even superior to him. Indeed, Uddhava prays for the sweetness of the gopis’ pure love.**

*tatha hi sri-dasame,*  
*etah param tanu-bhrto bhuvi gopa-vadhvo*  
*govinda eva nikhilatmani rudha-bhavah*  
*vanchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayam ca*  
*kim brahma-janmabhir ananta-katha-rasasya*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha hi — thus; sri-dasame — in the Tenth Canto; etah — these women; param — alone; tanu — their bodies; bhrtah — maintaining successfully; bhuvi — on the earth; gopa-vadhvah — the young cowherd women; govinde — for Lord Krsna; eva — exclusively; nikhila— of all; atmani—the soul; rudha— perfected; bhavah — whose ecstatic loving attraction; vanchanti — they desire; yat — which; bhava — of material existence; bhiyah— those who are afraid; munayah — sages; vayam — we; ca — also; kim — what use; brahma — as a brahmana or as Lord Brahma; janmabhih — with births; ananta — of the unlimited Lord; katha — for the topics; rasasya — for one who has a taste.

**Перевод:**

**Thus Uddhava says in the Tenth Canto s10.47.58\], “Among all persons on earth, these cowherd women alone have actually perfected their embodied lives, for they have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Lord Govinda, the soul of all existence. Their pure love is hankered after by those who fear material existence, by great sages, and by ourselves as well. For one who has tasted the narrations of the infinite Lord, what is the use of taking birth as a high-class brahmana, or even as Lord Brahma himself?”**

**Комментарий:**

Uddhava understands perfectly well that Sri Krsna is akhilatma, the soul of everything. Only the gopis, however, have attained the greatest possible intimacy with Him. Their love for the cowherd Krsna, on the ultimate level of maha-bhava, can only be dreamt of by seekers of liberation like Saunaka and even by already liberated sages like Narada.

Uddhava submits that, despite being Krsna\`s constant friend and advisor, he can only aspire with a faint hope to someday bring Krsna under the control of his love as fully as the gopis have. If he cannot achieve the gopis\` level of perfection and pure love for Krsna, he sees no use in taking birth as Brahma in his own universe.

One symptom of a persons being a less intimate devotee than the Vraja gopis and their faithful followers is that one is not spontaneously attracted to hearing about these infinitely sweet pastimes of Krsna.

*tatrapi sarva-gopinam*

**Комментарий:**

Among the agama scriptures that glorify Sri Radha is the Brhad-gautamiya-tantra, which states:

*devi krsna-mayi prokta*  
*radhika para-devata*  
*sarva-laksmi-mayi sarva-*  
*kantih sammohini para*

**“The transcendental goddess Srimati Radharani is the direct counterpart of Lord Sri Krsna. She is the central figure for all the goddesses of fortune. She possesses all the attractiveness to attract the all-attractive Personality of Godhead. She is the primeval internal potency of the Lord.”**

The Purusa-bodhini Upanisad contains a passage that begins with the words gokulakhye mathura-mandale and includes the following statements: govindo 'pi syamah, dve parsve Candravali radhika ca, and yasya amse laksmir durgadika saktih. That is: “In the place known as Gokula in Mathura district... swe find\] dark-blue Govinda... swith\] two sgopis\] standing at His side, Candravali and Radhika.... sOf the two,\] She, Radha, is Krsna\`s original potency. Laksmi, Durga, and so on are Her partial expansions.”

### Text 45

*yatha padme,*  
*yatha radha priya visnos*  
*tasyah kundam priyam tatha*  
*sarva-gopisu saivaika*

**Пословный перевод:**

yatha —as; padme—in the Padma Purana; yatha — as; radha — Radha; priya — dear; visnoh — to Lord Visnu; tasyah — Her; kundam — pond; priyam — dear; tatha — so; sarva-gopisu— of all the gopis; sa — she; eva — indeed; eka — alone; visnoh — to Lord Visnu; atyanta — supremely; Vallabha — dear.

**Перевод:**

**For example, in the Padma Purana: “Just as Srimati Radharani is most dear to Sri Krsna, Her bathing place sRadha-kunda\] is also dear to Him. Among all the gopis, Srimati Radharani is supermost and very dear to Lord Krsna.”**

**Комментарий:**

Srila Rupa Gosvami, in his Sri Upadesamrta, discloses that Radha-kunda is the most sacred place in the universe. He tells us that only the most fortunate souls can approach Radha-kunda and take bath there. Lord Narayana\`s consort may not enter. Narada and Uddhava also do not set foot there, but remain in their places of worship just outside the border of Sri Radha-kunda. And Lord Siva stands guard at the edge of the holy pond.

Concluding his Saranga-rangada commentary, Srila Baladeva Vidya-bhusana prays,

*yad-vakyat sadhavah krsnam*  
*samvidanti sa-parsadam*  
*sri-rupas tattva-vid-bhupah*  
*sa me krpayatu prabhuh*  
*sri-vidyabhusaneneyam*  
*laghu-bhagavatamrte*  
*tippani racita bhuyat*  
*tustaye rama-varninah*

**“May my master, Sri Rupa, the king of those who know the Absolute Truth, show me his mercy. By the power of his words, pious devotees can understand Krsna and His associates. Thus I, Sri Vidyabhusana, have composed this brief commentary on the Laghu-bhagavatamrta. May Rama Varni be satisfied with it.”**

*iti sri-sri-laghu-bhagavatamrte sri-bhaktamrtam namottara-khandam samaptam*

**Перевод:**

**Thus ends the second part of Sri Sri Laghu-bhagavatamrta, entitled Sri-bhaktamrta.**

*iti sri-sri-laghu-bhagavatamrtam sampurnam*

**Перевод:**

**Thus Sri Sri Laghu-bhagavatamrta is complete.**
